## TURN 418 (VCARVE-4 PLAN) — V-carve cut-path SVG export design — branch agy1

### Context & References
- **Ground truth:** Shaper V-carve tab is live in `apps/shaper` (`VCARVE-3a 1c4554b`, `VCARVE-3b e59a6b1`). State carries declared `state.vcarves = [{ id, region, vbit: { angle }, dStep, maxDepth }]` with undo/redo (`packages/core/document.js:45-46, 97-99`, `packages/ui/sketch-state.js:61-62, 84, 161`).
- **Core offset stack:** `packages/core/vcarve.js:15-28` (`vcarveContours` using `offsetPolygon(boundary, -d)`).
- **V-bit presets & angle math:** `apps/shaper/src/shaper.js:34-35` (`VBIT_PRESETS`, `vbitHalfAngleTan(angle) = Math.tan((angle/2) * Math.PI / 180)`).
- **Shaper serializer:** `packages/core/shaper-export.js:1-248` (`exportShaperSVG`, pure, no DOM, host-passed `loopPolys`).
- **Exact-string tests:** `tests/shaper-export.test.js:1-253` (SP1j-1, SP1j-2, SP1j-3, SKETCH-4e).

---

### 1. THE FORMAT: Shaper Cut Type & Per-Path Cut Depth
- **Namespace:**
  - `xmlns:shaper="http://www.shapertools.com/namespaces/shaper"` declared on the root `<svg>` (`packages/core/shaper-export.js:22, 246`).
  - Standard SVG namespace: `xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"` (`packages/core/shaper-export.js:21`).
- **Cut type attribute & color encoding:**
  - Attribute: `shaper:cutType="online"` (`packages/core/shaper-export.js:119`).
  - Color encoding: `fill="none"` and `stroke="#7F7F7F"` (`apps/shaper/src/shaper.js:28`, `packages/core/shaper-export.js:112-115`).
  - Semantics: In Shaper Origin, `online` centers the tool path directly on the vector line (`apps/shaper/src/shaper.js:28`: `desc: 'Center the cut on the path'`).
- **Per-path cut depth attribute & units:**
  - Attribute: `shaper:cutDepth="<value><unit>"` (`packages/core/shaper-export.js:120-121`).
  - Suffix formatting: `format(dep, docUnit, { unit: true })` via `packages/core/units.js:43-55`.
  - For `docUnit === 'mm'`: e.g. `shaper:cutDepth="5mm"`, `shaper:cutDepth="10mm"`.
  - For `docUnit === 'in'`: e.g. `shaper:cutDepth="0.1969in"`, `shaper:cutDepth="0.3937in"`.
  - Stored values live in base mm (1 world unit = 1 mm, `packages/core/units.js:13`).
- **Geometry & viewBox coordinates:**
  - Coordinate data in `d="M ... L ... Z"`, `width`, `height`, and `viewBox` are mm-canonical world units, unscaled by `docUnit` (`packages/core/shaper-export.js:11-12, 58-66`).
- **Tool diameter attribute:**
  - For standard cuts, `shaper:toolDia` is emitted (`packages/core/shaper-export.js:124-125`).
  - For V-carve contours, `toolDia` is omitted (`WORK-LOG.md:6059-6060`: "`toolDia` OMITTED for vcarve (a V-bit's Ø varies with depth)").
- **Verification status: VERIFIED.**
  - Confirmed by actual Shaper sample files in repository:
    `apps/shaper/samples/Untitled-2.svg:11`:
    `<path ... stroke="#7F7F7F" fill="none" stroke-width="0.1" ... shaper:cutType="online" shaper:cutDepth="0.125 in" shaper:cutOffset="0.200 in" shaper:toolDia="0.250 in" ... />`
    and `apps/shaper/samples/Untitled-2.svg:20`:
    `<path ... stroke="#7F7F7F" fill="none" stroke-width="0.1" ... shaper:cutType="online" shaper:cutDepth="0.394 in" shaper:cutOffset="0in" shaper:toolDia="0.125in" ... />`
  - Confirmed by parser: `apps/shaper/src/shaper.js:158-164` reading `getShaperAttr(el, 'cutDepth')`.
  - Confirmed by unit tests: `tests/shaper-export.test.js:108-109, 118-121`.

---

### 2. THE MATH: Inset, Depth, Clamping & Termination
- **Parameters:**
  - `boundary`: ordered points of the region loop in base mm (`[{x, y}, ...]`).
  - `angle`: V-bit included angle in degrees from `vbit.angle` (`apps/shaper/src/shaper.js:34`, 90°, 60°, 45°, 30°, 20°).
  - `halfAngleTan`: $\tan(\text{angle}/2 \cdot \pi / 180)$ (`apps/shaper/src/shaper.js:35`).
    - 90° bit: $\tan(45^\circ) = 1.0$ (1:1 depth to inset).
    - 60° bit: $\tan(30^\circ) \approx 0.57735$ ($\approx 1.732\times$ depth).
    - 45° bit: $\tan(22.5^\circ) \approx 0.41421$ ($\approx 2.414\times$ depth).
    - 30° bit: $\tan(15^\circ) \approx 0.26795$ ($\approx 3.732\times$ depth).
    - 20° bit: $\tan(10^\circ) \approx 0.17633$ ($\approx 5.671\times$ depth).
  - `dStep`: radial horizontal inset step in base mm (default 0.5 mm, `apps/shaper/src/vcarve-view.js:27`).
  - `maxDepth`: user-configured maximum cutting depth in base mm (default 6.0 mm, `apps/shaper/src/vcarve-view.js:27`).
- **Depth of each contour:**
  - For pass index $i = 1, 2, \dots$:
    - Inset distance: $d = dStep \cdot i$ (mm).
    - Inward contour: `contour = offsetPolygon(boundary, -d)`.
    - Depth: $h = d / halfAngleTan$ (mm) (`packages/core/vcarve.js:25`).
    - Derivation: With groove cross-section half-angle $\theta$, depth $h$ creates top half-width $w = h \cdot \tan(\theta)$. Setting tool offset $d = w$ ensures the V-cutter boundary meets the region edge.
- **Step between contours:**
  - Horizontal spacing: $\Delta d = dStep$ (mm).
  - Vertical depth step: $\Delta h = dStep / halfAngleTan$ (mm).
- **Max depth & clamping:**
  - Maximum iterations: `maxIters = Math.max(1, Math.min(MAX_CONTOURS, Math.floor((maxDepth * halfAngleTan) / dStep)))` (`apps/shaper/src/vcarve-view.js:59`, with `MAX_CONTOURS = 200`).
  - Depth bound: Because $i \le maxIters \le (maxDepth \cdot halfAngleTan) / dStep$, every contour depth satisfies $h \le maxDepth$. No contour ever exceeds `maxDepth`.
- **Termination at medial axis (deepest point):**
  - In `packages/core/vcarve.js:23-24`:
    `const contour = offsetPolygon(boundary, -d);`
    `if (!Array.isArray(contour) || contour.length < 3) break;`
  - In `packages/core/polygon-offset.js`, when inward polygon edges collide/collapse at the medial axis ridge, `offsetPolygon` returns `[]`.
  - The stack terminates cleanly at the innermost non-empty contour. No center-line jump or degenerate zero-area paths are emitted.
- **Units:**
  - All geometric calculations, `dStep`, `maxDepth`, and contour points are strictly base millimeters (mm).
  - Serializer formats depth strings via `format(depth, docUnit, { unit: true })`.

---

### 3. THE DERIVATION: Single Shared Source of Truth
- **Current state:**
  - Preview derivation logic lives inline inside UI code in `apps/shaper/src/vcarve-view.js:58-60`:
    ```javascript
    const tan = vbitHalfAngleTan(r.vbit.angle);
    const maxIters = Math.max(1, Math.min(MAX_CONTOURS, Math.floor((r.maxDepth * tan) / r.dStep)));
    const contours = vcarveContours(boundary, { dStep: r.dStep, halfAngleTan: tan, maxIters });
    ```
- **Proposed architecture (DRY, pure, one source of truth):**
  - Export a shared helper from `packages/core/vcarve.js`:
    ```javascript
    export function deriveVcarveContours(boundary, vcarveRec, { maxContours = 200 } = {}) {
      if (!boundary || boundary.length < 3 || !vcarveRec) return [];
      const angle = vcarveRec.vbit?.angle ?? 90;
      const tan = Math.tan(((Number(angle) || 90) / 2) * Math.PI / 180);
      const dStep = Number(vcarveRec.dStep) > 0 ? Number(vcarveRec.dStep) : 0.5;
      const maxDepth = Number(vcarveRec.maxDepth) > 0 ? Number(vcarveRec.maxDepth) : 6;
      const maxIters = Math.max(1, Math.min(maxContours, Math.floor((maxDepth * tan) / dStep)));
      return vcarveContours(boundary, { dStep, halfAngleTan: tan, maxIters });
    }
    ```
  - `apps/shaper/src/vcarve-view.js` imports `deriveVcarveContours` and replaces its inline derivation.
  - `packages/core/shaper-export.js` imports `deriveVcarveContours` and uses it during export.
- **How export gets the exact same boundary polygon:**
  - The host app (`apps/shaper/src/main.js:67-68`) already computes `loopPolys[l.id] = loopPolygon(l, st, sById)` (using DOM arc sampling) and passes `loopPolys` into `exportShaperSVG({ state, entries, encoding, docUnit, options, loopPolys })`.
  - For each `vcarve` record in `state.vcarves`:
    - The boundary is looked up as `boundary = loopPolys[vcarve.region]`.
    - Contours are derived via `deriveVcarveContours(boundary, vcarve)`.
    - Each contour polygon is converted to an SVG path:
      `d="M ${p0.x} ${p0.y} L ${p1.x} ${p1.y} ... Z"`.
    - Tag emitted: `<path d="..." fill="none" stroke="#7F7F7F" shaper:cutType="online" shaper:cutDepth="..."/>`.
  - Result: 100% byte-for-byte geometric parity between canvas preview and exported SVG toolpath.

  - Contours derived ($dStep = 5$, $\tan = 1.0$, $maxDepth = 15$):

    - Pass 2 ($d = 10$ mm, depth 10 mm): 20×20 mm contour `M 10 10 L 30 10 L 30 30 L 10 30 Z`.
    - Pass 3 ($d = 15$ mm, depth 15 mm): 10×10 mm contour `M 15 15 L 25 15 L 25 25 L 15 25 Z`.
    - Pass 4 ($d = 20$ mm): collapsed to point/line -> `offsetPolygon` returns `[]` (terminated).
- **Exact Expected SVG:**
  ```xml
  <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:shaper="http://www.shapertools.com/namespaces/shaper" width="40mm" height="40mm" viewBox="0 0 40 40">
    <path d="M 5 5 L 35 5 L 35 35 L 5 35 Z" fill="none" stroke="#7F7F7F" shaper:cutType="online" shaper:cutDepth="5mm"/>
    <path d="M 10 10 L 30 10 L 30 30 L 10 30 Z" fill="none" stroke="#7F7F7F" shaper:cutType="online" shaper:cutDepth="10mm"/>

  </svg>
  ```
- **DocUnit variations:**
  - With `docUnit: 'in'`, geometry coordinates stay mm (`viewBox="0 0 40 40"`, path coords `5`, `35`), while `shaper:cutDepth` formats as `"0.1969in"`, `"0.3937in"`, `"0.5906in"`.

### 6. RISKS & OPEN QUESTIONS FOR THE OWNER
1. **Tool diameter on V-carve online paths:**
   - Standard Shaper cuts include `shaper:toolDia="3.175mm"`. On V-carve contours, tool diameter varies continuously with depth, so our design omits `shaper:toolDia`.
   - *Question for owner:* On physical Shaper Origin hardware, does opening an SVG with `shaper:cutType="online"` without `shaper:toolDia` work seamlessly (Origin uses currently loaded bit / prompts for bit), or does Origin expect a nominal tip or shank diameter?
2. **On-tool path selection workflow:**
   - An exported V-carve consists of multiple nested concentric `online` paths.
   - *Question for owner:* When loaded onto an Origin, does the operator tap each concentric path sequentially from shallow to deep, or does Shaper Origin offer automatic multi-pass depth sequencing?
3. **Loop exclusion from standard Prepare cut-plan:**
   - If a loop has both an entry in Prepare's `CUT_PLAN` (e.g. an assigned pocket or outside cut) AND an active entry in `state.vcarves`:
   - *Design proposal:* The exporter should prioritize the V-carve and suppress standard cut assignment for that loop (matching `WORK-LOG.md:6184-6185`: "Prepare sees a vcarve region as VCARVE-HANDLED — excluded from std cut assign").
   - *Question for owner:* Should this exclusion be automatic in the exporter, or should Prepare UI enforce mutual exclusivity?
4. **Outermost boundary path ($d = 0$):**
   - Our stack begins at $d = dStep$ (first inward inset). It does not emit a path along the region boundary at $d = 0$ (which would have depth 0 mm).
   - *Question for owner:* Is omitting the boundary path ($d = 0$) correct, or is a shallow surface trace at $d = 0$ ever expected by woodworkers for chamfering?
5. **Grouping behavior under `options.groupByCut`:**
   - In `packages/core/shaper-export.js:233`, `<g>` grouping hoists identical cut attributes. Because each V-carve contour has a different `shaper:cutDepth`, their attributes are not identical, so they remain ungrouped `<path>` elements. This is valid and clean, but noted for completeness.
6. **Robustness on intricate curved artwork:**
   - Inward offsetting via `offsetPolygon` terminates at the first collapse. On complex letterforms with thin necks or acute reflex corners, some branches may terminate earlier than others. This is the known limitation of the discrete offset-stack approximation (v1) ahead of VCARVE-5 (true medial axis).

2. **BUG FIX (Direct reload to Vcarve tab lists `(no closed loops)`):**
   - **Root Cause Identified (`apps/shaper/src/main.js:514` & `538`):**
     On page load or direct navigation to `vcarve` mode (`initMode === 'vcarve'` or clicking Vcarve without visiting Design), `showMode('vcarve')` invokes `ensureSketch()` (line 536).

## TURN 423 — Scoped gate leftover-browser check to smoke child PID — branch agy2

- **Problem & Root Cause:**

- **Fix (`scripts/gate.cjs`):**
  - Read `smokePid = smokeRes.pid` returned by `spawnSync(process.execPath, ['scripts/shell-smoke.cjs'])`.
  - Filtered `countHeadless()`:
    - `HEADLESS-LEFT`: counts only `msedge.exe` whose command line contains `*sk-shell-smoke-${smokePid}*`.
    - `HEADLESS-OTHER`: counts `msedge.exe` whose command line contains `*sk-shell-smoke*` but not `${smokePid}`.
  - Summary prints `HEADLESS-LEFT <n>` and `HEADLESS-OTHER <n>`.
  - Gate exit rule checks `headlessLeft === 0`; `headlessOther` is informational and does not fail the gate.

- **Verification & Proofs:**

## TURN 423b — Match gate smoke PID as a whole token — branch agy2

- **Problem & Root Cause:**
  - `scripts/gate.cjs` used `-like "*sk-shell-smoke-${smokePid}*"` to match leftover headless Edge processes.
  - The trailing wildcard `*` allowed PID prefix collisions: for example, a run with PID 123 would match another run's `--user-data-dir` containing `sk-shell-smoke-1234`, incorrectly counting the foreign browser as its own and causing a false gate failure.

- **Fix (`scripts/gate.cjs`):**
  - Updated process matching pattern to `sk-shell-smoke-${smokePid}(?=[\\\\/"''\\s]|$)` using regex matching (`-match` in PowerShell).
  - The positive lookahead requires the PID token to be immediately followed by a path separator (`\` or `/`), a quote (`"` or `'`), whitespace, or the end of the argument/string.
  - Prefix collisions like `sk-shell-smoke-1234` are rejected because `4` is not a token delimiter.

- **Unit-Level Proof (`tests/gate-pid-match.test.js`):**
  - Added unit test verifying both JS regex and PowerShell `-match`:
    - PID 123 matches `sk-shell-smoke-123` in quoted, unquoted, trailing-slash, and end-of-line command lines.
    - PID 123 rejects `sk-shell-smoke-1234` in all cases.
    - PID 1234 matches its own command lines and rejects `sk-shell-smoke-123`.
  - Output: `gate PID matching tests passed ✅`.

- **Gate:**
  - `npm run gate` (`scripts/gate.cjs`):
    - `GATE files=156 pass=156 fail=0`
    - `SMOKE 12/12`
    - `HEADLESS-LEFT 0`
    - `HEADLESS-OTHER 0`
    - Exit code 0.
## TURN 424 (VCARVE-5a PLAN) — V-carve contours that SPLIT via Clipper (no code) — branch agy1
Plan for VCARVE-5a: replacing the simple-loop `#core/polygon-offset.js` inside `#core/vcarve.js` with the robust Clipper offset from `#core/plot/clip.js`, so inward offsets split into multiple islands at neck pinches (letters B, 8, S, dumbbells) instead of aborting the entire contour stack at the first collapse.

### 1. How `clip.js` Offsets Inward
- **Module and Source of Truth:** `packages/core/plot/clip.js` wraps Angus Johnson's vendored Clipper library (`packages/core/plot/vendor/clipper.js`) via `packages/core/plot/vendor/clipper-node-shim.js` (ensuring Node ESM and browser parity without global pollution).
- **Coordinate Conversion & Precision (`clip.js:18-36`):**
  - Clipper operates on integer coordinates. `CLIP_SCALE = 1000` (`clip.js:19`): 1 integer unit = 1 µm (0.001 mm). At millimeter scale, this gives sub-micron precision without floating-point accumulation or geometry degradation.
  - `toClipper(points)` (`clip.js:22-29`) maps `[[x, y], ...]` to `[{ X: Math.round(x * 1000), Y: Math.round(y * 1000) }]`, dropping any duplicate closing vertex.
  - `fromClipper(path)` (`clip.js:32-36`) maps `[{ X, Y }, ...]` back to `[[x, y], ...]` in millimeters (`pt.X / 1000`), appending a duplicate closing vertex.
- **Offset API (`clip.js:38-49` & `clip.js:68-91`):**
  - `insetPolygon(polygon, amount)`:
    ```javascript
    // clip.js:43-48
    if (!ClipperLib.Clipper.Orientation(path)) path.reverse();
    const co = new ClipperLib.ClipperOffset(2 /* miterLimit */, 0.25 * CLIP_SCALE);
    co.AddPath(path, ClipperLib.JoinType.jtMiter, ClipperLib.EndType.etClosedPolygon);
    const sol = new ClipperLib.Paths();
    co.Execute(sol, -amount * CLIP_SCALE); // negative delta = inward
    return sol.filter(r => r.length >= 3).map(fromClipper);
    ```
  - For concentric multi-step offsets, `ClipperOffset` is initialized once with `co.AddPath`, and `co.Execute(sol, -d * CLIP_SCALE)` is called repeatedly for each `d` (avoiding redundant path preprocessing).
- **What it returns on a split:**
  - `sol` is a `ClipperLib.Paths` collection containing **multiple independent closed paths** (e.g. `sol.length === 2` for a neck pinch).
  - Each path is a complete, non-self-intersecting closed ring.
  - Unlike `#core/polygon-offset.js:127` which tests `selfIntersects(out)` and returns `[]` on any pinch, Clipper resolves the pinch into separate topologically valid loops.

### 2. The New Derivation (`packages/core/vcarve.js`)
- **Algorithm:**
  - Initialize `co = new ClipperLib.ClipperOffset(2, 0.25 * CLIP_SCALE)`.
  - Add the outer boundary (converted from `{ x, y }[]` to Clipper path).
  - Loop `for (let i = 1; i <= maxIters; i++)`:
    - `d = i * step`.
    - `co.Execute(sol, -d * CLIP_SCALE)`.
    - If `sol.length === 0`: every island has reached its local medial axis ridge -> terminate early (`break;`).
    - For each `ring` in `sol`:
      - Filter `ring.length >= 3`.
      - Convert vertices from Clipper integer `{ X, Y }` back to mm `{ x, y }` (stripping the duplicate closing vertex).
      - Push `{ polygon: pts, depth: d / tan }`.
- **Data Shape Recommendation: Keep FLAT `[{ polygon, depth }, ...]`:**
  - Grouping by depth (`[{ depth, polygons: [...] }]`) would require breaking changes across all consumers. Keeping the return shape flat `[{ polygon, depth }, ...]` ensures:
    1. **UI Preview (`apps/shaper/src/vcarve-view.js:83-87`):**
       ```javascript
       for (const c of contours) {
         const t = maxDepth > 0 ? Math.min(1, c.depth / maxDepth) : 0;
         const L = Math.round(66 - 44 * t);
         s += poly(c.polygon, `fill="none" stroke="hsl(28,50%,${L}%)" ...`);
       }
       ```
       Preview loop iterates `contours` directly; zero changes required.
    2. **Machine Export (`packages/core/shaper-export.js:246-253`):**
       ```javascript
       const contours = deriveVcarveContours(boundary, vc);
       for (const c of contours) {
         const d = polyToPathD(c.polygon);
         const common = colorAttrs(onlineEnc) + shaperAttrs({ cutDepth: c.depth }, onlineEnc, docUnit);
         items.push({ common, tag: 'path', a: `d="${d}"` });
       }
       ```
       Export emits one `<path>` per cut contour; zero changes required.
    3. **Tests (`tests/shaper-export.test.js:305-315`):**
       Preview-vs-export parity checks iterate `previewContours[i]` 1:1 against `exportedPaths[i]`; zero structural changes required.
  - **Cut & Depth Ordering:** Contours are emitted in depth-ascending order ($d = 1\cdot\text{step}, 2\cdot\text{step}, \dots$). When a step splits into multiple islands, those sibling islands are emitted consecutively at the same depth. This matches physical CNC machining (shallow passes are cut across all features before stepping deeper).

### 3. Behaviour Changes on Simple / Convex Shapes
- **Empirical Probe (40×40 square at $d = 5\text{ mm}$):**
  - **Geometric parity:** Exactly identical 30×30 mm square with corners $(5, 5)$, $(35, 5)$, $(35, 35)$, $(5, 35)$; area is exactly $900\text{ mm}^2$.
  - **Vertex Order & Start Point Difference:**
    - Today's `polygon-offset.js`: Starts at vertex 0 corresponding to input $(0, 0)$, traversing counter-clockwise (in SVG Y-down):
      `d="M 5 5 L 35 5 L 35 35 L 5 35 Z"`.
    - Clipper `insetPolygon`: Starts at bottom-right $(35, 35)$, traversing clockwise:
      `d="M 35 35 L 5 35 L 5 5 L 35 5 Z"`.
  - **Exported SVG Output:**
    The geometric cuts cut by Shaper Origin or a CNC machine are 100% physically identical. However, the path string `d` attribute starts at `M 35 35` instead of `M 5 5`.
- **Proposal for Exact-String Oracles:**
  - **Recommended Approach:** Update the exact-string oracle constants in `tests/shaper-export.test.js` (`wantMM` and `wantIN`, lines 273-291) to Clipper's canonical output (`M 35 35 L 5 35 L 5 5 L 35 5 Z`), documenting that Clipper defines the canonical vertex ordering for all offset operations.
  - **Alternative Evaluated & Rejected (Vertex Rolling):** Attempting to "roll" Clipper's polygon vertices so that the vertex closest to `boundary[0]` comes first works for 1:1 single loops, but is an unprincipled heuristic that breaks down as soon as a shape splits into multiple islands (where island 2 has no relation to `boundary[0]`). Adopting Clipper's native deterministic order is cleaner and robust.

### 4. Holes (Compound Regions, e.g. Letter 'O')
- **Today's Limitation:**
  - In `apps/shaper/src/vcarve-view.js:37` and `packages/core/shaper-export.js:240-254`, `state.vcarves[0].region` references a single loop ID.
  - For a letter 'O', `findLoops` returns two distinct loops (outer boundary and inner hole). Today, the user picks the outer loop, and `vcarveContours` carves straight through the center, completely destroying the hole.
- **Clipper's Native Capability:**
  - `ClipperOffset` supports compound polygons: if an outer loop and an inner hole loop are added via `co.AddPath(outer)` and `co.AddPath(hole)`:
    - The outer loop insets inward.
    - The hole loop offsets outward into the wall.
    - Both fronts advance toward each other and collapse simultaneously when they meet at the medial axis ridge (verified empirically: a 40×40 square with a 10×10 central hole collapses at $d = 7.5\text{ mm}$, yielding 0 rings at $d \ge 7.5\text{ mm}$).
- **Plan for VCARVE-5a vs 5b:**
  - In VCARVE-5a, `vcarveContours(boundary, opts)` will accept `boundary` as either `Point[]` (single loop) or `{ outer: Point[], holes: Point[][] }` (compound).
  - When given a single boundary (as the UI passes today), Clipper insets the outer ring.
  - The plumbing is thus hole-ready for VCARVE-5b, which can wire the UI/host to detect contained islands via `groupOfLoop` / `loopsInGroup` / `polygonContains` (reusing the pattern already proven for pocket islands in `shaper-export.js:192-212`).

### 5. Performance & The 200-Contour Cap
- **Empirical Benchmark:**
  - Run on a complex 60-vertex wavy star polygon (resembling intricate typography) with 200 concentric Clipper offset calls:
    - **Total execution time:** **42.29 ms** in Node V8.
    - **Total rings produced:** 158 rings across multiple splitting lobes.
  - 42 ms is well within the 100 ms threshold for 60 fps / instantaneous UI reactivity during interactive slider adjustments.
- **Keep `maxContours = 200`:**
  - **YES.** At `dStep = 0.5 mm`, 200 depth levels represents a 100 mm deep carve (far exceeding any CNC router bit reach).
  - The cap prevents runaway execution on corrupt inputs, micro-steps (e.g. `dStep = 0.001`), or degenerate slivers.
  - In the implementation, `maxIters = Math.min(maxContours, Math.floor((maxDepth * tan) / dStep + 1e-6))` limits the depth passes, while a secondary guard `if (out.length >= maxContours * 2) break;` prevents memory explosion if a complex fractal shape splits into dozens of islands per level.

### 6. Test Suite Plan
1. **Dumbbell Split Test (`tests/vcarve.test.js`):**
   - Shape: 60×20 bounding box with two 20×20 lobes (`x = 0..20` and `x = 40..60`) joined by a 4-high neck (`y = 8..12`, `x = 20..40`).
   - Parameters: `dStep = 1.0`, 90° bit (`tan = 1.0`).
   - Expected progression:
     - $d = 1\text{ mm}$: 1 connected contour (neck width shrinks from 4 to 2 mm).
     - $d = 2\text{ mm}$: 2 contours (neck collapses; splits into left and right lobes).
     - $d = 3..9\text{ mm}$: 2 contours per level (both lobes independently insetting toward centers $(10, 10)$ and $(50, 10)$).
     - $d = 10\text{ mm}$: collapses to 0 rings.
   - Assertions:
     - Exact contour count: $1 + 8 \times 2 = \mathbf{17\text{ contours}}$.
     - Depths: $1\text{ mm}$ (1 path), $2..9\text{ mm}$ (2 paths each).
     - Finite termination without hanging.
2. **Angled Waisted Pinch Test (`tests/vcarve.test.js`):**
   - Shape: 20×20 with an acute waist pinching at `x = 9..11, y = 10`.
   - Today's `polygon-offset.js` returns `[]` at $d = 1.0\text{ mm}$, yielding only **1 contour** total and abandoning both lobes.
   - Clipper derivation yields **15 contours** (1 connected + 7 split pairs), cutting cleanly down to $d = 4.0\text{ mm}$.
3. **Preview vs Export Parity Test (`tests/shaper-export.test.js`):**
   - Feed the dumbbell loop into `exportShaperSVG`.
   - Assert all 17 contours are exported as `<path shaper:cutType="online">`.
   - Verify every exported path matches `deriveVcarveContours` in coordinate string `d` and depth attribute `shaper:cutDepth`.
4. **Zero-Vcarve & Simple Loop Regression Tests:**
   - Verify non-vcarve exports remain 100% byte-identical.
   - Verify 40×40 square export matches the updated oracle.

### 7. Risks & Questions for Owner
1. **Cut Ordering Across Islands:**
   - Today's proposed order is **depth-first** (at depth $d$, cut island A then island B; then step to $d + \text{step}$ and cut island A then island B). This is standard CNC practice to prevent excessive radial tool engagement.
   - *Question:* Is depth-first ordering desired for Shaper Origin, or would woodworkers prefer cutting each island to completion before retracting and moving to the next island? (Recommendation: depth-first).
2. **Oracle Approval:**
   - Confirm approval to update `wantMM` and `wantIN` in `tests/shaper-export.test.js` to Clipper's canonical vertex start point (`M 35 35 ...`).
3. **Micro-loop Threshold:**
   - Near the apex of sharp acute corners, offsetting can occasionally leave microscopic residual loops ($< 0.1\text{ mm}$ perimeter).
   - *Question:* Should we filter out any contour with perimeter $< 0.2\text{ mm}$ or area $< 0.05\text{ mm}^2$ to prevent unnecessary on-tool stuttering?
4. **Consolidation / Two-Engine Debt:**
   - VCARVE-5a will route `vcarve.js` to `#core/plot/clip.js`. `#core/polygon-offset.js` will remain in use solely by `apps/shaper/src/prepare-view.js` (for pocket inset / toolpath visualization).
   - Eventual unification of `prepare-view.js` to Clipper will retire `polygon-offset.js` entirely per ROADMAP.md.

## TURN 423c — Ignore lingering Edge helper processes in gate leak check — branch agy2

- **Problem & Root Cause:**
  - On Windows, Edge launches subordinate helper processes (`--type=crashpad-handler`, `--type=utility`, `--type=gpu-process`, etc.) sharing the `--user-data-dir` profile.
  - When `shell-smoke.cjs` closes the browser, the main browser process exits cleanly. However, background helpers like crashpad-handler and utility services can linger for 1–2 minutes while flushing dumps or closing pipe handles.
  - `scripts/gate.cjs` previously counted all `msedge.exe` matching `sk-shell-smoke-<pid>`, causing false gate failures (`HEADLESS-LEFT 2`, exit 1) when helpers outlasted the 3s grace window.

- **Fix (`scripts/gate.cjs`) — Option (a):**
  - Count only MAIN browser processes (command lines with no `--type=` argument) as leaks for `HEADLESS-LEFT`.
  - Reason: In Chromium/Edge, the main browser process is the root of the process tree and is launched without a `--type=` flag. All child helper processes are subordinate and self-terminate once the main browser process terminates. Counting only main processes avoids imposing a 30s delay on gate runs while reliably detecting any actual leaked browser instances immediately.
  - Filter in `countHeadless()`: `Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -match 'sk-shell-smoke' -and $_.CommandLine -notmatch '--type=' }`.

- **Unit-Level Proof & Verification (`tests/gate-pid-match.test.js`):**
  - Added unit test assertions covering real Edge helper command lines:
    - Main process (`--headless=new --user-data-dir=...sk-shell-smoke-123` with no `--type=`) evaluates to `isMainProcess = true` and `testPowershellGateFilter = true`.
    - Helper processes (`--type=crashpad-handler`, `--type=utility`, `--type=gpu-process`, `--type=renderer`) evaluate to `isMainProcess = false` and `testPowershellGateFilter = false` (never counted as leaks).
    - Result: `gate PID matching and helper filtering tests passed ✅`.

- **Real Leak Detection Proof (Main browser leak still fails gate):**
  - Temporarily configured `shell-smoke.cjs` to spawn a detached browser and skip `closeBrowser`.
  - Ran `node scripts/gate.cjs`: failed as expected with exit code 1 (`HEADLESS-LEFT 1`, `HEADLESS-OTHER 1`).
  - Leaked process reaped and `shell-smoke.cjs` reverted.

## TURN 426 (VCARVE-5b PLAN) — V-carve regions WITH HOLES (no code) — branch agy1
Plan for VCARVE-5b: extending V-carve offsetting to compound regions with holes (letters O, A, B, and picture frames). The outer boundary insets inward while the hole boundary expands outward into the channel; both tool fronts advance toward each other and terminate at the medial axis ridge.

### 1. The Declaration (How a V-carve Record States Its Holes)
- **Existing Architecture (`packages/core/shaper-export.js:192-212` & `packages/core/group-model.js:52-67`):**
  - SKETCH-4e established the project standard for island/hole relationships:
    A loop is an island/hole if it belongs to the SAME user group (`groupOfLoop(L, state) === gid`) as the outer loop AND is strictly contained within the outer loop's polygon (`polygonContains(outerPoly, holePoly)` via `packages/core/loop-geometry.js:80-88`).
  - Requiring an explicit group prevents independent parts nested on a stock sheet (e.g. a small square workpiece nested inside a large sheet rectangle) from being accidentally absorbed as holes.
- **Record Structure (`state.vcarves`):**
  - Project principle: **DERIVE over materialize**.
  - The record continues to store `region: outerLoopId` (e.g. `{ id: 'vcarve-1', region: 'loop_outer', vbit: { angle: 90 }, dStep: 0.5, maxDepth: 6 }`).
  - At runtime, the host derives holes dynamically:
    ```javascript
    function findHolesForLoop(outerLoopId, loops, state, loopPolys) {
      const L = loops.find((l) => l.id === outerLoopId);
      if (!L) return [];
      const gid = groupOfLoop(L, state);
      if (!gid) return [];
      const outerPoly = loopPolys[L.id];
      if (!outerPoly) return [];
      const candidateHoles = [];
      for (const hid of loopsInGroup(loops, state, gid)) {
        if (hid === L.id) continue;
        const hp = loopPolys[hid];
        if (hp && polygonContains(outerPoly, hp)) candidateHoles.push({ id: hid, poly: hp });
      }
      // Filter out nested islands (depth 2): a hole cannot be contained in another hole
      return candidateHoles
        .filter((h) => !candidateHoles.some((other) => other.id !== h.id && polygonContains(other.poly, h.poly)))
        .map((h) => h.poly);
    }
    ```
- **Region Picker Display (`apps/shaper/src/vcarve-view.js:35-42`):**
  - When a group contains an outer loop and holes:
    - The dropdown displays: `Group 1: Loop 1 (1500 mm² · 1 hole)` or `Loop 1 (1500 mm² · 1 hole)`.
    - Inner loops that are absorbed as holes in a group are either omitted from the dropdown or grayed out (`Loop 2 (hole in Loop 1)`), preventing conflicting standalone vcarve operations on an absorbed hole.

### 2. The Derivation (`packages/core/vcarve.js`)
- **Signature & Unified Code Path:**
  ```javascript
  export function vcarveContours(boundary, { dStep, halfAngleTan, maxIters = 1000, holes = [] } = {})
  export function deriveVcarveContours(boundary, record, { maxContours = 200, holes = [] } = {})
  ```
  - Exactly ONE function. Single-boundary calls simply omit `holes` (defaults to `[]`), running through the exact same code path with zero forks.
- **Clipper Orientation & Setup:**
  - Outer boundary: checked with `ClipperLib.Clipper.Orientation(outerPath)`. If false, reversed to ensure **positive orientation** (outer boundary).
  - Hole boundaries: for each hole in `holes`, checked with `ClipperLib.Clipper.Orientation(holePath)`. If true, reversed to ensure **negative orientation** (Clipper hole).
  - Setup:
    ```javascript
    const co = new ClipperLib.ClipperOffset(2 /* miterLimit */, 0.25 * CLIP_SCALE /* arcTolerance */);
    co.AddPath(outerPath, ClipperLib.JoinType.jtMiter, ClipperLib.EndType.etClosedPolygon);
    for (const hPath of holePaths) {
      co.AddPath(hPath, ClipperLib.JoinType.jtMiter, ClipperLib.EndType.etClosedPolygon);
    }
    ```
- **Contour Output at Each Depth Step:**
  - `co.Execute(sol, -d * CLIP_SCALE)` is called with negative delta.
  - The outer boundary insets inward; the hole boundaries offset outward into the material.
  - At each depth $d$ before collision, `sol` contains **separate closed rings** (e.g. Ring 0 for outer wall slope, Ring 1 for hole wall slope).
  - Each ring is pushed into the flat array: `{ polygon: pts, depth: d / tan }`.
  - When the two slopes meet at the medial axis ridge, `sol.length` drops to 0, terminating the loop cleanly.
- **Export Output (`packages/core/shaper-export.js:246-253`):**
  - Emits one `<path shaper:cutType="online" shaper:cutDepth="..."/>` per ring.
  - In physical V-carve machining, online paths are cut as separate closed toolpaths (shallowest to deepest). No artificial bridging or compound path is required for online cuts.

### 3. Behaviour: No-Holes Byte-Identity
- When `holes = []` (or omitted), only `outerPath` is added to `ClipperOffset`.
- The execution path is identical line-for-line to VCARVE-5a.
- **Protected Oracles:**
  - `tests/shaper-export.test.js`: Test 14 (`wantMM` 40×40 exact string), Test 15 (`wantIN` exact string), Test 17 (preview parity), Test 18 (60° triangle), Test 19 (zero-vcarve byte-identity), Test 20 (Dumbbell split parity).
  - `tests/vcarve.test.js`: Tests 1–5 (square math & guards), Test 6 (dumbbell), Test 7 (waist), Test 8 (20° wedge sharpness).
  - All must remain 100% byte-for-byte identical.

### 4. Edge Cases
1. **Hole Touching Boundary:**
   - In SketchStudio, topological loops sharing an edge are adjacent planar faces (`findLoops`), not strictly contained loops.
   - `polygonContains(outer, inner)` enforces strict non-crossing containment (`segsCross` check). A touching loop returns false and is not treated as a hole.
2. **Nested Islands (Bullseye / Dot inside 'O's hole):**
   - Given Outer $A$ containing Hole $B$, and Island Dot $C$ inside $B$:
   - The region being carved is the solid material between $A$ and $B$.
   - Dot $C$ sits inside the void of $B$ and must remain uncarved raw stock.
   - Filtering rule: A candidate hole is only a valid hole of $A$ if it is NOT contained within any other hole of $A$. This safely filters out depth-2 islands like $C$.
3. **Hole Larger than Max Depth Reach:**
   - E.g. 100×100 outer, 60×60 hole (channel width 20 mm), with `maxDepth = 6 mm` and 90° bit.
   - The outer bevel insets 6 mm; the hole bevel offsets 6 mm.
   - They do not meet; an 8 mm flat uncut plateau remains between them.
   - Clipper handles this naturally: both insets proceed down to `maxIters = Math.floor(maxDepth * tan / dStep)` and stop, leaving the plateau uncarved.

### 5. Test Suite Plan
1. **Square Frame Fixture (`tests/vcarve.test.js`):**
   - Geometry: 40×40 outer boundary with 10×10 hole centered at $(20, 20)$ (`x = 15..25, y = 15..25`).
   - Channel wall thickness: $(40 - 10) / 2 = 15\text{ mm}$.
   - Medial ridge: $15 / 2 = 7.5\text{ mm}$.
   - Parameters: `dStep = 1.0 mm`, 90° bit (`tan = 1.0`), `maxDepth = 10 mm`.
   - Expected progression:
     - Depths: $d = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7\text{ mm}$ (7 depth levels).
     - At each depth $d = 1..7$: exactly 2 contours (outer wall pass + hole wall pass).
     - Total contours: $7 \times 2 = \mathbf{14\text{ contours}}$.
     - At $d = 8\text{ mm}$ ($8 > 7.5\text{ mm}$): 0 rings (finite ridge collapse).
   - Assertions:
     - Exact count: 14 contours.
     - Depths: pairs at 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 mm.
     - Orientation: outer contour positive, hole contour negative.
2. **Preview vs Export Parity Test (`tests/shaper-export.test.js`):**
   - Frame loop with hole assigned in `state.vcarves`.
   - Verify `exportShaperSVG` emits all 14 `<path shaper:cutType="online">` elements with matching `d` strings and depths.
3. **Letter 'B' / Double-Hole Fixture:**
   - 1 outer loop with 2 distinct holes.
   - Verifies Clipper handles arbitrary number of simultaneous holes.
4. **No-Hole Byte-Identity Check:**
   - Verifies 40×40 square, dumbbell, and wedge exports remain byte-identical.

### 6. Owner Questions
1. **Nested Island Inside a Hole (Bullseye):**
   - Confirm that an island $C$ inside hole $B$ of outer $A$ should remain uncut raw material when carving $A$. If the user wishes to carve $C$, they can assign a separate vcarve/cut entry to $C$.
2. **Explicit Group vs Automatic Containment:**
   - Should island detection strictly require the loops to be in a user group (`Ctrl+G` in Design, matching SKETCH-4e / `shaper-export.js:192-212`), OR should the Vcarve tab automatically treat any strictly contained loop as a hole even if ungrouped?
   - *Recommendation:* Require the explicit group to remain consistent with SKETCH-4e and avoid treating independent parts drawn on a common stock boundary as holes.
3. **Region Picker Presentation:**
   - Should absorbed holes be hidden from the Vcarve region dropdown, or listed as disabled (`Loop 2 (hole in Loop 1)`)?
   - (Recommendation: Hide or suffix as disabled so the user cannot accidentally assign a duplicate cut to an absorbed hole).

## TURN 430 (COMBINE + PROFILE PLAN) — A COMBINE SHAPES tool + a PROFILE selector that understands inner profiles (PLAN ONLY)

### Overview
This plan implements the owner's directive:
> *"to get real pocket island effect, we need a combine shape tool, and a profile selector that considers inner profiles"* and holes are *"not automatic"*.

Today, holes are derived on the fly from an explicit user GROUP (`Ctrl+G`, `group-model.js:52-108`) combined with geometric containment (`polygonContains`). Selection in Prepare (`prepare-view.js:154-164`) and Vcarve (`vcarve-view.js:35-42`) selects only individual topological loops.
This plan replaces group-as-holes with **COMBINED PROFILES**: an explicit, declared data structure representing a 2D machining region (outer boundary minus inner hole boundaries).

---

### 1. The Declaration (`packages/core/profile-model.js`, `document.js`, `sketch-state.js`)
- **Record Structure:**
  Declared in `state.profiles` on the shared sketch state (array of plain objects):
  ```javascript
  {
    id: 'profile-1',          // minted stable id
    outer: 'loop_so1-so2-...',// topological loop id of the outer boundary
    inners: ['loop_sh1-...'], // topological loop ids of the inner hole boundaries
    name: 'Profile 1',        // human-readable label for UI/tree/inspector
    sketchId: 'sketch-1'      // active sketch container (matches SKETCH-1a)
  }
  ```
- **Why Loop IDs for Outer/Inners:**
  - In SketchStudio, topological loops are planar cycles of joined edges (`packages/core/loop-finder.js:46: makeLoop: 'loop_' + edges.slice().sort().join('-')`).
  - Edge/shape IDs (`so1`, `sh1`) are immutable across solver movement, point drag, and solve iterations. Therefore loop IDs are topology-stable.
  - Using loop IDs connects directly with CAM target resolution in Prepare (`prepare-view.js:138`) and cut-plan keys (`cut-plan.js:8: keyOf(kind, id)`).
- **Persistence & Serialization:**
  - `packages/core/document.js`:
    - `serializeDocument(state)` (`document.js:44-48`):
      `profiles: Array.isArray(state.profiles) ? state.profiles.map(p => ({ ...p, inners: [...p.inners] })) : undefined`
    - `deserializeDocument(doc, state)` (`document.js:93-100`):
      Restores `state.profiles` from `doc.geometry.profiles` (defaults to `[]`).
  - `packages/ui/sketch-state.js`:
    - `_captureSnapshot()` (`sketch-state.js:59-63`): deep-clones `this.profiles`.
    - `_restoreSnapshot()` (`sketch-state.js:83-84`): restores `this.profiles`.
    - Undo/Redo (`state.undo()`, `state.redo()`): fully undoable and redoable with zero custom code.
- **Relationship to User Groups (`packages/core/group-model.js`):**
  - **Combine becomes THE ONE source of holes.**
  - `group-model.js` is stripped of all hole/containment logic and returns purely to entity organization (`userGroupId`, `makeGroup`, `ungroup`, `renameGroup`, `shapesInGroup`).
  - **What gets deleted:**
    1. `holesOfLoop` in `packages/core/group-model.js:78-112`: DELETED from `group-model.js`.
    2. `import { polygonContains } from './loop-geometry.js';` in `group-model.js:10`: DELETED.
    3. `loopsInGroup` and `groupOfLoop` in `group-model.js:54-69`: removed from hole lookups.
    4. Group-as-holes logic in `packages/core/shaper-export.js:195-212`: replaced by profile-based lookup.
  - **Saved Documents Policy:**
    - Per project principle: "no legacy path; ask only if data is genuinely irreplaceable".
    - Because Sketch-Studio is an in-development desktop app without legacy customer databases, no dual-codec compatibility shim is retained.
    - Existing saved groups continue to exist as user groups (organization). If a user wants holes in an old document, they select the shapes in Design and click Combine.

---

### 2. The Tool (Design Ribbon & Canvas Feedback)
- **Ribbon Button (`packages/ui/tool-ribbon.js`, `apps/shaper/src/main.js`):**
  - In the ribbon's `EDIT` or a new `PROFILE` group (`tool-ribbon.js:23-27`), add two action buttons:
    - **Combine** (`icon-combine`, label: "Combine")
    - **Uncombine** (`icon-uncombine`, label: "Uncombine")
- **Interaction Model (Selection-then-Action):**
  - Follows the established CAD pattern (Illustrator/Inkscape `Path > Combine`, Figma Boolean, Group `Ctrl+G` in `main.js:224-232`):
  1. The user selects shapes on the canvas (Shift-click or marquee selection in Select mode).
  2. The user clicks **Combine** (or presses `Ctrl+Shift+C`).
  3. **Validation (`validateCombine(selectedShapes, state)` in `profile-model.js`):**
     - Finds all closed loops whose edges are in `selectedShapes` (`findLoops`).
     - Must find $\ge 2$ closed loops (otherwise toast: *"Select shapes forming 2+ closed loops to combine"*).
     - Computes boundary polygon for each loop via `loopPolygon` (`loop-geometry.js:30`).
     - Sorts loops by `polyArea` descending. The largest loop is candidate `outerLoop`.
     - Remaining loops must be strictly contained in `outerLoop` via `polygonContains(outerPoly, holePoly)` (`loop-geometry.js:80`). If any is outside or intersecting, rejects with toast: *"Hole loops must be strictly inside the outer boundary"*.
     - Checks hole-hole non-crossing: no inner loop may intersect or cross another inner loop.
     - Checks nesting: inner loops may not be contained inside each other (depth-1 holes only, matching the clean uncut-island CAM rule).
  4. On valid check:
     - Mints `{ id: 'profile-N', outer: outerLoop.id, inners: innerLoops.map(l => l.id), name: 'Profile N' }`.
     - Appends to `state.profiles`.
     - Calls `state.saveState()` (undo point).
     - Toast: `Combined into Profile N (${innerLoops.length} hole${innerLoops.length === 1 ? '' : 's'})`.
  5. **Uncombine Action:**
     - When any shape or loop belonging to an existing combined profile is selected:
     - "Uncombine" button activates (or `Ctrl+Shift+U`).
     - Calls `uncombineProfile(state, profileId)`: removes the record from `state.profiles`, calls `state.saveState()`, and restores the loops as independent uncombined loops.
- **Canvas Visual Feedback in Design Mode (`packages/ui/svg-renderer.js`):**
  - In the sketch canvas world group (`#design-world-group`), behind the interactive line/arc strokes:
  - Each profile in `state.profiles` is rendered as a soft tinted compound polygon:
    `<path d="${outerD} ${inner1D} ${inner2D}..." fill-rule="evenodd" style="fill:var(--sk-profile-fill, rgba(122,167,224,0.08)); stroke:none;"/>`
  - Visual result: The solid channel between outer and holes displays a distinct soft blue tint, while the hole regions remain transparent (raw stock). This immediately cues the user that the shapes are combined into a profile with holes.

---

### 3. The Profile Selector (Prepare & Vcarve)
- **Concept: Every 2D Region is a Profile (`apps/shaper/src/prepare-view.js:138-164`):**
  - Today, Prepare resolves cursor proximity to `{ kind: 'edge', id }` or `{ kind: 'loop', id }`.
  - With combined profiles, the selectable region entity is extended to understand profiles:
    - If a loop is the outer loop of a combined profile $P$: it represents $P$ (outer minus inners).
    - If a loop is an inner loop of $P$: it is absorbed into $P$ and cannot be independently selected at top-level.
    - If a loop is not in any combined profile: it is a standalone plain loop profile (0 holes).
- **Cursor Hit-Testing (`resolveTarget(worldPt)` in `prepare-view.js:154-164`):**
  1. Edge proximity test runs first (`EDGE_TOL_PX` on stroke) -> returns `{ kind: 'edge', id }`.
  2. If not on an edge, evaluate profiles:
     - For each combined profile $P$:
       Check if `pointInPolygon(outerPoly, worldPt)` is true AND `!pointInPolygon(holePoly, worldPt)` for all holes in $P$.
       If yes, the point lies in the solid material of the combined profile!
     - For plain loops:
       Check if `pointInPolygon(loopPoly, worldPt)` is true.
     - Among candidate hits, pick the one with the smallest net area (standard CAD innermost-face rule).
     - Return `{ kind: 'profile', id: P.id }` (or `{ kind: 'loop', id: l.id }` for plain loops).
  3. **Cursor Inside a Hole:**
     - If the cursor is inside a hole of $P$:
       `pointInPolygon(holePoly, worldPt)` is true, so $P$ is NOT hit.
       If the hole contains another plain loop or profile (a nested island / bullseye dot), that inner loop is hit!
       If the hole is empty, no target is hit (empty void).
- **Hover & Selection Markup (`targetMarkup` in `prepare-view.js:167-172`):**
  - When `{ kind: 'profile', id: 'profile-1' }` is hovered or selected:
    Emits ONE compound SVG path:
    `<path d="${outerD} ${inner1D} ${inner2D}..." fill-rule="evenodd" style="${HOVER_STYLE | SELECT_STYLE}"/>`
  - Under `fill-rule="evenodd"`, the hover/selection tint highlights the EXACT solid region (channel) while leaving holes completely unhighlighted!
  - The selection outline traces both the outer perimeter and each hole boundary with `SELECT_STYLE` (solid blue border).
- **Vcarve Region Picker (`apps/shaper/src/vcarve-view.js:35-42`):**
  - Dropdown lists all available machining profiles:
    - Combined profiles: `Profile 1 (1600 mm² · 1 hole)`
    - Standalone loops: `Loop 2 (200 mm²)`
    - Inner absorbed loops are not listed as selectable outer regions.
  - Selecting `Profile 1` immediately feeds `boundary = outerPoly` and `holes = holePolys` into `deriveVcarveContours(outerPoly, rec, { holes: holePolys, excludeNested: true })`.

---

### 4. Export & Cut Types on a Combined Profile (`packages/core/shaper-export.js`)
When a cut is assigned to a combined profile $P$ (outer loop $L_{\text{out}}$, inner loops $L_{\text{in}, 1..k}$):

1. **Pocket (`cutType: 'pocket'`):**
   - Machining: Pocket out all material within $L_{\text{out}}$ while leaving $L_{\text{in}}$ islands uncut.
   - Export: ONE compound `<path d="${outerD} ${innersD}" fill-rule="evenodd" shaper:cutType="pocket" ... />`.
   - Prepare Look: Hatch pattern across the solid channel + tool-center offset paths around outer (inward) and inners (outward).
2. **V-Carve (in Vcarve Tab):**
   - Machining: Dual-slope V-carve grooving between outer wall and hole walls meeting at medial ridge.
   - Export: Concentric `<path shaper:cutType="online" shaper:cutDepth="...">` rings derived from ClipperOffset with outer and hole paths.
3. **Outside / Exterior (`cutType: 'exterior'`):**
   - Machining: Full cutout of the part (e.g. picture frame or washer).
   - In CNC CAM practice:
     - Outer boundary $L_{\text{out}}$ is cut with `shaper:cutType="exterior"`.
     - Inner hole boundaries $L_{\text{in}}$ are cut with `shaper:cutType="interior"`.
     - Tool cuts inner holes FIRST (while stock is rigid), then outer boundary (freeing the part).
   - Prepare Look: Outside kerf band on outer boundary, inside kerf bands on inner boundaries.
4. **Inside / Interior (`cutType: 'interior'`):**
   - Machining: Inverted cutout / aperture with island.
   - Outer boundary $L_{\text{out}}$ cut with `shaper:cutType="interior"`.
   - Inner boundaries $L_{\text{in}}$ cut with `shaper:cutType="exterior"`.
5. **On-line (`cutType: 'online'`):**
   - Machining: Trace tool centerline directly on all perimeters of the profile.
   - All loops ($L_{\text{out}}$ and $L_{\text{in}}$) receive `shaper:cutType="online"` at the assigned `cutDepth`.
6. **Guide (`cutType: 'guide'`):**
   - Reference lines for visual alignment on Shaper Origin screen. Emitted with `shaper:cutType="guide"`.

---

### 5. Fusion 360 Divergence
In Fusion 360:
- Planar faces (profiles) are automatically derived by a planar arrangement graph algorithm every time geometry changes. Clicking anywhere inside a boundary selects that dynamic face.

Why SketchStudio chose **EXPLICIT COMBINE** (and *"holes are not automatic"*):
- **What the user gains:**
  1. *Immunity from unintended cutouts:* In Fusion, nesting multiple parts inside a stock border or nesting small parts inside cutouts often inadvertently hollows out components unless painstakingly deselected. In SketchStudio, nested parts remain independent solid parts by default.
  2. *Topological & Solver Stability:* Dynamic face-arrangement engines are computationally heavy ($O(N \log N + K)$) and notoriously glitchy during solver dragging or joint coincidence transitions. Storing an explicit, declared profile record (`state.profiles`) guarantees that toolpath assignments never flicker, invert, or vanish during edits.
  3. *Declarative Simplicity (Wizards-as-Data):* The user declares intent explicitly: "This outer loop and these holes constitute a combined workpiece."
- **What the user loses:**
  1. *Zero-click face detection:* The user must explicitly execute the "Combine" action in Design mode rather than instantly clicking on an enclosed hollow region.
  2. *Automatic face splitting:* If an outer loop is bisected by a line in Fusion, the face splits automatically; in SketchStudio, modifying the outer loop's topology requires re-combining.

---

### 6. Slicing into Build Tasks (One Turn Per Slice)

- **Scope:**
  - Create `packages/core/profile-model.js`: `makeProfile`, `uncombineProfile`, `profilesOf`, `profileForLoop`, `validateCombine`.
  - Add `state.profiles` to `packages/ui/sketch-state.js` (`_captureSnapshot`, `_restoreSnapshot`) for undo/redo.
  - Add `state.profiles` to `packages/core/document.js` (`serializeDocument`, `deserializeDocument`).
  - Delete `holesOfLoop` from `packages/core/group-model.js`.
  - Update `packages/core/shaper-export.js` and `apps/shaper/src/vcarve-view.js` to read holes from `profile-model.js`.
- **Tests:**

  - `tests/document.test.js`: serialization and round-trip verification of `state.profiles`.
  - Existing export and vcarve tests updated and passing.

## TURN 428 — Fix false black constraint-status on under-constrained filleted geometry — branch agy2

- **Owner Repro & Symptom:**
  - Rectangle with bottom-left corner at the origin (fixed), H/V constraints, height dimension = 100 on the left edge, and top-right corner filleted with $R=20$.
  - Symptom: The left line, top line, and fillet arc rendered BLACK (`#202020` / "fixed, cannot move"); the right and bottom lines rendered BLUE (`#60A5FA`). Dragging moved the top line and arc (the width is free), yet they remained black.
  - Expected: Left line is black (pinned by origin + vertical + height 100); top line, fillet arc, right line, and bottom line are blue (depend on the free width).

- **Hypothesis Testing & Bisect:**
  - **H1 (Task 416 c375f26 virtual-sharp pointOnLine) RULED OUT:**
    - Tested at `c375f26~1` (prior to Task 416): top line and arc were already incorrectly marked fixed (`fixedShapes.has(topLine.id) === true`, `fixedShapes.has(arc.id) === true`).
  - **H2 (Owner commit 5bffb68 "solver-respecting rigidity for filleted geometry") RULED IN:**
    - Tested at `5bffb68~1` (immediately before commit): `topLine.fixed === false`, `arc.fixed === false` (both blue).
    - Tested at `5bffb68`: `topLine.fixed === true`, `arc.fixed === true` (both black).

- **Root Cause (`packages/core/constraint-status.js`):**
  - In `analyzeConstraintStatus`:
    - For `CONSTRAINT_TYPES.TANGENT`, lines 490–530 correctly propagate directional axis locks (`lockedAxisY` or `lockedAxisX`) for horizontal/vertical lines tangent to an arc/circle.
    - At lines 533–534, `applyDecIfNeeded(c, centerId)` and `if (sharedRim) applyDecIfNeeded(c, sharedRim)` were called unconditionally, recording `'tangent:auto'` into `dofSources`.
    - In `provisionalDOFFromLocks` (line 168) and Phase 3 (line 768), `'tangent'` was missing from the skip list (which already skips `horizontal` and `vertical` because their effects are accounted for by axis locks).
    - Consequently, the tangency constraint was double-counted: once as an axis lock (reducing joint base DOF from 2 to 1), and again in `otherReductions` (reducing from 1 to 0). This drove the arc center, top rim, and right rim to DOF 0, erroneously causing the solver to treat the arc and top line as fixed.
    - Furthermore, linear constraints (`pointOnLine`, `horizontal`, `vertical`, `tangent`) could reduce an ungrounded joint to 0 DOF in 2D space even when both coordinate axes were not locked.

- **The Fix (`packages/core/constraint-status.js`):**
  1. Removed redundant `applyDecIfNeeded(c, centerId)` and `applyDecIfNeeded(c, sharedRim)` calls from the tangent handler (lines 533–534).
  2. Added `'tangent'` to the skip lists in `provisionalDOFFromLocks` (line 169) and Phase 3 (line 773).
  3. Added linear reduction guards in `provisionalDOFFromLocks` and Phase 3 ensuring ungrounded joints with only linear constraints cannot drop below 1 DOF unless both world coordinate axes are locked.

- **Tests & Evidence:**
  - **Fail-First Test (`tests/filleted-underconstrained-movability.test.js`):**
    - Ran on unpatched code: failed with `AssertionError: Top line must be blue (NOT fixed), true !== false`.
    - Ran on patched code: passed (`filleted underconstrained movability tests passed ✅`).
    - Verified movability: under solver drag target $X=60$ on arc center, arc center moves smoothly from 30 to 60 while the left line remains pinned at $X=0$.
    - Contrast case: adding a width dimension ($W=50$) locks all 5 shapes and all joints to fixed (black), confirming fully constrained sketches remain rigid.
  - **Live Headless Edge Reproduction (SketchStudio):**
    - Captured with unpatched code: `.evidence/428/before-bug-top-and-arc-black.png` (verbatim DOM: top line and arc stroke `var(--sk-geo-fixed, #202020)`).
    - Captured with patched code: `.evidence/428/after-fixed-correct-colors.png` (verbatim DOM: left line is `#202020`; top line, arc, right line, bottom line are `var(--sk-constraint-fill, #60A5FA)`).
    - Captured dragged state: `.evidence/428/after-dragged-width-stayed-blue.png` (width dragged from 50 to 80; top line and arc moved and stayed `#60A5FA`).

- **Gate:**
  - `npm run gate` (`scripts/gate.cjs`):
    - `GATE files=157 pass=157 fail=0`
    - `SMOKE 12/12`
    - `HEADLESS-LEFT 0`
    - `HEADLESS-OTHER 0`
    - Exit code 0.

  - `git fetch && git merge --ff-only origin/main` could not fast-forward (`agy1` had `3069ff3..f31e66f` while `origin/main` had `d75f409..95b217c`); merged `origin/main` cleanly into `agy1` before applying 431c changes.
- **did:**
  1. **Pure profile resolution (`packages/core/profile-model.js`)**:
     - Added and exported `resolveProfileViews(state, loops, loopPolys)` returning a `Map<string, { d, invalid, reason, outerLoopId, innerLoopIds }>`. Writes NOTHING into `state` or `state.profiles`.
     - Matches each stored profile to today's closed loops from its surviving member shapes (`matchLoop`), so filleting an outer or hole corner resolves the 5-edge loop and compound arc path `d` without mutating the stored profile record, and deleting hole edges marks the returned view `{ invalid: true, reason: 'Hole loop missing or open' }` while preserving `outerLoopId` and outer `d`.

  2. **Renderer (`packages/ui/svg-renderer.js`)**:
     - Replaced `profileToPathD` / `p.d` / `p.invalid` with `resolveProfileViews(st)` inside `draw`.
     - Emits background fill beneath shapes and emits invalid profile warning dashed strokes (`stroke="#ef4444" stroke-dasharray=...`) right after the shape stroke pass (beneath joints, `pointer-events="none"`) so the red dashed warning outline is visibly rendered over the blue geometry lines rather than occluded beneath them.
     - Re-measured per-frame render cost on a 200-shape (50-loop) sketch over 200 frames (after 30-frame warmup):
       - WITH `resolveProfileViews` (1 profile): `140.97 ms total (0.705 ms/frame) hasTint=true`
       - WITHOUT profiles (0 profiles): `64.78 ms total (0.324 ms/frame) hasTint=false`
  3. **Sweep & deletion (`packages/core/profile-model.js`, `packages/ui/svg-renderer.js`, `tests/profile-model.test.js`)**:
     - Deleted mutating `resolveProfiles` and `profileToPathD`.
     - Removed `invalid`, `invalidReason`, and `d` from `makeProfile`, `derivedProfileForLoop`, and `cloneProfiles` (which now explicitly clones only the declared schema `{ id, name, outer, inners, outerShapes, innerShapes }`).
  4. **No topology-edit record writes**:
     - Added zero profile-record writes to `delete`, `fillet`, or `trim`; all topology tests pass purely via `resolveProfileViews`.
  5. **Tests (`tests/profile-model.test.js`)**:
     - Updated topology tests (outer corner fillet, hole corner fillet, single hole-edge delete, whole-hole delete) to assert `resolveProfileViews` outputs and `deepStrictEqual(state.profiles, beforeProfiles)`.
     - Added test 11 (`Renderer draw() purity`) asserting `deepStrictEqual(state.profiles, before)` before and after `draw(...)` for both valid filleted and deleted-hole invalid cases, plus snapshot/serialize/deserialize/clone assertions that no `invalid`/`invalidReason`/`d` keys exist.
- **evidence:**

## TURN 438 — Single undo step for newly placed dimensions (pre-selection + value commit) — branch agy2

- **Root Cause & Mechanism:**
  - History snapshots capture state *before* mutations. In commit `5bffb68`, `startDimensionFromSelection` in `packages/ui/input-handlers/dimension-tool.js` (Case A single line and Case B two joints) lost `beginDimUndo(state)` / `endDimUndo(state)`, capturing no snapshot prior to dimension creation.
  - When committing the first value of a new dimension in `packages/ui/numeric-input-manager.js` (`handleCommit`), `saveState()` was invoked unconditionally after the dimension already existed, pushing a snapshot holding "line + dimension at measured value".
  - Consequently, Undo #1 restored the dimension at its measured value, and Undo #2 reverted the line.

- **Implementation (Minimal, Exact, Reusing Existing Undo Groups):**
  - `packages/ui/input-handlers/dimension-tool.js`:
    - Wrapped pre-selection constraint creation in `beginDimUndo(state)` / `endDimUndo(state)` in both Case A (single line) and Case B (two joints), identical to click paths.
    - Recorded `c.__birthHistoryLength = state.history ? state.history.length : null;` upon birth after `endDimUndo`.
    - In `resetDimensionState`, called `state.discardSnapshotAt(pc.__birthHistoryLength)` when `pc.__newlyPlaced === true` before clearing flags.
  - `packages/ui/numeric-input-manager.js`:
    - In `handleCommit`: added `const isFirstValue = uiState.target.__newlyPlaced === true;` before clearing `__newlyPlaced`, and skipped `saveState()` when `isFirstValue === true` (`if (!isFirstValue && uiState.appState.saveState) uiState.appState.saveState();`).
    - In `handleCancel`: called `uiState.appState.discardSnapshotAt(uiState.target.__birthHistoryLength)` when `uiState.target.__newlyPlaced === true`.
  - `packages/ui/sketch-state.js`:
    - Added atomic helper `discardSnapshotAt(len) { if (this.history.length !== len) return false; this.history.pop(); return true; }`.
  - Untouched: Click paths (:540-:740), `anchorPlacingDimension`, `input-manager.js`, and all other tools.

- **Verification & Evidence:**
  - Added `tests/dimension-undo-step.test.js`:
    - T1 (Line pre-selection): Ran red before fix (`Error: One undo() must leave NO distance constraint, but found: {"type":"distance",...}`), passes green with fix.
    - T2 (Two selected joints): Commits value 50, 1 undo removes distance constraint and restores original distance. Passed green.
    - T3 (Escape while placing): `resetDimensionState` leaves history length unchanged and no constraint. Passed green.
    - T4 (Escape in value box): `handleCancel` leaves history length unchanged and no constraint. Passed green.
    - T5 (Regression): Editing an existing dimension adds exactly 1 history entry, and 1 undo restores previous value. Passed green.
    - T6 (Fillet single-undo): `tests/fillet.test.js`, `tests/fillet-virtual-sharp.test.js`, `tests/filleted-rectangle-rigidity.test.js`, `tests/filleted-underconstrained-movability.test.js` all green.
    - Measured click path: `CLICK_PATH_UNDO_COUNT: 2`.
  - Updated `tests/dimension-preselection-workflow.test.js` to assert single undo step across preselection and value commit.
  - Live Headless Edge Captures in `.evidence/438/`:
    - Shaper: `shaper-before-undo.png` (`md5=0a190b4a26cd2d76334925d00ce43889`) vs `shaper-after-undo.png` (`md5=f70ce42cc728341c795b204284ae9dd4`).
    - SketchStudio: `sketchstudio-before-undo.png` (`md5=1c0ca23ea16c8a99f88658c9986c1b38`) vs `sketchstudio-after-undo.png` (`md5=60ed068d692a1918128afaf07e3b9375`).

## TURN 433 (PROFILE CUT SEMANTICS PLAN) — Cut-Type Semantics on Profiles with Holes — branch agy1

### 1. Context & Today's Audit
- **Problem**: Since TASK 432, a picked profile in Prepare represents an entire face region: either a derived profile (outer loop minus its directly contained holes) or a combined profile (`profile:<id>`).
- **Export Today (`packages/core/shaper-export.js:203-222`)**:
  - `pocket` (`shaper:cutType="pocket"`): constructs a compound `evenodd` path containing both the outer loop and its hole subpaths (`lines 208, 217`).
  - *Every other cut type* (`exterior`, `interior`, `online`, `guide`): lines 211 and 220 call `geom = loopGeom(outerLoop, state, shapeById)`. Holes (`prof.inners`) are silently discarded!
- **Prepare Preview Today (`apps/shaper/src/prepare-view.js:288-341`)**:
  - `computeLook`: for `pocket` (`lines 304-328`), insets outer and outsets holes (`clearedHoles`) to render the pocket hatch.
  - For `exterior` and `interior` (`lines 329-333`), it runs `offsetPolygon(pl.outer.polygon, ...)` on the outer loop only. Holes are not offset or shown as cut paths.
  - For `guide` and `online` (`lines 335-341`), it calls `targetMarkup` which draws the raw compound loops without tool-kerf offset.
- **Declared Cut Types (`apps/shaper/src/shaper.js:24-30`)**:
  - `CUT_TYPES` declares exactly 5 types: `exterior` (Outside), `interior` (Inside), `pocket` (Pocket), `online` (On line), and `guide` (Guide).

---

### 2. Profile Cut Semantics Table (All Declared Cut Types)
When a target profile has outer loop $O$ and directly contained hole loops $\{H_1, H_2, \dots, H_k\}$:

| Cut Type ID (`shaper.js:24-30`) | Menu Label | Outer Loop $O$ Cut Type | Outer Offset Side | Hole Loops $H_i$ Cut Type | Hole Offset Side | Emitted SVG Form |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `exterior` | Outside | `outside` (`#000000`) | Outward ($+r$) | `inside` (`#FFFFFF` / `#000000`) | Inward ($-r$) | Holes first as `inside` `<path>`, then outer as `outside` `<path>` |
| `interior` | Inside | `inside` (`#FFFFFF` / `#000000`) | Inward ($-r$) | `outside` (`#000000`) | Outward ($+r$) | Holes first as `outside` `<path>`, then outer as `inside` `<path>` |
| `pocket` | Pocket | `pocket` (`#7F7F7F`) | Inward ($-r$) | `pocket` (hole boundary) | Outward ($+r$) | ONE compound `<path d="M...Z M...Z" fill-rule="evenodd" shaper:cutType="pocket"/>` |
| `online` | On line | `online` (`none` / `#7F7F7F`) | Center ($0$) | `online` (`none` / `#7F7F7F`) | Center ($0$) | Hole `<path>` elements first, then outer `<path>` (each `shaper:cutType="online"`) |
| `guide` | Guide | `guide` (`#0068FF`) | None | `guide` (`#0068FF`) | None | Hole `<path>` elements first, then outer `<path>` (each `shaper:cutType="guide"`) |

*Note on Offset Distances*: $r = \frac{\text{toolDia}}{2} + \text{cutOffset}$. Outer loop positive offset expands outward from the material; inner hole loop positive offset in `inside` cuts expands inward into the hole void, preserving the material of the face.

---

### 3. Cut Order & Shaper Origin Machine Behaviour
- **Code & Notes Audit**:
  - `packages/core/shaper-export.js:140-270`: elements are gathered into an `items` array in first-seen order, or grouped under `<g fill="..." shaper:cutType="...">` if `options.groupByCut: true` is passed (`main.js:77`).
  - `WORK-LOG.md:11089-11091`: previously discussed V-carve split island depth-first sequencing; no machine-enforcement claims exist in code or logs for 2D profile cuts.
- **Findings**:
  - In standard CNC / woodworking, cutting interior holes **before** exterior perimeters is essential so the workpiece stays firmly clamped/supported by the raw stock until the final through-cut frees the part.
  - In our generated SVG, hole paths will always be emitted **before** outer boundary paths.
  - **UNVERIFIED (Owner Question)**: Does the Shaper Origin handheld router firmware enforce SVG document element order when executing cuts, or does it display all paths on screen and allow the operator to manually select/cut them in arbitrary order? (Emitting holes first in the SVG is physically correct regardless, but machine-side strict sequencing is unverified in repository notes).

---

### 4. Single-Source Derivation Architecture (Preview & Export Parity)
To prevent drift between the Prepare canvas visualizer and the SVG exporter, both must consume ONE shared derivation function in `#core`.
- **Proposed Helper**: `deriveProfileCuts(targetKey, rec, state, loops, loopPolys)` in `packages/core/profile-model.js`:
  ```javascript
  // Returns:
  // {
  //   isCompound: boolean,
  //   cuts: [
  //     { loopId, role: 'outer'|'hole', cutType: 'inside'|'outside'|'online'|'guide'|'pocket', offsetSide: 1|-1|0, poly: [...] },
  //     ...
  //   ]
  // }
  ```
- **How Shaper Export consumes it (`packages/core/shaper-export.js`)**:
  - Iterates `cuts`.
  - For `pocket` (`isCompound: true`): builds compound `evenodd` `d = outerD + ' ' + holeDs.join(' ')` with `shaper:cutType="pocket"`.
  - For other types: emits each cut path in order (holes first, then outer), stamping the derived `cutType` and the profile's cut parameters (`cutDepth`, `cutOffset`, `toolDia`).
- **How Prepare Preview consumes it (`apps/shaper/src/prepare-view.js:computeLook`)**:
  - Iterates the exact same `cuts`.
  - For `pocket`: uses outer polygon inset by $r$ and hole polygons outset by $r$ to draw the hatch pattern.
  - For `outside` / `inside`: applies `offsetPolygon(poly, offsetSide * r)` for each cut (both outer and holes!), rendering kerf band + dashed centerline for EVERY path of the profile.
  - For `online` / `guide`: renders kerf band and center dashed line directly on the loop polygons.

---

### 5. Island Semantics (Holes Inside Holes)
- **Owner Principle**: "An island is only cut if it has its own record."
- **Topology Behavior**:
  - `directlyContainedLoops(parentLoop, allLoops)` (`profile-model.js:366-398`) filters out depth-2 loops: if loop $O$ contains loop $H$, and loop $H$ contains loop $I$ (island), $I$ is **never** part of $O$'s profile. $O$'s profile has hole $H$ only.
  - Case `exterior`: $O$ cuts `outside`, $H$ cuts `inside`. Island $I$ sits in the void of $H$. If $I$ has no record, $I$ is not cut (it drops out with the slug). If $I$ has its own cut record, $I$ is emitted as its own distinct path with its own parameters.
  - Case `interior`: $O$ cuts `inside`, $H$ cuts `outside`. Island $I$ is part of the protected material inside $H$. If $I$ has no record, $I$ is untouched.
  - Case `pocket`: $O$ and $H$ form an evenodd pocket. Material between $O$ and $H$ is cleared; the area inside $H$ (containing $I$) is preserved. $I$ is only cut if assigned its own cut record.
  - In all cases, an island is strictly isolated from the parent profile's cut and never cut automatically.

---

## TURN 438b — Single undo step for click-placed dimensions — branch agy2

- **Root Cause & Mechanism:**
  - In TASK 438, pre-selection dimensions were fixed to be a single undo step. However, dimensions created by CLICKING with the Dim tool still exhibited `CLICK_PATH_UNDO_COUNT: 2`.
  - While click paths (`packages/ui/input-handlers/dimension-tool.js`) had `beginDimUndo(state)` at birth, they lacked the `c.__newlyPlaced = true` and `c.__birthHistoryLength` stamps that 438 introduced.
  - As a result, when the first value was committed in `packages/ui/numeric-input-manager.js`, `isFirstValue` evaluated to false, causing `handleCommit` to push an extra snapshot ("line + dimension at measured value").
  - On Escape during placement or before value commit, click paths previously leaked a history snapshot without removing the pending dimension cleanly from history.

- **Implementation (Single Unified Helper & All Click Doors):**
  - Unified helper in `packages/ui/input-handlers/dimension-tool.js`:
    ```javascript
    function finalizeDimBirth(c, state, inheritedBirthLength){
        endDimUndo(state);
        if (!c) return;
        try { c.__newlyPlaced = true; } catch (_) {}
        c.__birthHistoryLength = typeof inheritedBirthLength === 'number'
            ? inheritedBirthLength
            : (state && state.history ? state.history.length : null);
    }
    ```
  - Routed all 7 dimension birth doors through `finalizeDimBirth`:
    1. Pre-selection Case A (single line): `startDimensionFromSelection`
    2. Pre-selection Case B (two joints): `startDimensionFromSelection`
    3. Click line: `handleDimensionPointerDown` Case B (`shape.type === 'line'`)
    4. Click circle/arc radius: `handleDimensionPointerDown` Case B (`shape.type === 'circle' || shape.type === 'arc'`)
    5. Click point-to-point: `handleDimensionPointerDown` Case B (`hitJoint` second click)
    6. Click point-to-line: `handleDimensionPointerDown` Case A (`hitShape.shape.type === 'line'`)
    7. Upgrade line-to-line / angle: `handleDimensionPointerDown` Case 2a (inherits `pending.__birthHistoryLength`)
  - Escape Behavior Analysis (Keep vs Delete):
    - During placement (before anchor / in cursor-placement mode): Click path has always deleted the pending dimension via `resetDimensionState(state)` (`state.constraints.splice`). With `finalizeDimBirth`, it now additionally discards the birth snapshot via `state.discardSnapshotAt(pc.__birthHistoryLength)`. Pre-selection and click paths both delete the pending constraint and restore history length.
    - In value box (`#dimInput`): With `c.__newlyPlaced = true`, `handleCancel` deletes the uncommitted constraint and discards the birth snapshot, matching pre-selection and standard CAD (Fusion 360) behavior.

- **Verification & Evidence:**
  - Extended `tests/dimension-undo-step.test.js` with tests C1, C1-Esc1, C1-Esc2, C2, C2-Esc, C3, C3-Esc:
    - C1 (Click line): create + commit 75 -> 1 undo removes distance constraint and restores line length 100.
    - C1-Esc1: Click line -> Escape while placing leaves history unchanged and no constraint.
    - C1-Esc2: Click line -> Escape in value box leaves history unchanged and no constraint.
    - C2 (Click radius): create + commit 35 -> 1 undo removes radius constraint.
    - C2-Esc: Click radius -> Escape while placing leaves history unchanged and no constraint.
    - C3 (Click two points): create + commit 60 -> 1 undo removes point-to-point constraint.
    - C3-Esc: Click two points -> Escape while placing leaves history unchanged and no constraint.
    - Click path measurement: asserts `CLICK_PATH_UNDO_COUNT === 1` (verified changed from 2 to 1).
  - Fillet regression tests: all 4 fillet test suites remain green.
  - Live Headless Capture in `.evidence/438b/`:
    - Shaper (`/apps/shaper/index.html`):
      - Line created, Dim tool selected, line clicked directly (no pre-selection), value 3 committed.
      - Before undo: `shaper-before-undo.png` (`md5=d884ca0585478e4f745cea1cc3e78d38`) shows line with dimension 3.0.
      - Dispatched ONE Ctrl+Z:
      - After undo: `shaper-after-undo.png` (`md5=040f9de1361a22784f16eb0d7b4d941e`) shows line with no dimension.
      - Different MD5s verified.
  - Gate (`cmd.exe /c "cd /d D:\APPS\Sketch-Studio-agy2 && npm run gate"`):
    - `GATE files=162 pass=162 fail=0`
    - `SMOKE 12/12`
    - `HEADLESS-LEFT 0`

## TURN 438c — Fix angle/line-line upgrade birth & existing constraint recovery — branch agy2

- **Root Cause & Issues Addressed:**
  1. **Angle / Line-Line Upgrade Birth (Bug 1):**
     - When upgrading from a pending line dimension to an angle or line-line distance constraint (lines ~380-450 in `packages/ui/input-handlers/dimension-tool.js`), the code spliced out `pending` and called `ConstraintManager.createConstraint` with no `beginDimUndo(state)` before it, yet called `finalizeDimBirth(targetConstraint, state)`.
     - Consequently, no birth snapshot existed for the new angle dimension; `isFirstValue` in `handleCommit` skipped the commit snapshot, causing the angle dimension to have no undo entry of its own. A single `Ctrl+Z` undesirably rolled back the user's previous action (e.g., drawing lines).
     - Furthermore, Escape in the value box popped the prior action's history snapshot via `discardSnapshotAt`.
  2. **Existing Constraint Recovery (Bug 2):**
     - When clicking two lines that already had an angle or distance constraint, `createConstraint` returned a duplicate, and the recovery fallback found the existing constraint. It then incorrectly stamped the existing constraint with `finalizeDimBirth`, marking an already existing dimension as newly placed.
     - Pressing Escape in its value box invoked `handleCancel`, which deleted the user's pre-existing dimension from the canvas and popped history.
  3. **Clarification on Escape-in-Value-Box Behavior Change (Correction 3):**
     - On `origin/main`, only pre-selection paths set `__newlyPlaced`, so `handleCancel` previously kept click-placed dimensions at their measured value when Escape was pressed in the input box.
     - With `finalizeDimBirth` stamping `__newlyPlaced = true` across all newly created dimension doors (click and pre-selection alike), `handleCancel` now consistently deletes uncommitted, newly-created dimensions on Escape, matching standard CAD (Fusion 360) behavior.

- **Implementation:**
  - `packages/ui/input-handlers/dimension-tool.js`:
    - In `handleDimensionPointerDown` (case 2a upgrade):
      - Discarded `pending`'s temporary birth snapshot via `state.discardSnapshotAt(pending.__birthHistoryLength)` when discarding `pending`.
      - Checked upfront whether an existing constraint of `type` already exists between `s1` and `s2`. If found, recovered it via `startPlacing` without opening or closing an undo birth, and without calling `finalizeDimBirth`.
      - For brand new constraints, opened a birth with `beginDimUndo(state)` directly before `ConstraintManager.createConstraint`, followed by `finalizeDimBirth(targetConstraint, state)` on success, or `endDimUndo(state)` + `discardSnapshotAt` on failure.
  - `tests/dimension-undo-step.test.js`:
    - Added test C4: click two non-parallel lines → angle dimension → value 45 committed → ONE undo removes angle dimension (lines remain intact) → second undo rolls back prior action (reverting to base line 0).
    - Added test C4-Esc: Escape in angle value box leaves history length and top snapshot reference exactly identical to pre-dimension state, leaving no angle or distance constraint.
    - Added test C5: dimensioning two lines that already share an angle constraint → Escape in value box leaves the existing angle dimension completely intact in `state.constraints` and history unchanged.

- **Verification & Evidence:**
  - `node tests/dimension-undo-step.test.js`: all tests T1-T5, C1-C3 (with Esc variants), C4, C4-Esc, C5 pass green (`CLICK_PATH_UNDO_COUNT: 1`).
  - Fillet regression tests: all 4 suites (`fillet.test.js`, `fillet-virtual-sharp.test.js`, `filleted-rectangle-rigidity.test.js`, `filleted-underconstrained-movability.test.js`) pass green.
  - Repo gate (`cmd.exe /c "cd /d D:\APPS\Sketch-Studio-agy2 && npm run gate"`):
    - `GATE files=162 pass=162 fail=0`
    - `SMOKE 12/12`
