## TURN 433b — Built Profile Cut Semantics on Profiles with Holes — branch agy1

### 1. Unified Cut Derivation Architecture
- **Single Source of Truth (`packages/core/profile-model.js`):**
  - Added and exported `deriveProfileCuts(target, rec, state, loops, loopPolys)`.
  - Resolves target through `resolveTargetKey(target, state, allLoops, loopPolys)`.
  - For open chains: emits chain cut descriptor with `offsetSide: 0`.
  - For compound/pocket profiles: emits single compound cut with `outerPoly` (outerOffsetSide: -1) and `holePolys` (holeOffsetSide: +1), preserving holes in `evenodd` preview hatch and export.
  - For discrete profile cuts:
    - `exterior` (Outside): hole loops emitted FIRST as `interior` (`offsetSide: -1`), outer loop emitted LAST as `exterior` (`offsetSide: 1`).
    - `interior` (Inside duality): hole loops emitted FIRST as `exterior` (`offsetSide: 1`), outer loop emitted LAST as `interior` (`offsetSide: -1`), keeping cutter strictly inside face material.
    - `online` (On line): hole loops emitted FIRST as `online` (`offsetSide: 0`), outer loop emitted LAST as `online` (`offsetSide: 0`).
    - `guide` (Guide): hole loops emitted FIRST as `guide` (`offsetSide: 0`), outer loop emitted LAST as `guide` (`offsetSide: 0`).
  - Parameter inheritance: all hole cuts inherit cut parameters (`toolDia`, `cutOffset`, `cutDepth`) from the parent record.
  - Sketches without holes: `spec.inners` is empty, so only outer loop is emitted with `rec.cutType`, guaranteeing 100% byte-identical export for simple loops.

### 2. Export & Prepare Preview Parity
- **Shaper Export (`packages/core/shaper-export.js`):**
  - Replaced manual per-kind branching with `deriveProfileCuts(e.target, e.rec, state, loops, ensurePolys())`.
  - Iterates over derived cuts in order (holes first, outer last) and maps each to Shaper SVG elements with respective colors and `shaper:*` attributes.
  - Retained `compoundOrLoopGeom` for compound pocket export (`fill-rule="evenodd"`).
- **Prepare Preview (`apps/shaper/src/prepare-view.js`):**
  - Updated `computeLook` to consume `deriveProfileCuts(t, rec, state, loops, loopPolys)`.
  - For pocket: insets outer polygon and outsets hole polygons for the pocket hatch.
  - For outside/inside: renders semi-transparent kerf band + dashed centerline on BOTH outer and hole boundaries at their respective offset sides.
  - For online/guide: renders centerline/guide dashes on both boundaries.
  - **Zero Duplicate Logic**: neither export nor preview contains a second hole or offset loop; both delegate exclusively to `deriveProfileCuts`.

### 3. Verification & Evidence
- **Exact-String Export Tests (`tests/shaper-export.test.js`):**
  - Test 23: Frame with Outside (`exterior`) cut → hole as inside first, outer as outside last.
  - Test 24: Frame with Inside (`interior`) cut → hole as outside first, outer as inside last.
  - Test 25: Frame with Pocket (`pocket`) cut → compound evenodd path.
  - Test 26: Frame with On line (`online`) cut → discrete paths, hole first then outer.
  - Test 27: Frame with Guide (`guide`) cut → discrete paths, hole first then outer.
  - Test 28 (Q4 decision): Outer profile Outside + hole's own loop record On line → 3 paths emitted.
  - All 28 tests pass byte-for-byte; existing tests 1-22 are byte-identical.
- **Prepare View Unit Tests (`tests/prepare-profile-pick.test.js`):**
  - Added tests P9 and P10 verifying that both Outside and Inside cuts produce kerf toolpaths on BOTH outer and hole boundaries with correct offset coordinates. All 12 tests pass.
- **Live Headless Edge Captures (`.evidence/433b/`, untracked):**

  - `.evidence/433b/prepare-frame-inside.png` (MD5: `6D38F6FEBD533FE77C602F5BE38CC4BB`): shows outer kerf band at $-r$ and hole kerf band at $+r$.

## TURN 440 (PLAN) — Pen Plotter Design Geometry Export

### 1. A Toolpath's Target: How Design Geometry Exports by Default
- **Default values in `state.js:219-242` (`makeToolpath`):**
  - `targetType`: `"selection"` (legacy discriminator)
  - `targetArtLayerId`: `targetArtLayerId` (defaults to `null`)
  - `targetShapeIds`: `[]` (starts empty)
  - `plotColorId`: `null` (defaults to null; scheme color used)
- **Pen Plotter Pen Model:**
  - `state.plotColors`: array of physical pens `{ id, name, color, strokeWidth, penSlot }`.
  - Quoting `state.js:162-167` `penIdForShape`:
    ```javascript
    export function penIdForShape(shapeId) {
        const hex = shapeColorFor(shapeId);
        if (!hex || !state.plotColors.length) return null;
        const idx = nearestColorIndex(hex, state.plotColors.map(p => p.color));
        return idx >= 0 ? state.plotColors[idx].id : null;
    }
    ```
  - Quoting `state.js:172-177` `toolpathPenId`:
    ```javascript
    export function toolpathPenId(tp) {
        if (!tp) return null;
        if (tp.plotColorId) return tp.plotColorId;
        for (const id of (tp.targetShapeIds || [])) { const p = penIdForShape(id); if (p) return p; }
        return null;
    }
    ```
- **How a Toolpath Knows Which Shapes Belong to It:**
  1. *Explicit targets:* When `tp.targetShapeIds && tp.targetShapeIds.length > 0`, it resolves those exact shape IDs (checking `state.artLayers` first, then `#core` sketch shapes via `resolveCoreShapes`).
  2. *Explicit art layer:* When `tp.targetArtLayerId` is set, it resolves the shapes of that art layer (`state.artLayers.find(l => l.id === tp.targetArtLayerId).shapes`).
  3. *Default / Pen-matching (#core sketch):* When `!tp.targetArtLayerId` and `(!tp.targetShapeIds || tp.targetShapeIds.length === 0)`:
     - The toolpath targets `#core` sketch geometry (`state.coreSketch.shapes`) filtered by pen:
       - `tpPen = toolpathPenId(tp)`
       - If `tpPen != null`: matches `#core` shapes where `penIdForShape(sh.id) === tpPen`.
       - If `tpPen == null`:
         - If `state.plotColors.length === 0` (clean project start, no palette defined): all shapes have `penIdForShape(sh.id) === null`, so the default toolpath targets ALL `#core` sketch shapes.
         - If `state.plotColors.length > 0`: targets `#core` shapes unassigned to any palette pen (`penIdForShape(sh.id) === null`).
     - This ensures that drawing in Design with the default starter "Outline" toolpath automatically targets and exports all drawn Design geometry without requiring manual target-editing or selection!

### 2. Preview / Export Split Audit & Unification
- **The Split Today:**

## TURN 440 — Unified Pen Plotter Shapes-of-Toolpath Resolution & Design Export

### 1. Root Cause & Architecture
- **Root Cause Verified:**

When drawing in Design, geometry went to `#core` sketch (`state.coreSketch`), which only resolved if explicit IDs were passed.
  - `apps/penplotter/src/preview.js:151-170` had its own separate `resolveToolpathShapes` that only read `targetShapeIds` or `targetArtLayerId`.
  - The default starter "Outline" toolpath has `targetShapeIds: []` and `targetArtLayerId: null`. Neither preview nor export resolved `#core` sketch shapes for this default toolpath.
- **Unified Collector (`apps/penplotter/src/core-geometry.js`):**
  - Implemented single source of truth `collectToolpathShapes(tp)`.
  - Resolution precedence:
    1. Explicit `tp.targetShapeIds`: resolves IDs from `state.artLayers` and `#core` sketch via `resolveCoreShapes`.
    2. Explicit `tp.targetArtLayerId`: resolves `state.artLayers` shapes.
    3. Default / #core sketch geometry: when `!tp.targetArtLayerId` and `targetShapeIds` is empty, matches `#core` sketch shapes against the toolpath's pen (`toolpathPenId(tp)`), or all shapes when no pen/palette is configured.

- **Preview & Export Wiring:**

## TURN 437 (SPINDLE MOTION PLAN) -- CC-A. PLAN ONLY, no product code.
Owner ask: "in Prepare, show the movement of the spindle in the toolpath". All file:line below re-verified on the current origin/main (after 432/433/446/429).

### 0. What exists today (the facts the plan rests on)
- ONE cut derivation: `deriveProfileCuts(target, rec, state, loops, loopPolys)` (packages/core/profile-model.js:659). It returns an ORDERED list of cut descriptors: pocket = ONE compound cut (outerPoly + holePolys, outerOffsetSide -1, holeOffsetSide +1; :699-716); outside/inside/online/guide = HOLES FIRST then the outer LAST (:726-752, offsetSide +-1/0); chain = one open chain, offsetSide 0 (:668-678).
- Preview (apps/shaper/src/prepare-view.js) calls it at :291 and draws a STATIC cutter-centre outline: `offsetPolygon(poly, offsetSide * (toolDia/2 + cutOffset))` (:308, :312, :347), a tool-diameter band (stroke-width = toolDia), guide = dashed (:333-341), pocket = hatch + depth label (:322). There is no notion of order, direction or depth pass.
- Export (packages/core/shaper-export.js `exportShaperSVG`) does NOT emit offset paths. For each cut-plan entry (in `cutPlanEntries()` order = CUT_PLAN Map insertion order, apps/shaper/src/cut-plan.js:23-29) it emits the DESIGN geometry as drawn (`loopToPathD`, loop-geometry.js:122; a circle = two arcs; compound pocket = one path, fill-rule evenodd) plus the attributes shaper:cutType / cutDepth (omitted when 'unset') / cutOffset (omitted when 0) / toolDia (shaper-export.js:84-95). The Origin computes the tool offset itself. V-carve contours are appended AFTER all entries (shaper-export.js:223-239), each as an `online` path with its own `shaper:cutDepth = d/tan(halfAngle)` (vcarve.js:70-83). groupByCut only regroups identical attribute sets (:241-252, first-seen order kept).
- The Simulate/Export tab (#view-simexport, apps/shaper/index.html:266; main.js:56-90) is a Generate/Sync panel only.
- The owner question is already open (NEXT-SESSION.md:108): does the Origin follow SVG path order?

### 1. WHAT MOVES, per cut type  (D = derivable today, from where; N = needs a new declared field)
Path ORDER
- on line / inside / outside: D. Within a target: holes first, outer last (profile-model.js:726-752). Between targets: CUT_PLAN insertion order (cut-plan.js:23).
- pocket: D. One compound path (holes are part of it); between targets as above.
- guide: not cut (reference mark) -> no motion.
- V-carve: D. Contours come after all entries, in generation order = inset step i ascending, rings of one step in Clipper order (vcarve.js:55-76).

DIRECTION along a path
- closed loops (on line / inside / outside): D. loop.joints order. loop-finder traces every bounded face counter-clockwise / positive area (loop-finder.js:9-10), holes included and NOT reversed; arcs flip their sweep flag per traversal (shaper-export.js:43-58).
- chain: D. chain order from findOpenChains (loop-finder.js:139).
- pocket: D. outer + holes as drawn in the compound path.
- V-carve: Clipper output ring winding is UNVERIFIED (vcarve.js:50-52 normalises only the INPUT orientation).
- SCREEN SENSE: "counter-clockwise" is in math coordinates; whether it looks CW on screen depends on the y-down world->screen map. UNVERIFIED -> must be checked before arrows are drawn (slice 1 test c).

DEPTH PASSES
- on line / inside / outside / pocket: N/A in data. There is a single `rec.cutDepth` (default 'unset', apps/shaper/src/shaper.js defaultCutRecord) -> one shaper:cutDepth attribute. No pass count or pass step exists.
- V-carve: D. The depth ladder IS in the data: each contour has its own depth d/tan (vcarve.js:70); each ring is a separate `online` path at its own depth = one "pass" each, shallow to deep.

PLUNGE / RETRACT points
- all cut types: N. Not in our data. The start point of a closed loop = loop.joints[0] (D, arbitrary), of a V-carve ring = ring[0] (D, arbitrary). The real plunge/retract is the Origin's (section 2).

TRAVEL between paths
- N. Not in our data. A straight "air move" from the end of one path to the start of the next is the only honest drawable; the real travel is the operator moving the tool.

NEW DECLARED FIELDS (only if we want to CONTROL the job, not just show it; none is needed for slice 1):
- (a) `rec.passDepth` (mm, default 'unset' = single pass) in the cut record (apps/shaper/src/shaper.js defaultCutRecord + CUT_PLAN) - ONLY if Q2 says the Origin honours it from the SVG.
- (b) `rec.direction` ('auto' | 'ccw' | 'cw', default 'auto') - ONLY if Q1/Q3 say direction is ours to set.
- (c) an explicit cut ORDER list (`state.cutOrder: [targetKey, ...]`, default = CUT_PLAN order) - ONLY if Q1 is yes.

### 2. What the ORIGIN decides vs what OUR SVG decides (no invented machine behaviour)
- CONFIRMED from code: the SVG we emit carries geometry + shaper:cutType/cutDepth/cutOffset/toolDia only (shaper-export.js:84-95). There is no order hint, no pass depth and no direction attribute in our output.
- CONFIRMED from code: the tool offset is applied by the Origin, not baked into our paths (our preview's offsetPolygon is a display approximation; shaper-export.js never calls it).
- UNVERIFIED (not in code or the repo notes) = OWNER QUESTIONS:
  - Q1: Does the Origin cut multiple elements in SVG document order, or does the operator/Origin choose the order?
  - Q2: Does the Origin split depth into passes by itself (its own max pass depth), so cutDepth alone gives passes? Who sets the pass depth: the operator on the tool or the SVG?
  - Q3: Is the direction around a closed path taken from the SVG path winding, or decided by the Origin/operator (climb vs conventional)? The Origin is handheld: the operator walks the router and the tool corrects XY only a little, so the "motion" shown on screen is really the operator's path guide, not a CNC toolpath.
  - Q4: Where does a pass start / plunge and how does it retract between paths? (Z belongs to the tool; we have no field.)
  - Q5: Do V-carve `online` contours at different depths get cut in document order shallow-to-deep, or in the Origin's own order?
- Consequence: everything the view shows must be labelled by what it IS: "order and direction as exported" (certain, from our own data) vs "what the machine will do" (unknown until Q1-Q5 are answered). Slice 1 shows ONLY the first kind.

### 3. THE VIEW (one design)
- WHERE: PREPARE (the owner's words; it already owns the cutter-centre outline, the tool band and the per-target cut records). The Simulate tab is only the Generate/Sync panel and would need the canvas + derivation re-mounted; it stays export-only until an optional whole-job playback (slice 5).
- WHAT: in Prepare, a "Motion" strip under the canvas: Play/Pause, scrub slider (0..total length), speed, and a "Show motion" toggle. With it on: (1) direction chevrons along each cutter-centre path, (2) a tool dot of TRUE tool diameter (world units, scales with zoom) moving along the paths in sequence order, (3) completed length solid / remaining dashed, (4) a depth chip next to the dot showing the current cut depth in the document unit (single cutDepth, or the V-carve contour's own depth), (5) the travel between paths as a thin straight "air move" line styled as NOT a cut.
- ONE DERIVATION: new pure module `packages/core/cut-sequence.js` `deriveCutSequence({ state, entries, loops, loopPolys })` -> ordered [{ targetKey, cutType, kind (loop | compound | chain | vcarve-ring), polygon (design geometry, direction as exported), cutDepth, toolDia, cutOffset, offsetSide, isHole }]. exportShaperSVG's body loop (shaper-export.js:198-239) is refactored to CONSUME it (byte-identical output, proven by the existing export oracles) and the Prepare motion view consumes the SAME list, deriving only the display-side cutter-centre path from `polygon` with offsetPolygon (as prepare-view.js:308-347 does today). Order and direction therefore exist in exactly one place; the view and the export cannot disagree. The timeline (arc-length parametrisation, dot position at s) is a second pure function `packages/core/cut-motion.js` `motionAt(sequence, s)`.

### 4. SLICES
1. SLICE 1 (smallest that shows real motion): extract `deriveCutSequence` from exportShaperSVG with ZERO output change; in Prepare add the toggle, direction arrows and a Play button moving a tool dot (to-scale diameter) along the cutter-centre paths in sequence order. No depth, no scrub, no new fields. Labelled "order and direction as exported".
2. SLICE 2: scrub slider + speed + pause/resume + completed/remaining styling + air-move lines between paths.
3. SLICE 3: depth readout (chip) from cutDepth for pocket/online/inside/outside, and the V-carve contour ladder (each ring at its own depth, shallow to deep).
4. SLICE 4 (only after the owner answers Q1-Q5): Q2 -> `rec.passDepth` + pass-by-pass replay; Q1/Q3 -> `rec.direction` and an explicit order control, with the export honouring them through the same sequence; Q4 -> plunge/retract markers.
5. SLICE 5 (optional): a whole-job playback on the Simulate tab reusing `motionAt` (no new derivation).

### 5. TESTS per slice (Node oracles unless noted; fail-first)
- S1: (a) export oracle: exportShaperSVG output byte-identical before/after the extraction over the existing fixtures (rects, holes-first profile, pocket, chain, vcarve, groupByCut); (b) deriveCutSequence order: holes before outer, targets in CUT_PLAN insertion order, vcarve after the entries, vcarve-excluded loops absent; (c) direction: a CCW-authored square and a CW-authored square give the exported winding in `polygon` (documents the loop-finder CCW fact, including the screen-sense check of section 1); (d) real-event CDP test in Shaper Prepare: toggle on, press Play, the dot's position changes over time and its radius = toolDia/2 x zoom; arrow count > 0; Prepare with no cuts shows no motion UI and no error.
- S2: `motionAt` pure: s=0 -> start, s=total -> end, monotone, continuous across path joins, air-move segments flagged; scrubbing to s puts the dot where playing to s does; pause holds position.
- S3: depth per element: a pocket at cutDepth 6 -> chip 6; V-carve ring i -> d_i/tan, increasing with i; 'unset' -> chip "unset" (no invented depth).
- S4: passDepth 2 on cutDepth 6 -> 3 passes in the replay and (if Q2 = yes) in the export attribute; direction 'cw' flips the exported winding AND the arrows together (one derivation); an order override changes export element order and replay order identically.
- Always: the full gate; a legible screenshot per slice; no view-only code path (the view reads the sequence, never re-derives order).

## TURN 449 (CC-A) -- Prepare shows each cut's CONVENTIONAL travel direction as animated marching dashes
### First-principles derivation (screen = viewed from above; world/SVG y points DOWN, so "on screen" is stated visually)
1. The Origin's cutter rotates CLOCKWISE viewed from above (support article "Climb cutting and conventional cutting"). Owner rule: always conventional, no climb mode or switch anywhere.
2. Conventional = at the contact point the tooth moves in the SAME direction as the tool travels (so it opposes the work's relative feed). Check: facing the travel direction "up the screen", a clockwise-turning tooth at the cutter's LEFT side moves UP (= along the travel: conventional) and at its RIGHT side moves DOWN (= against the travel: climb). (Cross-check with CNC: G41 = tool left of the path with a CW spindle is CLIMB; there the stock being engaged is on the tool's right, which is exactly my "right = climb".)
3. The finish pass engages the thin layer between the bit and the FINISHED WALL, so the engaged material is on the WALL side of the bit. Conventional therefore = the wall stays on the LEFT of the travel direction.
4. OUTSIDE cut (bit outside, wall = the part's edge, part inside the path): part on the left -> COUNTER-clockwise around the part. INSIDE cut (bit inside a hole, wall outside it): wall on the left -> CLOCKWISE. POCKET finish pass: outer wall = an inside cut -> CLOCKWISE; an island = an outside cut -> COUNTER-clockwise. An Outside profile's holes are emitted by deriveProfileCuts as inside cuts (clockwise); an Inside profile's holes as outside cuts (counter-clockwise).
5. Result AGREES with the expected directions in the task (no STOP). Also matches the woodworking rule for a handheld router (outside edges counter-clockwise, inside clockwise).
6. y-axis: the sketch world is y-DOWN (verified: in the Shaper screenshots of 448 the corner (0,0) is top-left and (0,40) is below it). The shoelace area x_j*y_i - x_i*y_j is positive for a clockwise loop ON SCREEN; `orientOnScreen` encodes that and the test checks direction with an independent rule (left-half edges run DOWN the screen = counter-clockwise).
7. On line (material both sides) and Guide (not a cut): NO direction. OWNER QUESTIONS: does the Origin give an On-line cut (and an open chain) a direction, and how should the preview show it? Guide is not cut, so presumably none.
### What changed
- #core (packages/core/profile-model.js, next to deriveCutFootprint): `orientOnScreen(poly, 'cw'|'ccw')`, `arrowsAlongClosed(path, n)`, `deriveCutTravel(footprints)` -> [{ role: outside|inside|wall|island, direction, path (the bit-centre polygon ordered in the travel direction), arrows }]. deriveCutFootprint now also tags each footprint with `cutType` and, for a pocket, exposes the finish-pass centre paths `wall` (outer inset by r+off) and `islandCenters` (holes grown by r+off, round joins) -- the same erosion/dilation the footprint already used, so travel and footprint cannot disagree.
- View (prepare-view.js): for each cut with a direction, a `.sk-travel` path along the centre path (replaces the static dashed centreline for that cut) + a `.sk-travel-arrows` group; on line / guide / chains keep the old static dashed line. A hidden-by-default one-line legend `#prepare-dir-legend` "direction: conventional (Shaper Origin)" is shown only while some cut has a travel (set in refreshLook).
- CSS (apps/shaper/index.html): `.sk-travel` marching dashes = CSS animation `sk-march` on stroke-dashoffset 0 -> -12 (decreasing offset moves the dashes FORWARD along the path); NO requestAnimationFrame. `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`: animation off, static arrows shown instead.
- Export: packages/core/shaper-export.js untouched; the existing exact-string export tests pass in the gate (174/174). Nothing in the cut record changed: no climb field or switch exists anywhere (test asserts the word is absent from shaper.js and prepare-view.js).
### Tests (tests/cut-travel.test.js)
Outside square -> CCW, Inside -> CW (also with reversed input winding: same); Outside frame -> [hole inside CW, outer outside CCW]; Pocket with an island -> [wall CW, island CCW] and the wall path is inset by r; On line, Guide, open chain -> no travel; too-big bit -> none; arrows lie on the path and point along it; CSS: animation present, forward keyframes, arrows hidden by default, reduced-motion rule, no RAF, no climb. Mutation-checked: swapping the role table fails the direction asserts; flipping the y-down sign in orientOnScreen fails them too.
### Live (headless Shaper, real tab clicks; design seeded via state): a frame (Outside) with its hole, an Inside rect, a Pocket with an island, 1/4" bit
- 5 `.sk-travel` paths, legend visible, computed animation-name sk-march; screenshots (reduced-motion shot shows the arrows): Outside top edge arrows point LEFT, left side DOWN, bottom RIGHT, right UP (CCW); its hole and the Inside rect: top RIGHT, right DOWN, bottom LEFT, left UP (CW); Pocket wall CW, island CCW.

## TURN 451 (Pen Plotter persists its own document)
Seat CC-B. Fixes audit finding #1 of TURN 443: after a reload the geometry and active stage came back, but the doc size, pens, toolpaths, settings and shape styles did not.

**Cause (one place):** `sketch-stage.js` created the shared autosave buffer without `hostName`/`getHostData`, so `doc.hosts` stayed empty; nothing else stored the plotter-side state.

**Change**
- New `apps/penplotter/src/plotter-doc.js` = the ONE list of what the plotter owns. `captureHistoryState/applyHistoryState` = the undo subset (art layers, toolpaths, pens, active ids, doc size); `capturePlotterDoc/applyPlotterDoc` = that subset PLUS settings, shapeStyles (Map -> entries) and staticShapeIds (Set -> array), versioned.
- `history.js` `serialize()/restore()` now call the history pair (same fields as before, no copy of the list). Why two subsets: settings, styles and static ids are edited WITHOUT `snapshot()`, so an undo that restored them would silently revert edits made since the last snapshot. Persistence needs them; undo must not touch them.
- `sketch-stage.js`: `createDocumentBuffer({ hostName: 'penplotter', getHostData: capturePlotterDoc })`; after `docBuffer.restore()` a sidecar, when present, is applied and `refreshAfterPlotterRestore()` repaints what was built from defaults at mount (underlay, doc fields, Toolpath settings inputs when that stage is mounted, the fit of whichever canvas is showing, the preview, the Pens/Ops/Active panels). An old buffer has no sidecar -> nothing applied, defaults stay.
- `state.js`: `reseedUid(ids)`. The id counter restarts at 1 on every load; without it a toolpath made after a restore could reuse a restored id ("toolpath12"). Also corrected the `shapeStyle` comment that said nothing persists the map.
- Conflict check requested by the advisor: the sketch restore (`deserializeDocument`) replaces geometry and returns `hosts`; it does not touch plotter state and keeps shape ids (`{...s}`), so toolpath targets and style keys still match. Order: geometry restore, then solve, then plotter apply. No conflict found.

**Tests (all run in the gate)**
- `tests/penplotter-persist.test.js` (live headless, real page reload): real SVG import through the file input, real + Pen click, toolpaths (outline passes 2 dashed; fill crosshatch 30 deg / 1.5 / 0.5), settings, a non-default doc size, a renamed/resized pen; wait for "Saved"; reload. Asserts: active stage; the whole plotter document deep-equal; geometry count; exported G-code deep-equal (byte-identical strings); Pens panel rows; canvas readout "100 x 80 mm"; the feed input; fresh uids don't collide. Then strips `hosts.penplotter` from the saved IndexedDB buffer (an old document) and reloads: geometry kept, doc 200x200, no pens, one default toolpath, default feed.
- `tests/penplotter-doc.test.js` (node): history subset keys unchanged, persisted adds settings/shapeStyles/staticShapeIds/version, round trip through JSON, Map/Set types, absent parts keep defaults, undo restore leaves settings/styles alone, no id collision after restore.
- NOT vacuous: removing the `hostName` line fails the live test at "the whole plotter document ... equal after reload" (after-reload doc 200x200, 0 pens, 1 toolpath), restored by copy; making `applyPlotterDoc` skip `reseedUid` fails the unit test ("fresh ids toolpath5,pen6,toolpath7 vs restored toolpath3,toolpath5,pen5"); restored. (My first version of the id check used ids 9999 and passed even with the reseed removed: vacuous, replaced by ids sitting exactly at the next counter value.)

**Live (headless, real reload, `.evidence/451/`)**: the TURN 443 repro (`tp.cjs persist`): BEFORE == AFTER for doc {100,80}, 6 pens, 6 toolpaths, draw feed 1234, 24 styles, 24 statics, active toolpath, stage; `DIFF {}`; readout "100 x 80 mm  ·  1.98x display"; Design underlay has 24 paths.
- before the fix (TURN 443 capture, shows 200x200, empty Pens, one Outline): `.evidence/451/before-fix-after-reload.png` md5 `b8ba208722eb08846a33f7b37ce8f834`
- after the fix: `.evidence/451/after-fix-after-reload.png` md5 `b64c3f7a33f678d6c18a05cb12e73670` (shows 6 pens, the toolpath tree, the crosshatched circle, "100 x 80 mm").

**Behaviour changes for existing users**
1. A reload now restores pens, toolpaths, settings, styles and doc size (the point). The default empty "Outline" toolpath is replaced by the saved list.
2. The autosave poll (1.5 s) now also serialises the plotter document, and the buffer's hosts sidecar carries it (a few KB).
3. Undo/redo behaviour is unchanged (same fields).
4. **OPEN, for the advisor:** the buffer key is shared across apps and `createDocumentBuffer` writes only ITS OWN host. If the user edits in Studio/Shaper and then returns, their save writes `hosts: {}`, which drops the plotter sidecar (geometry survives, plotter state resets to defaults). Not touched: it lives in shared `packages/ui/document-buffer.js` (preserve unknown hosts on write). Needs a ticket.
5. The sidecar is applied after an async IndexedDB read; an action in the first few ms after load (before the read resolves) is overwritten by the restore.

**Removal sweep:** nothing removed. Callers of the changed `history.serialize/restore`: internal to history.js only (`grep serialize apps/penplotter/src`).

**Gate:** `GATE files=176 pass=176 fail=0`, `SMOKE 12/12`, `HEADLESS-LEFT 0`, `HEADLESS-OTHER 0`.

PLAN ONLY (CC-C, branch agy3). No product code. Verified at agy3 head 8cf5a34 (origin/main 859c896).

### 0. What exists (verified)
- Footprints: `deriveCutFootprint(cuts, rec, state)` packages/core/profile-model.js:764 returns [{kind, fillRule ('evenodd' pocket / 'nonzero' bands), rings, finishRings, center, chain}]. ### 1. STOCK (proposal)
ONE declared field, `stock = { thickness, width, height, margin }`, all BASE mm (same convention as cutDepth), in `hosts.shaper.stock` of the shared document (verbatim host sidecar, packages/core/document.js:30-52; no core change). Needs Shaper to pass hostName 'shaper' + getHostData/setHostData to createDocumentBuffer (slice S0; CUT_PLAN could ride the same sidecar later: separate ticket, advisor's call). Default `{thickness: 19.05 (3/4 in; Q1), width: null, height: null, margin: 12.7}`. width/height null = DERIVED = bounds of (design joints + all footprint rings) grown by margin on every side (a waste skirt around outside cuts, like the real board); non-null = explicit board size centred on the design bounds. Edited in a small card on the Review tab (thickness/size inputs via the existing formatUnit/parseUnit like cut-panel.js:26), not in Prepare.
Through-cuts: depth >= thickness (clamped) = THROUGH: the region has no floor and the bottom face has the same hole, so the background shows through. Unset rules: exterior/interior with cutDepth 'unset' = THROUGH (they are cut-outs); pocket/on-line 'unset' = skipped and listed in a "not shown: N cuts have no depth" line (never guess). Guide = never shown. V-carve depth capped at its own maxDepth and at thickness.

### 2. GEOMETRY: (a) TERRACES. Decision and numbers
Level-set model. Distinct depths d_1<...<d_n (clamped to T). Each cut gives a region (outer + holes) from its footprint with the footprint's OWN fillRule. R_k = union of regions of all cuts with depth >= d_k (nested: R_1 contains R_2 ...). Mesh = top face (stock rect minus R_1) + for each k: floor_k = R_k minus R_{k+1} at z=T-d_k (omitted when d_k>=T) + wall strips along boundary(R_k) from depth d_{k-1} to d_k + bottom face (stock rect minus R_through) + 4 outer side quads. Walls are quads from ring edges (pure arithmetic); flat faces are polygons-with-holes triangulated by earcut.
Heightfield (b) rejected. Numbers at 8x11 in (203.2 x 279.4 mm = 56.8k mm2):
- (b) at 0.5 mm = 227k cells = ~454k triangles (~900k at 0.25 mm). That is 5-10x the budget, and walls are 1-cell staircases: a 1/8 in groove (3.175 mm) is only 6 cells wide, diagonals alias, bit-rounded corners facet at cell size, V-carve steps (dStep 0.5 mm) sit AT the cell size. Needs a normal-map/smoothing hack = a second approximation of the geometry. Build is dominated by filling a 450k-vertex buffer.
- (a): triangles scale with vertex count, not area. A typical sheet (a few hundred ring vertices; arcs sampled by the existing 24-step sampleArc) = 5-40k triangles, and EXACT: walls exactly vertical, bit rounding is exactly the footprint rings Prepare draws, V-carve contours are already per-depth rings = terraces natively (6 mm / 0.5 = 12 levels, each one Clipper union + difference, ms each). Build time well under 100 ms.
- Code size: (a) ~250 lines core + the Clipper helpers; (b) ~120 lines + the smoothing hack. (a) wins on every axis except smooth slopes (ball-nose, V-bit), which (a) approximates with stepped terraces (S4: same dStep, 12+ levels reads as a smooth V at review zoom; the Origin itself cuts V-carve in steps).
ONE derivation: the builder takes ONLY `deriveCutFootprint` output + `rec.cutDepth` + `deriveVcarveFootprint` output + rec.cutterShape. No cut geometry is re-derived in 3D.
Two small additions to #core in S1 (both with tests): (i) `regionsFromRings(rings, fillRule)`, `unionRegions`, `diffRegions` in packages/core/plot/clip.js returning [{outer, holes}] via Clipper PolyTree. The existing unionPolygons is flat nonzero: it would FILL a pocket's islands, because the pocket footprint is evenodd; this is THE trap. (ii) a vendored earcut (mapbox, ISC, ~3 KB) at packages/core/plot/vendor/earcut.js so the builder is three-free and WebGL-free.
Builder home: `packages/core/relief-model.js` (new, pure ES module; imports clip.js + earcut only): `buildRelief({stock, items:[{depth, footprints, cutterShape}]}) -> { levels, meshes:{top,floor,wall,bottom,side:{positions:Float32Array, normals, indices}}, stats }`. The Review view only converts to THREE.BufferGeometry (no geometry logic in the view).

### 3. RENDERING
- three.js `three@0.170.0` (exists on npm, 2024-12, older than 2 weeks). VENDORED, not CDN: Shaper is a shop tool and the Clipper precedent (zero-dep, offline) applies; a CDN failure would blank the tab. Files: packages/ui/vendor/three/three.module.js + addons/controls/OrbitControls.js (examples/jsm; ~1.2 MB + 30 KB, static). S1 verifies r170's module is a single file (the three.core.js split came later; if the pinned tarball is split, vendor both). Importmap gains `"three": "../../packages/ui/vendor/three/three.module.js"` and `"three/addons/": "../../packages/ui/vendor/three/addons/"` (index.html:12-18). Only the Review view imports it, so no other host (SketchStudio, Pen Plotter, Trace) loads it.
- Mount on demand: `await import('three')` inside showMode('review') the first time; nothing at page load. A test asserts index.html has no static three import.
- Axes: sketch (x, y-down) -> world X = x, Z = y, Y = height (top face Y=0, down to -T). Top-view camera up = -Z so it is NOT mirrored versus Prepare.
- Look: MeshStandardMaterial (roughness .8), HemisphereLight + one DirectionalLight from the upper-left; real shading on walls replaces Studio's inner-shadow-by-depth; no shadow maps in S1. S1 = plain warm board colour, floors slightly darker by depth via vertex colour (cheap, mirrors Studio's depth shade).
- Controls: OrbitControls (damping), wheel zoom, right-drag pan, buttons Reset (3/4 iso), Top, Fit; double-click = Fit. Render ON DEMAND (controls 'change' + rebuild), no idle RAF (battery; deterministic headless shot).
- Perf targets: build <= 150 ms and <= 100k triangles for the 8x11 in reference design; >= 30 fps orbit on the owner's laptop; rebuild only when the plan signature changes (the sigOf idea at prepare-view.js:286: cutType|toolDia|cutOffset|cutDepth|cutterShape per cut + stock + state.vcarves); geometry/material disposed when leaving the tab.

Replace "Simulate/Export" with "Review" (Studio's last tab is Review). Same router entry: `data-mode="simexport"` -> `review`, VIEWS key, section `#view-review`; the existing export panel (Generate SVG / ShaperHub buttons) keeps working as a side card INSIDE the Review view (export kept, no behaviour change). Not a 6th tab: the nav is already 5 wide and Review replaces a near-empty placeholder.

## TURN 458 (shared document buffer keeps other apps' host sidecars)
Seat CC-B. From TURN 443/451: the buffer key is shared by every app and a save wrote only its own host, so SketchStudio/Shaper (no host) wrote `hosts: {}` and wiped `hosts.penplotter`.

**Reproduced live first** (headless, real UI, `tests/document-buffer-hosts.test.js` part A on the unfixed code): Pen Plotter saved pens/toolpaths (stored hosts include penplotter); SketchStudio opened on the same origin, real click on Line + two canvas clicks, autosaved; stored buffer then read straight from IndexedDB: `after SketchStudio save: shapes 4 -> 5 | hosts []` and `AssertionError: SketchStudio's save dropped the Pen Plotter sidecar (hosts: [])`. Same keys in all apps (one IndexedDB `sketch-studio-documents` / `current`), so it is real.

**Fix (one place):** `packages/ui/document-buffer.js` `writeBuffer` now does a read-modify-write of `hosts` inside ONE readwrite transaction: `put({ ...doc, hosts: { ...stored.hosts, ...doc.hosts } })`. The buffer replaces only the hosts it owns (its hostName entry); every other host passes through; a host-less buffer owns none, so it deletes none. The change signature (`sig`) still covers only the buffer's own doc, so no extra writes.

**Step 3, every writer of the document:** `grep serializeDocument|createDocumentBuffer` over apps/packages/functions: `serializeDocument` callers = `document-buffer.js` (the only store writer, fixed) and `packages/ui/diagnostic-log.js:110` (builds a Copy-Report blob; it writes no stored document, so nothing to drop). `createDocumentBuffer` callers = penplotter (hostName), shaper and sketchstudio (no host): all go through the fixed `writeBuffer`. No cloud-save or document-file export/import exists in apps/ or functions/ (trace/app.js:25 only mentions omitting it). Nothing else to fix.

**Test** `tests/document-buffer-hosts.test.js` (live headless, in the gate): A = the real repro above (Pen Plotter doc deep-equal after Studio saved and the plotter reloaded); B = in-page buffers with a 40 ms poll: A saves; B saves and A survives; A changes its own sidecar and B stays; B changes and A stays; a host-less buffer saves and deletes nothing. Fails 1/1 on the unfixed code (output above); passes after. Evidence `.evidence/458/before-after.txt`.

**Behaviour changes for existing users:** (1) sidecars of other apps now survive a save (the point); (2) a stored buffer keeps a host's entry for as long as the key lives (no pruning of a host that stops writing); (3) each write is now a get+put in one transaction (still one write per change). A save from a stale tab can still overwrite the OTHER fields (geometry) of a newer one, as before.

**Gate:** `GATE files=180 pass=180 fail=0`, `SMOKE 12/12`, `HEADLESS-LEFT 0`, `HEADLESS-OTHER 0`.

## TURN 454 (Active Toolpath panel follows state.activeToolpathId)
Seat CC-B. Audit finding #3: after + Outline / + Fill from a selection the Active Toolpath panel kept showing the OLD toolpath (and its dropdown listed only the old toolpaths), so edits went to the wrong one.

**Reproduced live first** (`tests/penplotter-active-panel.test.js`, real clicks, unfixed code): real click on the circle edge in Design, Toolpath tab, real click on + Fill: `+ Fill: active fill 2 | panel shows ANOTHER toolpath | labels Toolpath,Draw,Style,Passes` and `AssertionError: the Active Toolpath panel follows the new active toolpath  actual 'toolpath1'  expected 'toolpath4'`.

**Where activeToolpathId is set** (grep): `toolpath-layers-panel.js` 323 (delete), 347 (row click), 409 (createToolpathAndEdit), 500 (createToolpathsFromSelection, the bug), 666 (enterTargetEditing); `interaction.js` 210/252/345/347 (canvas/box selection); `keyboard.js:40` (Esc deselect -> null); `mix-toolpaths.js:46`; `svg-import.js:67`; `active-layer-panel.js:59` (its own dropdown); `state.js:259` (initLayers); `history.js` via `applyHistoryState` (`plotter-doc.js`: undo/redo/restore). Only 3 of ~12 sites refreshed the panel, each with its own `import(...).then(renderActiveLayerPanel)`.

**Fix: ONE refresh point.** `active-layer-panel.js` `syncActiveLayerPanel()`, called from `render-art.js` `renderArt()` in the same panel-refresh block that already redraws the Pens and Operations panels (every path above ends in `render()`/`renderArt`). It rebuilds the panel only when its signature changed: `[activeToolpathId, [id,name,type] of every toolpath, active toolpath's fill/outline/drawOutline]`. An edit made THROUGH the panel records its own signature first (`rememberShown`) so typing never rebuilds the input under the cursor. Removed the per-site calls: `toolpath-layers-panel.js` (row click, enterTargetEditing), `interaction.js` (2), `toolpath-stage.js` onEnter, `sketch-stage.js` post-restore. `renderActiveLayerPanel` is now module-private.

**One more mismatch closed:** with `activeToolpathId == null` (Esc deselects everything, `keyboard.js:40`) the panel used to fall back to the FIRST toolpath and edit it. It now shows a blank dropdown entry and "No active toolpath — pick one above or click a row."

**Tests** (real clicks, in the gate): + Fill shows the new fill's Pattern/Angle/Spacing/Offset controls; typing Spacing 3.5 changes ONLY that toolpath (`spacing: [2] -> [2,3.5]`); row click -> panel follows; delete the active -> panel shows the new active, lists exactly the remaining toolpaths; Esc -> "none" state; row click after none; undo and redo -> panel matches state. Fails on the unfixed code (quote above).

**Behaviour changes for existing users:** (1) the panel now follows every active-toolpath change (the point); (2) NEW: no active toolpath -> the panel shows "none", it no longer edits the first toolpath behind the user's back; (3) the dropdown shows an extra blank entry in that state only.

**Callers swept:** `renderActiveLayerPanel` last external callers removed (5 sites above); `grep renderActiveLayerPanel` now shows only active-layer-panel.js.

## TURN 460 (CC-A) -- Shaper keeps its cut plan and stock across a reload (3D plan slice S0)
- Cause: CUT_PLAN (apps/shaper/src/cut-plan.js) is a module-level session Map and Shaper's createDocumentBuffer had no hostName, so nothing of the cut plan was saved.
- Fix through the host sidecar, like Pen Plotter's 451: main.js createDocumentBuffer({ hostName: 'shaper', getHostData: captureShaperDoc }). ONE Shaper doc serializer, new apps/shaper/src/shaper-doc.js: `captureShaperDoc()` = { version, cutPlan: [[key, record]...] (every field of every record: cutType, cutDepth, cutOffset, toolDia, cutterShape, cutterAngle, ...), stock } and `applyShaperDoc(d)`.
- STOCK: CC-C's apps/shaper/src/stock.js (task 459) is THE stock declaration ({thickness 19.05, width null, height null, margin 12.7}, base mm = the owner-confirmed 3/4 in / 1/2 in); I persist IT (no second declaration). Added one small `setStock(obj)` to stock.js (defaults first, then the known fields present) for the restore. The Review card's thickness field round-trips (test types 1.25 in with real keys, reloads, field shows 1.250 and the stock is 31.75 mm); main.js re-syncs that field after a restore (`showStockThickness`) and re-enters Review if it is the visible mode.
- V-carve records are NOT duplicated: state.vcarves already rides in the buffer's geometry (document.js serializes vcarves), checked.
- Restore order: after the sketch restore (loop/chain ids are derived from shape ids, so stable), then Prepare is re-mounted if it is the visible mode (extracted `mountPrepare()` from showMode; the persisted-mode reload used to mount Prepare BEFORE the async restore finished, i.e. on an empty sketch); if another mode is visible the Prepare view is dropped so the next entry mounts from the restored state; Vcarve already refreshed. An old document (no sidecar) leaves the defaults (empty plan, default stock).
- UNDO (reported, not built): NO cut-field change goes through the sketch history. prepare-view's setFieldOnSelected / applyCutTypeToSelected write CUT_PLAN via setFieldFor with no state.saveState(); the only saveState calls in the Shaper app are the three SVG-import paths in main.js (:228, :239, :295), and those snapshots do not include CUT_PLAN (so undoing an import leaves its cut records behind, orphaned but harmless: stale keys match no loop). So cut-plan edits are not undoable today.
- Merge note: origin/main (459 Review) conflicted in showMode's prepare block with my mountPrepare extraction; resolved keeping `mountPrepare()` plus the new review branch.
- Tests tests/shaper-persist.test.js (headless Edge, REAL reloads): 5 cut records (pocket/outside/inside/on line/guide, cutterShape endmill/ballnose/vbit, cutterAngle 60, offsets incl. negative, depth 'unset') + non-default stock -> after a real reload every record is equal (JSON), the stock equals, the export (inch doc, groupByCut) is byte-identical, Prepare shows the geometry; the Review thickness field round-trip (above); SketchStudio drew a line and saved in between (the 458 guarantee, proven once) and the Shaper plan + stock survived; an OLD document (sidecar deleted from IndexedDB) loads with the empty plan and the stock defaults, geometry intact. Non-vacuous: with the applyShaperDoc call disabled the test fails at "every cut record is equal after a real page reload".

- Behaviour change: Shaper cut assignments and stock now persist across reloads (and across the cross-app buffer); the Prepare view re-mounts once after the async restore when it is the visible mode.

## TURN 453 (Pen Plotter input validation: one declared range per field, one helper)
Seat CC-B. Audit findings #4, #5, #6 and the related minors.

**Unit probe first (finding #6), unfixed code**, `scanlineHatch(square 10x10, 45, spacing)` under `timeout 8`: `spacing 2 -> 4 segments exit 0`; `spacing 0  exit 124` (killed, never returns); `spacing -1  exit 124`. (Probe script `.evidence/453/probe.mjs`.) After the fix: `spacing 0 -> 71 segments exit 0`, `spacing -1 -> 71 segments exit 0`.
Why the app never froze in the audit: `fills/index.js resolveParams` already floored spacing at the registry `min` for the PIPELINE, but the stored value stayed 0/-1 and the raw generators (and dots/stipple/dashed, which the registry never covered for ranges) were unguarded.

**One declaration, one helper**
- `packages/core/plot/params.js`: `coerceParam(def, raw, fallback)`: empty / text / non-finite -> `fallback` (the declared default, or, from a UI, the PREVIOUS value = reject), `integer` rounds, `min`/`max` clamp; `resolveParams`, `sanitizeParams` use it.
- Declared once, where the field lives: fill `SPACING` (`fills/utils.js`, min 0.1 max 100), the fill angle (-360..360) and offset (-100..100) in the fills registry, the outline `DASH_LENGTH` (0.1..100) / `DASH_GAP` (0..100) (`outlines/utils.js`), amplitude (0..20), frequency (0.05..20), passes (integer 1..10); machine fields `MACHINE_FIELDS` + `TOLERANCE_FIELD` (`gcode/params.js`: pen up/down Z -100..100, feeds integer 1..50000, tolerance 0.001..5); plotter-side `apps/penplotter/src/fields.js`: `DOC_FIELD` (10..2000 mm, from the ranges the dialog already showed), `PEN_WIDTH` (0.05..5), `STYLE_WIDTH` (0.05..10).
- Consumers rely on it: the fills/outlines registries and `expandLayerWithFill/Outline` use the shared `resolveParams` (two private copies removed); every generator coerces at its entry (hatch `scanlineHatch` which zigzag/crosshatch use, dots, stipple, concentric, dashed); `renderGcode` coerces the machine fields at its entry (feeds never 0/NaN, Z finite) and THROWS for pen up == pen down (Export shows the message); `optimize()` coerces the tolerance (so preview and export are both covered).
- Inputs: Document dialog (`settings.js`), settings fields, Active Toolpath params (`active-layer-panel.js`: while typing the box is left alone, on commit it shows the KEPT value), pen width (`plot-colors-panel.js`), style width (`sketch-stage.js`), `setDocSize` (import). Empty/text = rejected (previous value kept), out of range = clamped, the box shows the kept value; a refused pen Z pair toasts "Pen up Z and pen down Z must differ".
- A loaded document: `applyPlotterDoc` (`plotter-doc.js`) runs `sanitizeDoc/Pens/Toolpaths/Settings` so an OLD saved document holding a bad value loads clamped.

**Ranges I chose (proposals; none was obvious enough to stop on, say if you want others):** doc 10..2000 mm (the existing dialog limits; an SVG import larger than 2000 mm is now clamped too); feeds 1..50000 mm/min; pen Z -100..100 mm; tolerance 0.001..5 mm; pen-down ABOVE pen-up is ALLOWED (an inverted Z axis is legitimate), only equal is refused.

**Tests (in the gate)**
- `tests/penplotter-validation.test.js` (node): the helper table; every pattern and dashed run for bad spacing / dash values in a CHILD PROCESS with a 20 s timeout (hatch spacing 0 -> 141 segments, terminates); the emitter never writes F0 / NaN for feed 0, -5, '', 'abc', NaN, undefined and refuses equal pen Z; `keepSetting` / `keepNumber` cases; an OLD document with doc 99999 x -5, pen width 99, spacing -1, angle 9999, offset 5000, passes 2.5, dash 0 / -3, feed '', tolerance -1, equal pen Z loads clamped.
- `tests/penplotter-validation-live.test.js` (live, real typing + Tab): Document `-5 -> 10`, `99999 -> 2000`, empty keeps, `0 -> 10`; feeds `'' keeps`, `-5 -> 1`, zFeed `0 -> 1`, tolerance `0` and `-1 -> 0.001`, pen up Z `-1` (== down) refused and explained in the toast; fill Spacing `0, -1 -> 0.1`, `500 -> 100`; Passes `0, -2 -> 1`, `2.5 -> 3`, `99 -> 10`; pen width `-3 -> 0.05`, `99 -> 5`; in each case the box shows the kept value; exported G-code has no F0 / NaN.
- Not vacuous: the live test on the PRE-change input files (settings / active-layer-panel / plot-colors-panel restored from HEAD temporarily) fails at once: `AssertionError: doc width negative clamps to the minimum: "-5" kept -5`; removing the `scanlineHatch` guard makes the unit test's child process die (it accumulates segments forever) -> `AssertionError: child failed`. Both restored.

**Behaviour changes for existing users:** (1) bad values are now clamped/rejected where they used to be stored (the point); (2) a document paper size is limited to 10..2000 mm everywhere incl. SVG import (an import wider than 2000 mm is clamped; before it set any size); (3) fill/outline params gain ranges: angle +-360, offset +-100, dash length >= 0.1, passes integer; (4) pen up Z == pen down Z is refused in the UI and Export throws a message for an old document holding it (the loader resets both to 5 / -1 first, so Export only throws for a direct caller); (5) feed fields are whole numbers 1..50000; (6) the outline/fill panel no longer rewrites the box while typing, only on commit.

**Removed ad-hoc checks (grep after):** `|| 0.1` tolerance fallback in export.js / preview.js, `Math.max(0.01, +width.value || DEFAULT)` in plot-colors-panel, `Math.max(0.1, spacing)` in concentric, `!(w > 0)` in setDocSize, `parseFloat ... > 0` for the style width, the two private `resolveParams` copies in the fills/outlines registries, the hardcoded `min/max` strings of `#docW/#docH` and the pen width input. ## TURN 463 (CC-A) -- Shaper cut edits are undoable through the SHARED history; undoing an import restores the cut plan
- DESIGN, one mechanism = (b) a generic HOST SNAPSHOT HOOK. packages/ui/sketch-state.js gains `hostSnapshot: null` ({ capture() -> JSON-safe, restore(data) }); `_captureSnapshot` adds `host: hostSnapshot.capture()` and `_restoreSnapshot` calls `hostSnapshot.restore(snapshot.host)` (3 lines, fully generic, no Shaper knowledge). Shaper sets it in ensureSketch: capture = `captureCutPlan` (the SAME function captureShaperDoc uses for the persisted sidecar, now split out in shaper-doc.js), restore = `applyCutPlan` + a Prepare refresh. Why not (a): putting CUT_PLAN into the sketch state would make the shared state own an app store (its records, keys, defaults), duplicate the sidecar's source of truth and need Shaper-specific fields in the shared factory; (b) keeps ONE snapshot list (the shared one, no second stack like Pen Plotter's history.js) and ONE definition of "the cut plan" (captureCutPlan) for both undo and persistence. The hook is small and generic, so no STOP.
- EVERY cut edit = one step: main.js `cutEdit(apply)` takes a pre-edit `state.saveState()`, applies the edit, and drops the snapshot again (`discardSnapshotAt`) if the plan did not change (picking the value it already has adds no step). Wired for onPickType / onSetField / new onSetFields (cut-panel: a V-bit angle pick sets shape+angle in ONE step instead of two). migrate/drop on load are not edits (no snapshot).
- IMPORT: the three SVG-import paths already call saveState BEFORE touching shapes or CUT_PLAN, so their snapshots now carry the plan as it was; undoing an import restores plan and shapes together (test), redo brings both back.
- Undo on PREPARE: after an undo the restore hook repaints Prepare (`prepareView.refreshLook()` + card) when only the plan changed (selection and card survive); if the sketch changed (an import undo) it re-mounts Prepare from the restored state (a geometry signature `geomSig`/`prepareSig` decides).
- KEYBOARD: Prepare has no sketcher input layer and the shared Ctrl+Z handler is gated by `isActive: () => currentMode === 'design'` (main.js ensureSketch), so Ctrl+Z on Prepare did nothing. main.js now has ONE document keydown listener that runs only while `currentMode === 'prepare'` (the two gates are mutually exclusive, so a key never fires twice; text inputs are skipped), uses the SAME key mapping as the shared handler (new exported `undoRedoKeyAction(e)` in packages/ui/input-manager.js, which the shared handler now uses too, so the combos exist once) and calls the same `state.undo()/redo()`. Test: one Ctrl+Z consumes exactly one history step (history length -1), not two.
- Tests tests/shaper-cut-undo.test.js (headless Edge, real clicks/keys): cut type -> Ctrl+Z gone -> Ctrl+Y back (selection/card survive); depth step -> undo -> 'unset'; offset preset, bit preset = one step each, the same value again = no step; V-bit angle = one step and one undo reverts it; the Design ribbon #btn-undo/#btn-redo reflect cut edits and drive them; an SVG import (via the real file input) adds a record, Ctrl+Z restores the plan and shapes to before it, Ctrl+Y brings the import back. Mutations: removing the hostSnapshot assignment, and disabling the Prepare keydown listener, each fail "Ctrl+Z on Prepare removes the cut type". (The shared history keeps only 5 steps (maxHistory), so the test clears it before measured edits.)
- Behaviour changes: Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y now work on Prepare and undo cut edits; undoing an import removes its cut records; Design Undo/Redo also revert cut-plan edits made on Prepare (they share the stack); a V-bit angle pick is one undo step.

## TURN 464 (3D REVIEW S3 V-carve + S4 cutter shapes + the two flags)
CC-C, agy3. Gate: exit 0 (GATE_EXIT=0 read directly), GATE files=188 pass=188 fail=0 / SMOKE 12/12 / HEADLESS-LEFT 0.
S4 cutter shapes. New pure `packages/core/cutter-profile.js`: `cutterProfile / cutterTerraces / SHAPE_SLICES {ballnose 6, vbit 5} / isShapedCutter`. A groove cut to depth d has depth D(x) at distance x from its line: ball nose D = (d - r) + sqrt(r^2 - x^2) (only sqrt(r^2-(r-d)^2) wide at the surface when d < r); V-bit D = d - x / tan(half angle) (vbitHalfAngleTan stays the ONE helper, reaches the surface at x = d*tan, capped at the flute radius). Terraces: n steps over half-widths xMax*j/n, each cut at D(mid of its step), the innermost at the true depth.
`deriveCutFootprintAt(cuts, rec, state, halfWidth)` in profile-model.js (approved): deriveCutFootprint with toolDia = 2w and cutOffset += (r - w), so the bit-CENTRE path (r + cutOffset from the wall) stays put and only the swept / opened width changes (pocket: autoOffset kept as derived for the nominal bit). NOTE the 4th argument is the cutter HALF-WIDTH, not z (the terraces are width-slices; the profile maths that maps width<->depth lives in cutter-profile.js). At w = r it returns deriveCutFootprint exactly (tested with deepStrictEqual).
relief-model: an item may carry `shape {cutterShape, cutterAngle, toolDia}` + `footprintsAt(w)` (+ optional `slices`); a non-through shaped cut becomes terraces (entries at depth D(mid), footprint at each half-width). Through cuts and endmills are unchanged (a through cut is cleared at full width; tested that footprintsAt is not even asked). planReliefItems (cut-plan.js) supplies `footprintsAt` from deriveKeyFootprints' `cuts`, which now returns `{rec, cuts, footprints}`.
S3 V-carve. Every contour ring of deriveVcarveContours (the ONE derivation shared with the preview and the exporter) is one V-bit On Line pass at the ring's own depth, exactly what shaper-export emits; planReliefItems turns each ring into an item (cutType online, cutDepth = ring depth, V-bit at state.vcarves[i].vbit.angle, flute dia = 2*depth*tan so it reaches the surface) and the S4 machinery makes each a V. 3 slices per ring (1 when more than 40 rings). Regions that have a V-carve are not also cut by their plan entry (the exporter drops them the same way). NOTE: I did NOT use deriveVcarveFootprint's bands as terraces: those are the SURFACE bands of each ring (width = ring inset) and as flat floors they would cut every band flat at the deepest ring's depth (a wide flat pit, not a V); the physical result is the union of the V passes. Real behaviour this shows: at maxDepth the middle of a wide shape is left UNCUT (the V passes stop at maxDepth), same as the exported passes.
Flags fixed. (1) overlapping labels: `marks` merge by SPOT (10 mm), `keys` lists every cut sharing it (an Outside+Inside on one hole = one label; a far cut keeps its own). (2) faint groove floor in the top view: floors are now clearly darker than the top (tone 0.78, darkening up to 40% over the thickness; walls 0.70; side 1.0 with 45%).
Performance (the first live run on the owner file with shapes came to 221,849 triangles and 29 levels: OVER the 100k target). Two causes found with in-page timing and fixed in relief-model.js: (a) a through-cut kerf is on the boundary of EVERY level, and each level re-drew its wall strip: `levelWalls` now merges an edge that is identical on consecutive levels into ONE tall quad (wall AREAS unchanged: all area tests still pass; the 22k-tri synthetic sheet became 5.7k); (b) level booleans re-processed the whole through region 29 times: floor_k = E_k minus R_k+1 and R_k = union(E_k, near R_k+1) with a pure bbox pre-filter (the far regions carry over unchanged; tested by a far-apart two-depth case that FAILS when the carry-over is removed: "top loses BOTH pockets: 9600 vs 9200").
Measured on the owner's file (6) imported through the real Design Import, with a pocket set to ballnose 6 mm deep, an Inside set to V-bit 60 (nothing fits: a 10 mm bit does not fit that hole, derives to nothing), an On Line set to V-bit 90 / 4 deep, and a V-carve (90 deg, dStep 0.5, maxDepth 3) on the Guide's loop: 38,969 triangles, 29 levels, 289-296 ms build (software WebGL, CPU-bound in Clipper/earcut: floors+diffs ~ half; the 150 ms target is NOT met for this deliberately heavy case; the same file without shapes is ~150-170 ms). Per-feature cost (alone, with the base 12 tris): ball-nose pocket 15.4k tris / 6 levels, V-bit 90 On Line 5.1k / 5 levels, V-carve 6 rings x ~3k = ~17k (3 slices each), unshaped through cuts 2-10k. Terraces cost ~ slices x the groove's ring complexity.
Tests (tests/relief-model.test.js, all in the gate): profile maths + terraces; BALL NOSE 6 mm / 4 deep sampled across the width from the real derivation: centre = 4 deep, still > 3.2 deep at half the radius (a V would be 2.5), shallow at the rim, nothing beyond r, monotone and symmetric, within one step of the true circle; V-BIT 90 and 60: the fitted slope of depth vs distance = 1/tan(half angle) within 12%, each sample within one step, a 60 deg V falls faster than a 90 deg V; END MILL stays one level; budgets; through cut = no terraces; deriveCutFootprintAt at the nominal radius deepStrictEquals deriveCutFootprint, a narrower cutter reaches the wall less; V-CARVE stack (planReliefItems on a 40x20 rect): 6 rings with depths 0.5..3, a floor at each ring's depth, depth ~ inset within one 1 mm step and deeper toward the middle, the middle beyond the last ring uncut, nothing outside; label merge. Mutations (each failed its test, restored from a scratch copy): ballnose not shaped -> "ball: shallow at the rim"; V slope doubled -> "fitted slope 1.14 vs 1.00"; far regions dropped -> "top loses BOTH pockets: 9600 vs 9200".
Export unchanged: `git diff HEAD --stat -- packages/core/shaper-export.js` empty. Behaviour changes for users: Review shows ball-nose / V-bit profiles and V-carves; floors are darker; labels merge per spot. Prepare is untouched (deriveKeyFootprints only gained a `cuts` field).
Evidence (.evidence/464/, local): owner6-464-top / -orbit / -reset / -orbit-zoom (md5 068e721f..., e9a33010..., c9c62e03..., 6f1ace31...). ## TURN 466 (CC-A) -- the shared undo history is 100 deep (was 5)
- MEASURED (headless Edge, `--enable-precise-memory-info`, gc'd before/after 100 captured snapshots; script .evidence/466/measure.cjs, local): TYPICAL = the owner's "8x11 dewalt plongeante copy 1 (10).svg" imported in Shaper: 1693 shapes, 1694 joints, 33 cut records -> 384,212 bytes JSON per snapshot, ~276 KB heap per snapshot. LARGE (synthetic): 2000 shapes, 4000 joints, 500 constraints, 300 cut records -> 423,782 bytes JSON, ~539 KB heap per snapshot (heap/JSON ratio ~1.3 for the large one).
- DEPTH: `export const HISTORY_DEPTH = 100` in packages/ui/sketch-state.js (named constant, comment with the measurements), used as `maxHistory` by the ONE shared state factory, so every app gets it (SketchStudio, Shaper, Pen Plotter's sketcher, Trace). Cost at 100: ~28 MB typical, ~54 MB large; history + redo together never exceed the depth (an undo moves an entry between the two stacks; a new edit clears redo), so the worst case is bounded by that figure. 100 steps keeps memory sane and is deep enough for a CAD session.
- Nothing relied on the old depth: grep of tests for `maxHistory` / history length: only relative checks (`historyBefore + 1`, restored length) in dimension-undo-step and dimension-preselection-workflow, which never cross a cap; tests/undo-redo-ribbon.test.js and shaper-cut-undo.test.js use small counts. The 463 test's `clearHist` helper (it existed only because the 5-step cap made `history.length` stop growing) is no longer needed and is removed; it still passes.
- Test tests/history-depth.test.js: 50 edits -> 50 undos each restoring the exact earlier value in order, then 50 redos, redo cleared by a new edit; past the depth the oldest steps drop (125 edits -> exactly 100 kept, undo reaches 100 steps back); the large sketch (379 KB JSON per snapshot here) x 100 x 1.3 = ~48 MB estimate < the 100 MB bound. Mutation: maxHistory back to 5 fails "the shared state uses the declared depth".
- Behaviour change: Undo now reaches up to 100 steps back (every app); memory grows with history up to the figures above.

## TURN 470 (arc preview never emits NaN / undefined)
Seat CC-B. From TURN 465 item 5: the arc preview could draw `M NaN,NaN` / `<circle cx="undefined">`.

**Deterministic repro FIRST** (`tests/arc-preview-contract.test.js`, unfixed code): `updatePreview(state, 'arc', [], pt, { center: 'cGone', radius: 30, ... })` with `cGone` not in `joints`, then `draw(...)`:
`AssertionError: arc preview with an unresolvable centre emitted: d="M NaN,NaN A 30,30 0 0,1 NaN,NaN" | cx="undefined" | cy="undefined"` (the exact strings from the audit). That is what a frame sees when the centre joint is deleted (tool reset, undo) between the pointer move that set the preview and the next draw.

**Who owns the resolution: the PRODUCER, and the preview-manager enforces the shape.** A preview is a transient snapshot of values the tool just computed (radius, start/end angle and the cursor point were already numbers); only the centre was a live reference, so the preview was half snapshot, half id. The tool has the joints in hand when it builds the preview and the renderer is a frame later, so resolving there is the only place that cannot go stale. Chosen contract (declared in `packages/ui/preview-manager.js`): a preview carries RESOLVED POINTS `{x,y}`, never joint ids. `isValidArcPreview` = centre point + finite radius, start angle, end angle + finite cursor point; `updatePreview` for an arc that fails it CLEARS the preview (no preview, never a half-drawn one). No guard in the renderer: `svg-renderer.js` arc preview now reads `active.preview.center` as the point (the id lookup + raw-id fallback is deleted), so a contract violation stays visible instead of being papered over.
- Producer: `input-handlers/arc-tool.js` passes `center: { x: center.x, y: center.y }` (it already held the joint object).
- Existing renderer test 4 (`svg-renderer-arc.test.js`) fed `center: 'c'` (the old id form); updated to the point form.

**Other previews (step 3), grep + read of the renderer's preview block and every producer of `active.preview`:** all CLEAN, no id-or-point ambiguity in what the preview carries. line / circle / polygon / rect / rect-center / rect-3pt draw from `pt` (a point) plus an anchor looked up from `active.start` / `startPt` / `secondPt` with an explicit rule (`joints.has(...) ? joints.get(...) : null`, no anchor -> nothing drawn); the manager's `line`/`circle` previews also store `p1`/`center: fixedPoints[0]` (an id) but the renderer never reads them for those types (checked); bezier preview holds points (`seg`, `handles`, `anchorDots`); `state.preview.points` (ids) is only read by `getPreviewData`, which maps a missing joint to null. The direct assigners (`line-tool`, `rect-tool`, `live-dimension-input`, `dimension-tool`) all set `pt` to a point. Fillet has no preview in the renderer. Not covered (listed): a NaN cursor point `pt` itself (would need the pointer position to be NaN) and `active.preview.pt === null` for the non-arc types (the renderer would throw a TypeError, not emit NaN; no caller passes null).

**Tests (in the gate):** `tests/arc-preview-contract.test.js`: (1) the repro above (fails on unfixed code, quoted); (1b) the REAL arc tool (`handleArcPointerMove`) previews with a resolved centre and the markup is clean after the joint is deleted (fails if the producer hands the id back: `AssertionError: the real arc tool previews with a resolved centre point: null`); (2) a point-centre preview survives the joint vanishing and still draws the arc + centre dot; (3) invalid radius / angle / centre / cursor are rejected; (4) a markup scan for `NaN|undefined` over line, circle, rect, rect-center, rect-3pt, polygon, arc(p1) and bezier previews, with the anchor joint MISSING and PRESENT.

**Behaviour changes for existing users:** none visible: the preview looks the same; a preview with an invalid arc description is dropped instead of drawn as NaN (SVG parse errors in the console are gone). The id form of `preview.center` is no longer accepted by the renderer (the only producer was arc-tool).

## TURN 471 (Review build performance: profile, cut, cache)
CC-C, agy3. Gate: exit 0 (GATE_EXIT=0 read directly), GATE files=191 pass=191 fail=0 / SMOKE 12/12 / HEADLESS-LEFT 0.
PROFILE (owner file (6) imported through the real Design Import, with the 464 shapes: ball-nose pocket, V-bit On Line, a V-carve; in-page, JIT-warm, 38969 triangles / 29 levels). `buildRelief` now reports `stats.ms` per stage. BEFORE (HEAD, runs 2-6): footprints 85-100 ms (itemPieces: the capsule unions of every terrace, `regionsFromRings`), levels 40-50 (the unions), floors 43-52 (diffs + earcut + emit), walls 30-37, mesh 2-3 => ~205-240 ms build, + planReliefItems 8-10 ms. Node `--cpu-prof` of 8 builds: Clipper `_execTree` = 80% of buildRelief (ProcessEdgesAtTopOfScanbeam 19% + BuildIntersectList 17% = the intersection sweeps of the overlapping capsules), `edgeKey` string building 5.5%, wall edge loop 6.7%, GC 5%. earcut ~3%, mesh upload/BufferGeometry ~2 ms.
WHAT WAS CUT (the mesh is unchanged, see PROOF):
1. Full-width regions of ball-nose/V-bit cuts were built and then thrown away when their terraces existed: now built only when needed (itemPieces).
2. Walls: string edge keys -> 4 integers + a 32-bit hash (collision-safe: a hit is confirmed on the integers); the quads are found from the level REGIONS alone (`wallQuads`) and emitted at their heights (`emitWalls`, no per-triangle cross products): 30-37 -> ~17-20 ms.
3. Flat faces: triangulated ONCE and height-free (`flatTris`, normal +Y; floors/bottom re-emit the same triangles at another height / mirrored).
4. bbox of a region computed once (WeakMap) for the `near` pre-filter.
5. A build CACHE (`createReliefCache`, optional `cache` option; the Review view keeps one): Maps keyed by content signatures, per item (regions of every terrace), per clipped piece (+ the board), per level set E_k / R_k (keys = the SET of cut pieces, not their depths, so a stock-thickness change moves only the through level's depth), per floor/top/bottom triangulation, per wall-quad set. Items carry a `sig` from `planReliefItems` (FNV-1a of the effective record + the cut geometry: polygons, chain shapes + joint coordinates, V-carve ring polygons); an item without `sig` switches the cache off for that build. After each build the maps keep only the keys it used (bounded). Cached values are the SAME objects a cold build makes.
RESULT, same file, in-page: cold build (no cache) 184-198 ms JIT-warm (the first build in a fresh page is ~240-315 ms: JIT + Clipper init); FILL 191 ms (171 misses); CACHED same inputs 4.8-9.2 ms (171 hits, 0 misses); CACHED after a stock thickness change 4.2-6 ms (0 misses); one cut changed (node, 1 of 26 items, full pipeline) 139 ms vs 272 ms cold; plus planReliefItems 8-15 ms. TARGETS: cached rebuild < 30 ms: MET (about 15-25 ms including planReliefItems). <= 150 ms cold on (6) with shapes: NOT MET (about 185-200 ms JIT-warm, 240-315 ms first build): the remaining time is the Clipper sweeps themselves (footprints 80 + levels 40 + floors 45 of ~190) which are unchanged work; going lower needs a faster boolean engine (e.g. a WASM Clipper2) or parallel workers, not more JS tuning. NO WORKER built: a module Worker cannot use the page's importmap (`#core/`), the cut items hold closures (footprintsAt) that cannot be posted, and cloning the ~8 MB of footprints would cost about what it saves; with the cache the build happens once per edit.
PROOF the mesh is identical (owner file, node harness on the exact items the page produced, HEAD's relief-model vs the new one, plus the in-page runs): triangle counts equal per mesh (top 3848, floor 13954, wall 20000, bottom 1159, side 8 = 38969). top, floor, bottom, side: ORDERED vertex-buffer hashes (FNV over positions+normals+indices) equal (39b00e70, 9525f2b1, bb3f2c39, ee55c2ad). WALL: the quads are emitted in another ORDER (a different mesh buffer order, same triangles): canonical (order-independent, per-triangle sorted-vertex hash over all five meshes) EQUAL 16f75229 before and after, and wall AREA equal 21972.0593733688. Also equal canonical hashes for thickness 25 (1d34de3) and for one cut changed (c5608c3c). Cached vs cold: ordered hash identical in-page (7f21eec4 for all builds at 19.05; 99ffbac for cold and cached at 25). PIXELS: the Review of the same file rendered before (464) and after (471): the orbit zoom crop md5 6f1ace31f0de722a02fa149d4d1c9a98 and the top zoom md5 2b6ec5a676c1f584cbcc7ba25f2d95ef are IDENTICAL (full-page shots differ only by the "built in N ms" text).
A real bug found on the way: my first flatTris had the cross-product sign inverted (every flat face wound clockwise = culled by the renderer, invisible from outside) while the stored normals were right and every existing test passed. New WINDING test: every triangle of every mesh must have its index-order normal agree with the stored normal (fails with the inverted sign: "top: triangle 0 is wound against its normal").
Tests (tests/relief-model.test.js, in the gate): cached fill / warm / thickness-change / one-cut-changed / same-depth-new-geometry / smaller board / back are byte-identical to cold builds; warm and thickness change have 0 misses; unused entries are dropped; no-sig disables the cache; signatures follow content (a moved joint changes them). Mutations, each caught: R key by index -> "same depth, new geometry: top.positions"; board dropped from the keys -> "smaller board: top.positions"; floor key without E -> "...floor.positions"; item key without sig -> "...top.positions" (the first draft of the test caught none of these: it only changed depths, whose geometry is the same; strengthened).
Behaviour changes for users: none visible (same mesh, same pixels). Export unchanged (`git diff HEAD --stat` for shaper-export.js empty).
Evidence (.evidence/471/, local): profile-after.txt (all runs with stage breakdown + hashes), owner6-464-*.png.
