## TURN 474 (PROJECTS: the store layer, folders + designs, files, migration)
Seat CC-B. Owner: "it seems like there no save project at all". Before: ONE autosave slot per browser (`#ui/document-buffer.js` on IndexedDB). Now: a project STORE with the Fusion Data Panel model (owner's second reference), file save/open, a recent list, and the old slot migrated. NO sidebar UI (task 473, seat sketch-stage 77); the API was agreed with 77 by message (their questions: newDesign yes, listRecent across all apps with the app shown, subscribe, the buffer exposed per host).
Not touched, as told: SketchStudio's "Save project" button (it saves the SETTINGS config, not the drawing).

**Model.** PROJECT = a folder `{ id, name, pinned, updatedAt }`; DESIGN = one document `{ id, projectId, name, app, updatedAt, document }` (`document` = `serializeDocument` + host sidecars). A "current design" pointer (global, so the cross-app carry still works: another app opens the same current design).

**Where it lives, and why a NEW module (decision asked for).** `packages/ui/project-store.js` (storage + project/design model, no knowledge of app state) beside `document-buffer.js`, which stays the AUTOSAVE LOOP (poll the app state, restore into the app, status) and now writes THROUGH the store: one write path, and the store is testable without a browser or app state. `packages/ui/project-file.js` = the file format + the file seam. `#core/document.js` gains `validateDocument` (the one acceptance check; `deserializeDocument` now calls it).

**Store API** (`getProjectStore()`; all async): designs: `listRecent({app?,limit?})` (across ALL projects, each row has `projectName`, no bodies), `listDesigns(projectId)`, `current()`, `get(id)`, `open(id)`, `newDesign(name,{projectId?})`, `saveAs(name,{projectId?,fromId?})`, `rename`, `duplicate` (same project, not current), `remove` (removing the current clears the pointer), `moveDesign(id, projectId)`, `save(document,{app,id?})` (autosave), `exportFile(id?, seam)`, `importFile(seam,{projectId?})`; folders: `listProjects()` (pinned first, then most recently changed), `createProject`, `renameProject`, `pinProject(id, pinned=true)`, `removeProject` (refuses a non-empty one: a folder never takes work with it); `subscribe(fn)` (here and in other tabs via BroadcastChannel). Buffer (returned by `createDocumentBuffer`): `restore/start/stop/flush`, `openDesign`, `newDesign`, `saveAs`, `saveFile`, `openFile`, `designId`, `store`; `onRestored({restored,hosts,name})` runs after the initial restore AND after open/new/open-file. Each host keeps the buffer in a module-level `docBuffer` (penplotter: `getDocBuffer()` exported from `sketch-stage.js`) for 77's sidebar.
- **Autosave goes to the design the buffer is BOUND to** (the one it loaded/created), not to whatever the global pointer says later: a second tab that opens another design must not get this tab's drawing written into it (test: "B stays bound").
- The 458 rule is kept per design (a save replaces only its own host sidecar; a host-less save deletes none), now in the store's `save`.
- **A design without this app's sidecar resets the app's own state to defaults** (Pen Plotter `resetPlotterDoc()`, Shaper `applyShaperDoc(undefined)` = defaults), otherwise opening a New/other design would keep the previous design's pens/cut plan and autosave them into it.

**Migration of the old slot (the STOP condition: could it lose a user's autosaved drawing in any path? I checked each and found none, so I did not stop).** On first use, if there is no design and the old slot (`sketch-studio-documents`/`kv`/`current`) holds a document, it becomes the design "Untitled" in the default project "My Designs" (neutral, user-facing; "Untitled" stays for the design) and the current design. The slot is READ-ONLY here, never written or deleted: it stays as a backup. Paths: (1) two tabs/apps booting at once: fixed ids + `putIfAbsent` + `setMetaIfAbsent` = exactly one design, later passes never overwrite newer work (tested, live on real IndexedDB with two store instances); (2) designs already exist (flag lost): the slot is NOT imported over them; (3) slot unreadable/empty: nothing created, no error; (4) a tab still running the OLD build keeps writing the old slot after the migration: those writes stay in the slot (not lost, but not in the project store) until reload; a downgrade would see the slot as of the migration. Both are the cost of a backup that is never touched.
- Test impact: the existing live tests that read the old slot directly (`document-buffer-hosts`, `penplotter-persist`, `shaper-persist`) now read the current DESIGN from `sketch-studio-projects`; they still pass, which also proves the three real apps restore/autosave through the store and the cross-app carry (Studio save keeps the plotter/shaper sidecar).

**Files.** One format: `{ "format":"sketch-studio-project", "version":1, "app", "name", "document" }`, 2-space JSON + trailing newline, extension `.sketch.json` (it is JSON, so editors/diff/zip work; a `.json` ending stays openable by any tool; the double extension marks it as ours). Open validates the envelope version, then `validateDocument` BEFORE anything is stored or loaded: a newer file gives "This project was made by a newer version of Sketch Studio (document version 2 is newer than this app understands (1)). Update the app to open it." (nothing stored, the app state untouched). The browser picker is ONE seam (`browserFileSeam`: File System Access API when present, else a download / `<input type=file>`); everything above takes a seam, so tests (and later Drive) plug another. Save -> open -> save is byte-stable per host (tested). The browser seam itself (real picker / download) is NOT exercised by a test (needs a user gesture); the logic above it is. File save/open is per DESIGN, no folder in the file.

**Remote adapter seam (Google Drive next; epic in NEXT-SESSION.md ~l.1263: ONE sign-in door, signing in must NOT start syncing, avatar from Drive `about.get`).** The store talks to an adapter with two levels (`listProjects/getProject/putProject/putProjectIfAbsent/updateProject/deleteProject`, `listDesigns/getDesign/putDesign/putDesignIfAbsent/updateDesign/deleteDesign`, `getMeta/setMeta/setMetaIfAbsent`); in-memory and IndexedDB adapters exist. A Drive adapter (project = Drive folder, design = file with `appProperties` for app/projectId, `modifiedTime` = updatedAt) implements exactly those methods plus two OPTIONAL hooks I added so no store change is needed: `newId(kind)` (async, opaque ids: `files.generateIds`) and `onChange(fn)` (remote changes -> subscribers). Rules written in the module header: meta (current pointer, flags) stays LOCAL (delegate to the IDB adapter); remote `update*` = optimistic concurrency (compare etag/version, re-read, retry); the adapter is only installed by an explicit user choice (signing in does not swap it; a router adapter choosing per project, e.g. a `location` field on the project, is where that lives). Tested with a stub adapter that has async ids + a push hook.

**Tests (all in the gate):** `tests/project-store.test.js` (node, memory adapter): CRUD + recent ordering + app filter + limit, rename/duplicate/remove, autosave into the current design + first autosave creates "Untitled", cross-host sidecars kept (host-less save deletes none), migration (+idempotent, two tabs, existing designs, empty slot), saveAs/duplicate independence, folders (create/rename/pin/order/move/refuse), file envelope + byte-stable round trip + cancel + 5 refusals (newer document, newer envelope, not JSON, other JSON, damaged document), the buffer (restore via migration, autosave target, sidecar survives another app's save, Save As, binding rule, open replaces state, new = empty, saveFile flushes, openFile, refused file changes nothing), the adapter-seam stub. `tests/project-store-idb.test.js` (live, real IndexedDB): the old slot written the old way migrates into "Untitled" in "My Designs" with BOTH tabs agreeing and one design, the slot untouched; the IDB adapter's CRUD, pinned order, move, per-design host merge across two store instances, notifications, and a change through another store instance reaches this one. Mutations: dropping `mergeHosts` fails "both sidecars kept"; skipping the migration fails "the slot became the design Untitled".

## TURN 480 (GOOGLE DRIVE with a RENEWABLE token: server session, Drive adapter, router, account)
Seat CC-B. Owner: "allow to have renewable token" = stay signed in across days, no hourly popup. Ported DDCS Studio's solved design (read-only references: server/googleAuth.js, functions/auth/google/[action].js, web/ui/cloud/googleDrive.js / googleSession.js / authState.js / providers.js), adapted, not copied blindly: renamed (cookies `__Host-sk_gflow` / `__Host-sk_gsess`, header `X-SK-Auth`, message type `sk-google-session`, key-derivation label), the Pages root is the repo root, the GIS fallback and the keep-alive are rebuilt with every browser dependency injectable so they are testable, and DDCS's PKCE-for-Dropbox/OneDrive and Picker parts are left out. NO real Google call in any test.

### 1. The server session (renewable)
`server/googleAuth.js` (all logic) + `functions/auth/google/[action].js` (routing only). Routes on the app's OWN origin: `GET /auth/google/start` (PKCE S256 + state sealed in a 10-minute flow cookie, 302 to Google with `access_type=offline`, `prompt=consent`, scope `drive.file`), `GET callback` (state checked against the flow cookie, code exchanged with the client secret + verifier, the refresh token sealed into a 180-day `__Host-` httpOnly Secure SameSite=Lax session cookie, a page that tells the opener (same origin only) and closes), `POST token` (Origin must equal this origin AND `X-SK-Auth: 1`; refreshes; `{access_token, expires_in}`; Google refusing the refresh token = 401 `lapsed` + cookie dropped; a Google outage = 502 and the cookie is KEPT), `POST logout` (same guards, revokes the refresh token at Google, clears the cookie even if the revoke fails). Sealing: AES-GCM under a key derived from `SESSION_KEY`, the cookie NAME bound as additional data (a flow cookie can never be replayed as a session cookie). UNCONFIGURED (any of `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` / `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` / `SESSION_KEY` missing) = every route 404; the client reads the 404 and uses the GIS token popup (that is also what localhost:8000 does: no Functions there). Scope drive.file only; client id `983232817866-b4pl67uuhfmqdrtah42vaf22ivimfh3j...` in `packages/ui/cloud/providers.js` (public). The secret is never in the repo and I never saw or handled it.

### 2. The client account (`packages/ui/cloud/`)
`google-account.js` `getGoogleAccount()`: `state()`, `signIn()` (SYNCHRONOUS popup / GIS request inside the click), `signOut()`, `subscribe`, `getAccessToken()`, `authedFetch()` (bearer, one re-mint + retry on a 401), `userInfo()` (avatar from Drive `about.get` photoLink, initials fallback, never a userinfo scope), `init()` (probe the server session once, schedule the refresh, wake on tab visible). Server session: re-mint = one same-origin POST, no popup, no gesture. GIS fallback: re-mint inside the next user gesture (the keep-alive arms a capture-phase pointerdown/keydown); a blocked popup is NOT a lapse, only a REFUSED refresh is. `auth-state.js`: the pure three-state gate (signedIn / needsRefresh / lapsed): an EXPIRED token is still signed in. `providers.js`: config + storage keys.

### 3. The Drive adapter behind the 474 seam (`drive-adapter.js`)
project = a Drive FOLDER under one app root folder "Sketch Studio" (appProperties skKind/skPinned/skUpdatedAt); design = a `<name>.sketch.json` FILE whose content is exactly the project file (so it also opens with "Open from file"), appProperties skKind/skApp/skUpdatedAt. Implements the 474 interface (listProjects, getProject, putProject, putProjectIfAbsent, updateProject, deleteProject, listDesigns, getDesign, putDesign, putDesignIfAbsent, updateDesign, deleteDesign, getMeta/setMeta/setMetaIfAbsent) plus the two optional hooks `newId` (files.generateIds) and `onChange` (+ `refresh()` that polls the remote signature). "Delete" = TRASH. Meta (current pointer, flags, the cached root id) stays on this device. Optimistic concurrency: Drive v3 has NO conditional write, so `updateDesign` reads `version`, runs fn, re-reads `version` just before writing, retries up to 4 times re-reading the new content, then throws a readable error rather than overwrite; the window between the last check and the write is small but not zero (the API's honest limit).

### 4. The router (`router-adapter.js`) and the owner's rulings
`getProjectStore()` now builds the store over a ROUTER (local IndexedDB adapter + the Drive adapter, created lazily). Local projects never touch the network (test: zero Drive calls, the Drive adapter is never even constructed). Drive is used only for a project the user explicitly moved: `store.cloud.moveProjectToDrive(projectId)` (copy, VERIFY every design reads back, rewrite the current pointer, delete the local copy LAST; a failed copy leaves the original untouched) and `makeProjectLocal` (the reverse, then trash the Drive copy). Drive projects are listed only while Drive is ON (`cloud.enable/disable/isEnabled`; moving turns it on); remote ids are `drive:`-prefixed and projects carry `location: 'drive'`; a remote listing failure (offline) never hides local work (`cloud.lastError()`); a single design cannot cross between device and Drive ("move the whole project"). SIGNING IN CHANGES NOTHING: tested (same lists before/after sign-in, `driveEnabled` still off, zero Drive file calls). `docBuffer.followMoves(result.designIds)` lets a buffer follow a moved design's new id. Nothing in the UI yet: 77 (473/479) owns the sidebar; the slot contract (state / signIn / signOut / subscribe / userInfo, and the cloud actions) was sent to 77.

### 6. OWNER STEPS (the advisor walks the owner through these; I never ask for or handle the client secret)
Prerequisites already done by the owner: the OAuth Web client exists, the redirect URI `https://sketch-studio.pages.dev/auth/google/callback` is registered (2026-11-08).
A. **Google Cloud console -> publish the consent screen** (otherwise refresh tokens die after 7 days): console.cloud.google.com -> select the Sketch Studio project -> "Google Auth Platform" (older UI: APIs & Services -> OAuth consent screen) -> Audience -> Publishing status -> "Publish app" -> confirm "In production". `drive.file` is non-sensitive: no verification review.
B. **Copy the client secret yourself**: same project -> APIs & Services -> Credentials -> OAuth 2.0 Client IDs -> the Sketch Studio web client -> "Client secret" (copy icon). Do NOT paste it in chat, a file or the repo: it goes straight into the Cloudflare field below.
C. **Make SESSION_KEY yourself** (32+ random bytes; nobody else needs to see it). In a terminal (Node is installed): `node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('base64url'))"`. (Windows PowerShell 5.1 alternative: `$b = New-Object byte[] 32; [System.Security.Cryptography.RandomNumberGenerator]::Create().GetBytes($b); [Convert]::ToBase64String($b)`.) Copy the printed line.
D. **Cloudflare dashboard**: dash.cloudflare.com -> Workers & Pages -> click the project `sketch-studio` -> Settings -> "Variables and Secrets" (older UI: "Environment variables") -> Add -> choose Type **Secret** (not Plaintext) -> add three, one at a time, for the **Production** environment: `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` = `983232817866-b4pl67uuhfmqdrtah42vaf22ivimfh3j.apps.googleusercontent.com` (this one is public, may be Plaintext), `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` = the secret from step B, `SESSION_KEY` = the line from step C -> Save. (Add the same for **Preview** only if you want preview deploys to sign in; without them a preview stays inert, which is fine.) Command-line equivalent from the repo root: `npx wrangler pages secret put GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET --project-name sketch-studio` (and the same for `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `SESSION_KEY`), pasting each value at the prompt.
E. **Redeploy** so the Functions see the new secrets: Deployments tab -> the latest production deployment -> "..." -> Retry deployment (or push any commit to main).
F. **Check it is live** (no sign-in needed): open `https://sketch-studio.pages.dev/auth/google/token` in a browser. `Not found` = the three secrets are not all set on Production (or not redeployed); `{"error":"forbidden"}` = configured and working (a plain GET is refused on purpose). Then sign in from the app: the popup shows Google's consent for "See, edit, create, and delete only the specific Google Drive files you use with this app"; afterwards close the browser, come back the next day: still signed in, no popup.
G. Rotating `SESSION_KEY` (same place) signs every browser out (their cookies stop opening); revoking the app in the Google account page does too (the next token request answers `lapsed`).

New Pages routes `/auth/google/*` answer 404 until the owner sets the secrets.
Uncovered: no real Google or browser run (by design); the keep-alive/popup code is exercised only through fakes; the Drive `appProperties has` query and multipart upload shapes follow Google's documented API but were verified only against my fake, so the first real Drive call is the true test (low risk: same endpoints DDCS Studio uses).

## TURN 496
**Bug:** joints drawn as black "fixed" dots could still move (owner trapezoid: fillet tangent points / arc centres / virtual sharps). Cause (verified): `analyzeConstraintStatus` decided per-joint DOF by heuristic propagation; the Jacobian nullspace was only used as a downward clamp. On main, `tests/joint-dof-truth.test.js` failed with: `j_fillet_mw887bxn_4 / mw887om4_4 / mw887vcz_4 / mw887y37_4 reported 0, true freedom 1`.
**Fix (one place each):** `NewtonSolver.jointFreedom()` (solver/engine.js, exposed as `engine.jointFreedom()`) = nullspace of the SAME `_assemble` rows (non-driven, no mouse_spring) via row-normalised RREF; returns per-joint freedom 0/1/2, free-x/free-y sets and global nullity. `analyzeConstraintStatus` now sets jointDOFs / fixedJoints / constrainedJoints / lockedAxisX/Y from it (heuristic code kept only for dofSources provenance + radialLocked) and returns `dof` = nullity; result cached on a signature of joints+constraints+shapes (renderer calls it each frame). Old Jacobi-eigen block removed. Design panel "DOF n" now = `dof` (was the SUM of per-joint DOFs: fixture showed DOF 12, now 1 = nullity).
**Perf:** fixture (19 joints) 0.37 ms; synthetic 100 joints 3.19 ms; 300 joints 25.61 ms (uncached; cached when unchanged).
**Behaviour changes:** joints with 1 free direction are no longer in constrainedJoints, so they draw as white rings (were black); joints/lines the heuristic called fixed but that can move turn blue/white; DOF count in panel is the nullity. Fully pinned things stay black. Limit: a zero-length distance (value 0) has a degenerate Jacobian row so its joint reads free (linearisation) though it is pinned.
**Tests updated:** cluster-dof-sync case 3 used distance value 0 (degenerate; now offset 3, same intent); filleted-underconstrained-movability asserted the virtual sharp "reads d0 per Task 416" (that was the bug; now asserts not fixed). New: tests/joint-dof-truth.test.js (truth vs report, global DOF == nullity, pin-perturbation cross-check, perf).

## TURN 507 (ops journal: the debug report reproduces a drawing, in order)
**Why:** a pasted report's `document` was only the FINAL state and the `[addConstraint]` log lines came from RELOADING it, so nothing said in what order the drawing was made. The undo history (HISTORY_DEPTH 100) already holds the answer.
**What changed**
- `packages/core/journal.js` (pure, README block at the top): `diffSnapshots` / `applyPatch` (exact inverse) / `buildJournal(history, current, {redoStack, maxBytes})` / `replayJournal` / `describePatch` / `documentHash`. journal = `{base, steps:[{seq,t,label,patch}], redo:[...], current:{seq,hash,counts}, truncated:null|{droppedSteps}}`. Lists are matched by key: joints/shapes/sketches/groups/profiles/vcarves by `id`; **constraints have no stable id in this code base, so they are keyed by their content (canonical JSON)**: an edited dimension shows as one constraint removed + one added (step 4 below). A reordered list falls back to `{replace}`.
- `packages/ui/sketch-state.js`: every stored snapshot is stamped `t` + `label` by ONE helper (`_stamp`); `saveState(label)`, `saveStateForce(label)`, `beginUndoGroup(label)`; default label = `state.currentTool`. undo/redo carry the label (redo entries are labelled with the action they re-do). Undo/redo behaviour is unchanged (only the order of two independent statements in undo()/redo()).
- Labels at the main gestures: delete (constraints/shapes/joints/selection), dimension edit (`dimensionEditLabel` in dimension-seams.js: 'edit dimension 23.6 -> 17', used by numeric-input-manager + live-dimension-input), dimension tool, move dimension label, trim, break, fillet, combine/uncombine, drag snap/inference constraints, toggle construction, sketch new/rename/visibility, Shaper group/ungroup/import/cut plan edit/vcarve region, Trace import. The draw tools keep the default (their tool mode: line, rect, circle, arc, bezier, polygon).
- `packages/ui/diagnostic-log.js`: report gains `journal` (null with no state; `journalError` if building it threw), size cap 3 MB on the journal (oldest steps folded into a newer base, `truncated.droppedSteps`). MAX_TOUCH_EVENTS 60 -> 300; the same ring now also records `keydown` (key, ctrl/shift/alt, inInput; a printable character typed into an input/textarea/select/contentEditable is stored as `"char"`, never its value) and coarse `wheel` (deltaY rounded to 50, throttled 100 ms). All old report fields are unchanged.
- `tests/harness/sketch.js` `replayReport(report)` (verifies against `journal.current.hash`); `scripts/replay-report.cjs <report.json> [out.json] [--redo]` prints the step list and writes the replayed document.
**How to replay a pasted report:** save it to `r.json`, run `node scripts/replay-report.cjs r.json`; feed `doc.geometry` to `createSketch().load(...)`.
**Limits:** the journal holds the DOCUMENT (serializeDocument's parts); a host's own undoable data (`hostSnapshot`, e.g. Shaper's cut plan) is not in it. A plain joint drag does not take a history snapshot (selection-tools only saves for snap/inference constraints), so a drag's movement shows up inside the NEXT step's patch; the replay is still exact because every patch is the difference between consecutive stored states.
**Tests:** `tests/journal.test.js` (60 random sessions incl. undo/redo, removes, reorders, constraint edits, sketches: apply(diff)=b and replay=live; stamps; 120-step cap; redo; old fields), `tests/journal-live.test.js` (real mouse/keys in SketchStudio, Diagnostic Log panel Copy Report, node replay deep-equals the app's document, labels in order, no typed digits in the key ring).
**Evidence (.evidence/507/, local):** `step-list.txt` (scripts/replay-report.cjs on the live session) and `session-report.json` (62596 bytes). Heap for 100 steps on a 100-shape sketch (`heap.txt`): 3.98 MB with or without the stamps (about 40 bytes per step).

## TURN 506 round 2 (G1-G5, #7)
- G1: drive-writer entries carry `cancelled` (set by cancel()); attempt/arm/catch/queue honour it, `write` gets `isCancelled()` and writeRemote never recreates for a cancelled entry. store `forgetRemote(id)` is the one place that drops writer entry, shadow, base, header, copy record (used by remove, removeProject, makeProjectLocal).
- G2: per-design lock `withLock` serialises every Drive read/write of a design (a read never sees our own write half done) and `loadDesign` shares one in-flight run per id (waiters get a clone). While the writer owns a design (queued / in flight / just confirmed) loadRemote returns the writer's newest content and never makes a copy. Conflicted copies are tracked per foreign Drive version: a newer local edit against the SAME version updates that copy (instead of moving the base, which would let the stale payload overwrite the other device's version).
- G3: after dropLocal, if a newer payload arrived the writer re-keeps it.
- G4: removeProject (Drive) drops shadows/bases/headers of its designs (found by header and by shadow.projectId); makeProjectLocal flushes Drive writes first and forgets the moved Drive designs. "On purpose" = we cleared the local copies at the action, so nothing is left to recreate; "Drive lost it unexpectedly" = a local copy still exists, so it is re-created.
- G5: writer `canWrite` (signed in): signed out = no attempt and no retry timer, status "Google sign-in is needed again"; router `onSignInChange` -> writer.resume(); explicit flush still tries.
- #7: covered by G2 owner path (writer.unconfirmed()).

## TURN 517
Fixed coverage-properties findings N-F4 + N-F3, N-F1, N-F2 (branch agents/task-517-fields-fillet).
- N-F4/N-F3 (lost dimension fields): `packages/core/constraints.js` now builds every dimension case (joint distance, line-line, radius, angle) through ONE helper `withDimensionState(obj, params)`, which carries isDriven/driven (both always), drivenReason, dimMode, dimSign, dimSignMode, glyphPos, __pos, labelAngle, labelPos. The per-case copies (and task 511's hand copy in ANGLE) are gone. Behaviour changes for existing documents: radius gets `driven` (was only isDriven); angle always has isDriven/driven (false when driving); dimSign/dimSignMode/labelAngle/dimMode survive. Fillet radius dimension now also carries `driven:false` (fillet.js) so a fillet document is byte-identical after save/load.
- N-F1 (fillet at the origin): the fillet's virtual sharp V is `j_origin` itself when the corner cluster contains it (the origin is already fixed at the corner, both trimmed lines are held to it by pointOnLine, measurement dimensions re-link to it, arc.filletSharp = 'j_origin'); the cluster delete skips j_origin; no virtualSharp joint is created. Nullity of a corner snapped to the origin is unchanged by the fillet.
- N-F2 (polygon corner): `findCornerAtJoint` ignores construction lines when counting lines on a corner (falls back to all lines only if no solid line touches the corner, so a pure-construction corner still fillets as before). The radial MUST stay attached (the polygon's equal-radial constraint uses it), so applyFillet re-links any construction line on the corner to V (the sharp corner, which stays on both trimmed sides): radial length/equality is preserved.
- Tests: new tests/dimension-fields-and-fillet-517.test.js (8 dimension modes x {driving, reference} x {save/load, undo/redo}; fillet at origin triangle + rectangle; hexagon, all six corners). tests/coverage-properties.test.js: KNOWN N-F1, N-F2, N-F3, N-F4's roundtrip entries deleted (documents are now identical after save/load for all 13 drawings).
- Not changed (found): filleting a corner whose joint is `fixed` but not the origin deletes that joint and its fixed flag (nullity 4 -> 6 in a probe).
## TURN 520 (dimension tool + perpendicular: NEW-1, NEW-2, NEW-5, NEW-3)
- NEW-1 dimension-tool.js: `handleDimensionPointerDown` is now a thin wrapper around `dimensionPointerDown`; its `finally` ends any undo group the click opened (also on a throw, nothing caught): the ONE place that owns the group. The out-of-scope `c` disappeared with the NEW-2 rewrite of that branch.
- NEW-2 the point-to-line dimension is ONE `distance` constraint with three joints `[point, line end A, line end B]` (arity = declaration, like joint-form collinear/equal); no helper joint, no pointOnLine. Solver: engine.js sets the existing `__lineLine` row (definitions.js distance: |perp dist P to AB| - value) for it, so it removes exactly 1 DOF (nullity delta -1, no free helper) and holds when the line swings. Understood by: constraint-verifier (measure), svg-renderer resolveDimEnds (P to the foot), updateConstraintOffset + anchorPlacingDimension, live-dimension-input (edit check), dimension-seams toggleDriving, ConstraintManager (_edgeHasDrivingDistance one driver per point+line, _mathPreCheck/_triangleCheck only for 2-joint pairs, validity check), geometry-labels ("Pt - Line n"). New helper `isPointLineDistance` in core/geometry.js. Option chosen: a stored 3-joint distance instead of a `{joint, shape}` form because constraints.js (not mine, task 517) normalises only joints / shapes / isRadius distances.
- NEW-5 line-line value is `Math.abs(perpendicularDistance(...))`. The solver row is |signed|, so the side is not stored (no dimSign needed, unlike H/V where the sign picks a direction).
- NEW-3 ConstraintManager.placePerpendicularFromParallel (called from placeForCreation, the one creation-placement place): from an EXACTLY parallel start (|cross| <= 1e-9 |u||v|, parallel or anti-parallel) the second-picked line turns +90 degrees (counter-clockwise tie) about a fixed/shared joint of that line, else its midpoint. `_sandboxVerify` now calls placeForCreation first (the check must start where the real add starts; positions are restored after). No branch is locked after the turn: the branched perpendicular residual is stationary at exactly 90 degrees (Jacobian row = 0, found while testing: nullity delta 0), so a locked branch would hide the removed DOF.
- Tests: tests/dimension-point-line.test.js (node; the four matrix repros as passing assertions + undo group closes on a throw + DOF -1 + typed value + delete leaves no joint), tests/dimension-point-line-live.test.js (SketchStudio, real mouse/keyboard: point then line, typed value drives 3 -> 4.5 scales the perpendicular distance by 1.5, swing the line by a real drag and the distance holds, ONE Undo removes the dimension; line-line in both click orders is driving and positive). Fail-first: both fail on d703ebb's packages (ReferenceError: c is not defined / undo does not remove the dimension). KNOWN NEW-1/2/3/5, their repro pins (matrix-findings.js) and classify rules deleted; coverage-matrix: 3384 cells, 1783 PASS, 0 unexplained.
- Harness changes needed by the new form: tests/harness/audit/lib.js oracle maps a 3-joint distance to PlaneGCS p2l_distance; inventory.js recognises `addViaManager(CONSTRAINT_TYPES.x` as a creation site (pointOnLine had only the dimension tool's site in its scan; snap-constraints still creates it) and the dim-point-line mode text; matrix-run.js `produces` of dim-point-line = 3 joints.

## TURN 515 (circle radius is a solver unknown, like Fusion; fixes F2)
DESIGN (written before coding):
1. ONE declaration `hasRadiusUnknown(shape)` in packages/core/solver/engine.js: a `circle` with one joint (its centre) and a finite numeric `radius`. Arcs are not touched (their radius stays live through the rim joints).
2. Variable layout (engine.js `_pack`): x = [x,y of every free joint representative ..., radius of every such circle in shapes order]. `_radiusSlot` maps shape id -> k; radius k is x[2*freeReps + k]. No parallel structure: the same x, the same J columns.
3. Dense layout for Definitions (`_positionsFromVector`, now the ONE builder used by `_assemble`): [x,y per joint in insertion order ..., radius k at 2*joints.size + k]. A row reads its circle radius through `params.radiusAt` (a dense index) and writes its derivative into the same outRow; `_assemble` copies the radius columns into J like the joint columns.
4. Rows that read the unknown: distance isRadius (r - value, replaces the inert zero row), point-on-circle (|P-C| - r), tangent line-circle (|s| - r), tangent circle-circle (|C2-C1| - (r1+r2) or |r1-r2|, `radiiAt`), equal with a circle operand (`params.terms`: a circle term is r, a line/arc term is |a-b| of its first two joints, so circle-arc equal is r - |centre-rim|).
5. Write-back: ONE place, `_unpack(x)`: shape.radius = x[...] (the solved value; shape.radius stays the only store).
6. A roll-back needs the radius too: `snapshotSolverState/restoreSolverState(joints, shapes)` exported next to the declaration; the try-a-solve-then-restore sites use them (constraint-manager _preAdd + _sandboxVerify, dimension-seams commitDimensionEdit, dimension-tool's two fixed-pair probes, live-dimension-input validateWithSandbox).
7. commitDimensionEdit: the direct `shape.radius = val` writes are removed; the radius dimension's value drives the unknown through the solve (walked in steps like every other dimension).
8. jointFreedom() returns `radiusFree` (circle ids whose radius column is in the nullspace); nullity counts it; constraint-status puts a circle in fixedShapes/constrainedShapes only if its centre is fixed AND its radius is not free (colour). rankRowRedundant's circle special case goes (the row is real now).
9. Saved files: no format change. The stored `radius` is the start value of the unknown on load and the solved value on save.
10. Arcs: unchanged (3 joints, 6 DOF per bare arc minus its structural equal = 5 = Fusion's arc DOF); reported, not changed.
WHAT CHANGED (commits 855b909, 2e71203 on agents/task-515-circle-radius-dof):
- packages/core/solver/engine.js: `hasRadiusUnknown` (the one declaration), radius slots appended in `_pack` (x) and `_positionsFromVector` (dense; now the only dense builder, used by `_assemble`), one `copyRow` copies joint AND radius columns into J, `_unpack` writes `shape.radius` back (THE write-back point). Synthesis: radius distance -> `radiusAt` (the old inert zero row for a circle is gone; a radius on a missing shape keeps an explicit zero row), point-on-circle / tangent line-circle -> `radiusAt`, tangent circle-circle -> `radiiAt`, equal with a circle operand -> `terms`. `rankRowRedundant`'s circle special case removed (the row is real). `jointFreedom()` returns `radiusFree`. `snapshotSolverState` / `restoreSolverState` exported.
- definitions.js: distance, point_on_line(onCircle), tangent (both forms) and equal read the radius unknown and write its derivative.
- constraint-status.js: a circle is in fixedShapes / constrainedShapes only if its radius is not free (colour).
- Roll-back sites now restore joints AND radii: constraint-manager `_preAdd` + `_sandboxVerify`, dimension-seams `commitDimensionEdit`, dimension-tool's two fixed-pair probes (task 516's file: 2 snapshot/restore lines each, flagged to the advisor), live-dimension-input `validateWithSandbox`.
- dimension-seams.js commitDimensionEdit: the direct `shape.radius = val` writes (3) are removed; the radius dimension drives the unknown and walks in steps like every other dimension. Callers: numeric-input-manager.js:388 (has an engine with getShapes). No function lost its last caller.

## TURN 542
- Flake in tests/numeric-input-self-hiding.test.js (Pen Plotter part, only under load): CAUSE is an app race, not the test. `docBuffer.restore()` awaits an IndexedDB read and then REPLACES the whole sketch state (every constraint becomes a new object). Pen Plotter is the 2nd host in that test, so a design (Shaper's autosave) is stored; when the read lands after the test seeded the sketch and opened the dimension box, the box edits a stale constraint object and the live one stays 50. Instrumented copy (wrapping engine.solve): `solve at onRestored (sketch-stage.js:279) ... load (document-buffer.js:74)` 78 ms after the box opened, then `sameC=false`, Enter walks the stale object 50 -> 80, `"c": [["distance", 50]]`. For users: anything started before the restore lands is thrown away.
- Fix in ONE place, packages/ui/document-buffer.js: new `canvas` option; until the INITIAL restore settles (load + the host's onRestored, or nothing to restore) the buffer ignores pointer / keyboard input on that canvas (one window-capture listener per event type, removed when ready; typing in a text field is not blocked) and carries `data-doc-ready="0"`, then `"1"`. `buffer.ready` is the same signal as a promise. The three hosts (SketchStudio, Shaper, Pen Plotter) each pass their Design canvas (one word each). A failed load of the stored design still boots an empty sketch, silently as before (the existing best-effort `catch` was not changed); the buffer is ready either way.
- Tests: new tests/document-restore-gate.test.js (Pen Plotter with a stored design, loadCurrent held back via a fixture copy of the app's own index.html: a real press is ignored before the restore, the restored design is in place when ready, the edit then lands on the live constraint; verified to FAIL with the gate listener removed). numeric-input-self-hiding.test.js waits on data-doc-ready; shaper-persist.test.js's "viewBox width > 100" wait (task 532, the same race) switched to it.
- Behaviour change for users: pointer / keyboard input on the Design canvas is ignored for the few ms until the saved drawing has loaded. No "Loading..." text added (Pen Plotter's status slot is fixed width, TASK 522, and the restore is a local IndexedDB read).
- tests/polygon-tool-live.test.js (`shaper: a hexagon 0 !== 6`) is NOT this race: an instrumented copy shows `data-doc-ready=1` and tool=polygon before the drag, pointerdown + pointerup delivered, and the Shaper shape count never leaves 0. ## TURN 549 (drawing: one drawn element = ONE undo step, no orphan point)
- Measured first (real pointer + Ctrl+Z, SketchStudio and the Shaper Design tab; .evidence/549/before-*.txt): a single line, rect, circle, arc, polygon, bezier and fillet were already one step each. The bugs: (1) a CHAIN of lines: the floating start joint + coincident of the next segment were made right after the previous commit, outside any step, so they rode into the next step's "before" snapshot: Ctrl+Z on segment 2 left 2 loose joints, on segment 3 left 2 more (the owner's "seq 9 added only a joint"); (2) a draw cancelled by Esc or by picking another tool left its first-click joint behind (rect, circle, polygon, bezier; arc on tool switch) and, for line/rect, a phantom empty undo step (the group opened at the first click was never closed).
- The ONE mechanism (packages/ui/sketch-state.js): `beginDrawStep(label, snapshot?)` opens the step at the element's first click (an optional `snapshot` captured earlier via `captureUndoSnapshot()` is its "before"); `closeDrawStep()` is where a draw that did not commit ends: nothing committed (no new shape) -> the document is restored exactly and the step dropped ('cancelled'); something committed (bezier / line chain kept by Esc) -> step kept ('kept'); a non-draw group (dimension edit, delete, drag) is never touched ('none'). `undo()` mid-draw cancels that draw only; `redo()` closes an open draw first. Callers of closeDrawStep: handleEscape and Ctrl+Z key (input-manager.js), switchToTool (keys) and the shared ribbon's selectTool (buttons), arc's own Esc, the line tool's abort paths (zero-length segment, Enter), polygon's two abort paths. Tools that already had begin/end now call beginDrawStep: line, rect, circle+polygon (base-tool beginDrawing), arc, bezier. Their commit paths (saveState / endUndoGroup) are unchanged.
- Line chain: each committed segment closes its step and remembers the document BEFORE the floating next-start joint (`pendingStepSnapshot`); the next segment's first click opens its step from that snapshot, so undo removes the segment's start joint, end joint, shape and constraints and nothing else (the shared start stays: the previous segment owns it). THE SWITCH for chain granularity (owner/advisor declared choice): SettingsManager `LINE_CHAIN_UNDO` in packages/core/settings-manager.js, 'per-segment' (default) | 'per-tool-session' (the whole chain, first click to Esc / Enter / another tool, is ONE step); read only by line-tool.js (`chainPerSession()`). Not shown in the Style panel.
- Tests: tests/draw-step.test.js (state + real line tool, both settings, snapped-onto point kept, Esc, labels, redo without a floating joint); live (real pointer events, key presses, deep-compare of joints/shapes/constraints): tests/draw-undo-live-*.test.js on SketchStudio (lines, session, shapes, esc, esc-2, switch, switch-2) and draw-undo-live-shaper.test.js (every scenario + the undo stack and journal labels), all via tests/draw-undo-runner.js. Mock states in 31 existing drawing tests got the four new state methods stubbed.
- Before (main) / after (branch), Ctrl+Z once per element: chain of 3 lines left 2 then 2 loose joints (after: 0, 0, and every step exact); Esc mid rect/circle/polygon/bezier left 1 loose joint (after: 0); tool switch mid rect/circle/arc/polygon/bezier left 1-2 loose joints (after: 0); Esc mid line/rect left a phantom step (history 11 -> 12; after: 11 -> 11).
- Behaviour changes for existing users: (a) Esc / picking another tool mid-draw now removes the half-drawn element's points (before: loose points stayed) and takes no undo step; (b) Ctrl+Z mid-draw cancels that draw only (before: undid the previous element); (c) a chain's segment undo no longer leaves the floating start point; (d) a zero-length line click (double-click to end a chain) removes the floating start joint instead of leaving it; (e) a click on the centre again in the polygon tool is cancelled through the same path (no empty step). Nothing a tool draws or snaps to changed.
- Found, not fixed: a fillet leaves a hidden orphan corner joint (`j_fillet_*`) in the document (pre-existing, not part of this task).
## TURN 545
**Task:** every geometry drag is ONE undo step (follow-up of the task 543 diagnosis: journal steps "move dimension label" holding joint moves).
**Proved first (live, real pointer events, SketchStudio, unfixed main):** draw line, line, circle; drag a line endpoint: journal steps stay `["line","line","circle"]` (NO step for the drag); Ctrl+Z then undoes the CIRCLE and the drag together (`circlesAfterCtrlZ: 0`, geometry not back to pre-drag only because the circle vanished). So a plain drag was not undoable alone, and geometry dragged after a label drag lands in the "move dimension label" journal step. Evidence: `.evidence/545/unfixed-proof.txt`, `unfixed-live.txt`.
**Fix (one place, selection-tools.js):** `ensureDragUndo` takes the drag's single snapshot through `state.saveState` at the FIRST pointer move (before the solver moves anything), labelled from `DRAG_UNDO_LABELS` / `DRAG_SHAPE_UNDO_LABELS` (data next to DRAG_TYPES in packages/core/constants.js: drag point / drag points / drag line / drag circle / drag arc / drag shape). A press without a move saves nothing. `settleDragUndo` on release discards the snapshot (`discardSnapshotAt`) when joints, shapes and constraint count equal it (drag ended where it started). The three snap / inference sites on release used beginUndoGroup + saveState (a snapshot taken AFTER the move, so Ctrl+Z could not undo the drag) and now call `ensureDragUndo` (a no-op once the drag has its snapshot): drag + snap constraint = one step.
**Behaviour change for existing users:** Ctrl+Z after a drag undoes exactly that drag (before: the previous action, with it). Snap/inference constraints on release no longer make a separate step. A drag that ends where it started leaves no step, but any real movement clears the redo stack (as any new action does). Dimension offset-handle drag (c.offset) still saves no snapshot (not geometry; reported, untouched).
**Tests:** tests/drag-undo.test.js (unit, fail-first: `history 0 -> 0` on main), tests/drag-undo-live.test.js (SketchStudio + Shaper Design). Seven hand-built mock states in older drag tests now spread tests/helpers/undo-stub.js (history + saveState + discardSnapshotAt).
**Fusion:** every drag is one undo step there (known behaviour; to verify in Fusion UI).

## TURN 548 (drag lag: the dragged geometry trails the cursor)
- MEASURED first (headless real CDP mouse at 60 Hz, SketchStudio + Shaper Design, axis snap and grid magnet off so a gap is not a snap; per animation frame a recorder rAF read the last pointer vs the drawn grabbed point). Free point / line body / rect corner / circle rim / chain at 2, 10, 40 px per event, default zoom (78.3 px/unit SketchStudio, 11.3 Shaper) and zoomed out (0.195 / 0.266 px/unit). The gap was 0.00 px every frame in every case EXCEPT a joint drag whose pointer moved more than 100 world units in one event: free point / rect corner at 0.195 px/unit, 40 px/event (205 units): gap +20 px per event up to 164 px, 184.5 px after the cursor stopped, never closing (Shaper 0.266: 107 / 120 px). Other gaps seen were declared snaps/inference (H, perpendicular, joint/shape magnets), all classified from Shaper's state per frame.
- CAUSE: the drag step cap in selection-tools.js (6049734, May 2026: "the solver gets a huge target displacement and can overshoot"): the joint's target was CLAMPED to SolverConfig.MAX_DRAG_STEP (100 world units) from the joint itself, recomputed only on a pointer event, so the joint moved 100 units per event and stayed behind when the cursor stopped (its comment "catches up over the next few frames" never happened: the frame solve keeps the clamped target). It also bent constrained targets: a dimensioned link pulled more than 100 units off its circle lagged the cursor's angle (node: 2.57 deg after 16 events at 0.2 px/unit). Not the cause: the mouse spring (converges: 0.00 px), the frame solve, QUICK_SOLVE, body drags (no cap).
- The cap's protection, re-measured on today's solver: every Fusion drag cell (161) flung in ONE pointer event at 1x/5x/20x/30x/50x without the cap: 0 collapses, every residual < 1e-6; the only failure is line.H.end.across at 70x (a 17 mm H line's end thrown 357 mm in one event): the select tool's VERTICAL inference is read against the other end's pre-event position (88 deg) and aims the end straight above it: the line collapses. With the cap (or a slow drag) it does not. So the step is still a needed safety, for the inference, not the solver.
- FIX (one place, packages/ui/input-handlers/selection-tools.js): the move handler's geometry part became `dragToward(e, svg, state, wpt, atPointer)`; for a JOINT drag a pointer jump longer than MAX_DRAG_STEP is walked as straight sub-moves of at most MAX_DRAG_STEP from the last pointer position (`state.drag.lastPointer`), each through the whole step (mask, inference, target, solve to convergence with SolverConfig.ITERATIONS), the last one AT the pointer (snap applies only there, quick solve, the frame solve follows). The clamp is gone. Body drags and jumps up to 100 units: unchanged (one step). solver-config.js comment updated (MAX_DRAG_STEP keeps its name and default, 0 still disables).
- Tests: tests/drag-follow.test.js (node, the real handlers + frame solve; 6 cases x 2/10/40 px x 78 and 0.2 px/unit: within 1 px of the closest reachable point every frame, nothing moves after the stop; fails on the old code: free-point / rect-corner / chain at 0.2 px/unit 40 px/event 20 px off at frame 1); tests/drag-fling-safety.test.js (161 cells x 1/5/20/70 one-event flings vs the slow drag: no new collapse, same tangent side, residuals, nothing fully constrained moved; control: MAX_DRAG_STEP 0 collapses line.H.end.across x70); tests/drag-step-cap.test.js rewritten (sub-moves of 100, solved to convergence, the last quick at the pointer; 25 / 0; next event starts at the last pointer; body drag one pass); tests/drag-follow-live.test.js (SketchStudio + Shaper, zoomed out, free point 10/40 px, rect corner 40 px: worst gap 0.00 px). tests/harness/coverage/prop-drag.js: its copy of the clamp removed (it never fired: frames of ~1.4 units), it now asserts its frames are shorter than MAX_DRAG_STEP.
- Fusion drag oracle: 134 same as Fusion before and after (161 cells, 0 lost); 0 of 161 cells change geometry (max difference 0 cm).
- Behaviour changes for existing users: (1) a joint drag whose pointer moves more than 100 world units in one event (zoomed out under ~0.5 px/unit, or a pointer jump) puts the joint under the cursor (or at its closest reachable pose) in that event instead of trailing 100 units per event; (2) such an event costs one solve per 100 units (100-constraint sketch: 250-unit jump 10.9 -> 31.9 ms, 1000-unit jump 10.9 -> 115.7 ms per event; ordinary events unchanged); (3) MAX_DRAG_STEP now means the sub-move length.
- FOUND, not fixed (reported): F1 the MIDPOINT inference threshold is in WORLD units (constants.js SNAP.MIDPOINT 1..4, commented "screen pixels") and includes the dragged end's OWN line: at SketchStudio's 78 px/unit a line end within 78..312 px of its own midpoint snaps to it (live: gap 59..77 px, stuck 59 px from the stopped cursor); F2 the H/V attached-line inference reads the other end's pre-event position and ignores an existing H constraint (the x70 collapse above); K548-1 (printed by drag-follow.test.js) the frame solve (500 LM iterations) does not converge when a chain is dragged fast through its fold (up to ~1000 more iterations; 3 of 25 frames, worst 10.2 px): LM steps rejected along the curved manifold under STRUCTURAL_DRAG_RATIO; F4 a chain pulled straight (singular) does not fold back when the cursor comes back inside its reach (live gap 137..310 px); F5 cost: the move handler's solve is ~5x the frame solve (prepass + LM): node 100 constraints move 11.1 ms + frame 2.2 ms, 200: 42.8 + 10.1 ms, 300: 113 + 28.7 ms; live Shaper frame interval 16.7 ms at 100 constraints, 33.3 ms at 200, 150 ms at 300 (task 541 scope).
- Evidence: .evidence/548/ (live-before545-nosnap.json / live-after-nosnap.json, live-before-chainbig.json / live-after-chainbig.json, cost-live-before/after.json, before-mid-drag.png / after-mid-drag.png, fusion-cells-geometry-before-after.txt, probe scripts).
- ADDENDUM (advisor, Fusion measured by task 551): chain default stays 'per-segment' (confirmed; the 'per-tool-session' switch is kept, it costs nothing). Ctrl+Z while a drawing tool is mid-draw (state.active set: line, rect, circle, arc, polygon, bezier) now removes NOTHING: it ends the tool exactly like Esc (handleEscape: the floating start point / half-drawn element goes, committed segments stay, tool goes to Select), and the NEXT Ctrl+Z undoes one element (input-manager.js, the one key handler). Test: 'ctrl+z while line active' in tests/draw-undo-runner.js (2 segments, Ctrl+Z x3: 2 lines left and tool ended, then 1, then 0 = pre-chain document exactly). Ctrl+Shift+Z is also accepted as Redo in this app (kept, harmless; Fusion ignores it). Behaviour change for existing users: Ctrl+Z mid-draw used to undo the previous element (or, for a chain, the last segment) and now only ends the draw.
## TURN 539 (design, written BEFORE coding)
- REPRESENTATION (ONE): two reserved built-in reference LINES `ref_axis_x` / `ref_axis_y`, declared ONCE in constants.js (extending `AXIS_SNAP_TARGETS`: shape id, a reserved fixed end joint `j_ref_x` (1,0) / `j_ref_y` (0,1), the direction). The line is `{ id, type:'line', joints:['j_origin', <end joint>], reference:true }`, so EVERY existing Definition (parallel / perpendicular / collinear / point_on_line / distance line-line / angle / tangent) resolves it unchanged as a fixed line through the origin. They are NOT in `state.shapes` / `state.joints` (no document geometry, nothing to filter out of exports, profiles, thumbnails, the Params list, the shape count, delete, selection): a "scene" layer (`packages/core/reference-lines.js`: layered joints Map + shapes list = the real containers read live, then the reserved entries) is handed to the places that RESOLVE a constraint's shape / joint ids (the solver store, the verifier, the status analysis, the ConstraintManager, the renderer's glyph lookup, the dimension tool), and to NO place that iterates geometry.
- WHY not reserved shapes/joints inside state: ~150 iteration sites over joints / shapes (render, export, profiles, thumbnails, params, bounds, hit test, delete) would each need a filter (a miss = an axis exported / counted); resolution sites are far fewer and a miss only leaves a constraint unresolved (caught by the tests).
- SAVED FILES: a constraint references an axis by its reserved id (`{ type:'parallel', shapes:['L_a_b','ref_axis_x'] }`, `{ type:'pointOnLine', joint:'j7', shape:'ref_axis_y' }`): the same fields as any constraint, an ADDITIVE value. Nothing else is stored; save / load / undo copy constraints already (document.js snapshot copies c.shapes). An old file has no such id and loads unchanged; the 537 horizontal / vertical-with-j_origin constraints stay valid and are not converted.
- PICKABLE NOW (one rule): `referenceLinesPickable(state)` in reference-lines.js, driven by the declared `REFERENCE_PICK_TOOLS` (tool modes that ask for a target: parallel, perpendicular, collinear, tangent, coincident (point-on-line), dimension). Callers of findSnap (hover-manager, the input-manager's click) pass `pickableShapes(state)` = the real shapes (+ the two axes appended ONLY when pickable); findSnap treats a `reference` line as INFINITE and never offers its midpoint. Real geometry wins a tie because the axes come last and a shape must be > 2 px nearer to replace the best. Targets are picked ONLY through findSnap (checked: no tool has a private hit test).
- WHO PICKS A TARGET and what each does with an axis (checked by grep): hover-manager.updateHover (hover highlight only when pickable) | input-manager click (hitShape) | constraint-tools parallel / perpendicular / collinear / tangent / equal / midpoint / coincident / H-V | dimension-tool (distance point-line, line-line, angle) | snap-detection findSnap (axis-x / axis-y snap target of 537 -> point-on-line with the axis) | inference-engine (unchanged: infers from real shapes) | selection-tools (never pickable: not passed) | delete-manager (never sees them) | exports / profiles / thumbnails / parameter-table / shape count (never see them: not in state).
- NOT APPLICABLE: there is no symmetric constraint in the solver (CONSTRAINT_TYPES has none), so "symmetric about an axis" cannot be built by this task; reported.

## TURN 553 (angle dimensions past 180 like Fusion: ONE stored sector)
- Owner-approved: 0 < value <= 360 like Fusion's box (task 551 measured: 30 -> 60 -> 120 -> 179 -> 190 (line at -170) -> 270 (-90) -> 360 (on the fixed line); 0 and -30 refused).
- THE representation (new packages/core/angle-sector.js, replaces task 543's `supplement` flag): a DRIVING angle stores `sector: { ray1, ray2, turn }` = the ray of line 1 / line 2 (+1 its joints[0] -> joints[1] direction, -1 the opposite ray) that bound the sector, and whether it runs from ray 1 to ray 2 counter-clockwise (+1) or clockwise (-1); `value` is its span. A reference stores none (it still measures the sector under its label, task 543). Creation (dimension-tool placing) and promotion (toggleDriving) store the <= 180 sector under the label (creation unchanged: Fusion creates 0..180 too). The renderer draws a driving angle from its sector (reflex arcs, label at the bisector, inside). packages/ui/angle-dimension.js moved into it (core needs it for the load conversion) and deleted.
- Solver row (definitions.js): target CCW angle u -> v = turn * value + (ray1 != ray2 ? 180 : 0) modulo 360. r = k (cross cos t - turn dot sin t) (k = ray1 * ray2) where within 90 degrees of the target: the SAME floating-point row as before up to its sign, so every near-target solve is bit-identical; beyond 90 degrees r = 2 sgn(S) |u||v| - S (C1, monotonic) so the only zero is the target (a 190 is not held by the 10 or 170 pose). Verifier: |theta - target| wrapped, no modulo 180. The pair keeps its CCW order (task 511) unless a caller names a sector; alignParallelOrientation, the one place a line's joints are swapped, flips that line's ray in the angles on it.
- Old files: converted ONCE in deserializeDocument (legacyAngleSector, the only reader of `supplement`): the old row's target nearest the loaded geometry, with the old turn (+value, or -value for `supplement`), and of its two sectors the arc the old build drew (else the one under the label). Deep compare (tests/angle-sector-old-files.test.js, fixture tests/fixtures/angle-dimension/legacy-angles.json written and measured by main 01000da with the one-off .evidence/553/gen-legacy.mjs + tests/harness/angle-legacy.js): 137 documents (d4-triangle, the only one of the 13 audit drawings with an angle; the owner document; 5 line pairs x 4 sectors x joint orders / shared vertex, driving + reference, 50 with `supplement`, 30 typed to 190 / 270 on main): load, 264 edits (+-7), jitter re-solve land on main's geometry with 0.0 difference; 107 arcs identical (worst 2.8e-13). ## TURN 560 -- live-test flakes under machine load (Sonnet subagent, branch agents/task-560-live-test-flakes)
Cause classification (all test/harness side; NO app code changed, nothing to STOP on):
1. HARNESS, the main shared cause: 14 live/browser tests each carried a copy-pasted launcher that picked the CDP debugging port from the clock (`9400 + Date.now() % 80` etc.; ranges overlapped between files). Two runs (two seats' gates, or two tests) that start in the same slot share a port: the second run attaches to the FIRST run's browser and drives its page, and the first run's close kills it. Reproduced with an instrumented copy of the old draw-undo runner pinned to one port (`.evidence/560/instr/orig-fixedport.mjs`, two runs 3 s apart): run A died with `CDP eval threw: {"exceptionId":1,...}` the moment B started, and B hung (no ROW line, no result). Fix: every one of them now uses `launchBrowser` of tests/helpers/cdp-browser.js (port 0, port read from the profile's DevToolsActivePort, unique profile): axis-snap + draw-undo + origin-snap runners, clear-all, context-menu, dimension-delete, dxf-import, polygon-tool, snap-release-slip, sidebar-account, sidebar-drive, sidebar-projects, snap-origin-coincident, style-panel-tabs. Left alone (gate script, not a test): scripts/shell-smoke.cjs still has `9300 + Date.now() % 600`.
2. TEST READS BEFORE THE REAL CONDITION: fixed `sleep(1200..3500)` after navigation instead of the app's own ready signal. Two helpers added to the shared helper (ONE place): `waitForApp(canvasId)` waits for `data-doc-ready="1"` (document-buffer.js, TASK 542); `flushAutosave()` triggers the app's own page-hide save and waits for the "Saved" status (replaces `sleep(1500..1800)` + a loose "Saved" poll that could be stale). Applied to the live tests listed in the commit. numeric-input-self-hiding: showEditInput focuses+selects in the next animation frame, the test waited a fixed 80 ms then typed; now waits for focus + whole value selected, and for the typed value. draw-undo runner fillet: waits for `#fillet-radius-input` focus / removal instead of 400/300 ms.
   Shaper and Pen Plotter create their Design buffer only when the Design tab is first entered, so `waitForApp` there comes AFTER entering Design.
3. NOT proven: that the stale autosave read was ever hit. An instrumented esc runner (reads after the old `sleep(1800)+waitSaved` and again after a page-hide flush) showed 72 fresh reads, 0 stale, under 14 cpu burners + coverage-matrix + drag-follow-live loops. The old numeric test also never failed in 15 runs under 2 loops (24-core box). Those readings are replaced anyway because they are the unbounded kind.
Remaining timed waits (left on purpose): pacing sleeps of 30-600 ms after each synthetic click/key (the CDP call returns after dispatch), render-settle waits before screenshots (no DOM state to wait on), and recentre-on-reload's 1200 ms settle / 3200 ms "two autosave ticks" (the test asserts that NOTHING happens over time; a two-frame settle made its Pen Plotter Open-recent step fail, so it was reverted).
Proof: each of numeric-input-self-hiding, draw-undo-live-esc, axis-snap-live-shapes, journal-live, fusion-drag-live ran 20/20 green (`.evidence/560/proof-natural-load.txt`) while other seats' gates ran on the machine (no deliberate load: the advisor asked to stop adding load). ## TURN 559 (copy / cut / paste of geometry: Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+V)
- ONE module `packages/ui/clipboard.js` (keys declared in `input-manager.js` next to the other shortcuts via `clipboardKeyAction`). Copy = core's `serializeDocument` over a sub-document (no second serializer); paste adds through `addConstraintObject` (the undo / load path, so `withDimensionState` keeps every dimension field and `addConstraint` names a dimension the next free dN); cut = copy + `deleteSelection` (the Delete key's path) on exactly the copied set. One additive export in `packages/core/parameters.js`: `remapExpressionNames` (renames every name of a formula at once through the AST; the existing `renameInAst` is one name at a time).
- WHAT: the selected shapes with their own joints (+ a fillet arc's virtual-sharp joint, + a selected point no shape uses). A constraint / dimension is copied only if EVERY operand (joint or shape) is inside the copy; links to outside geometry, to the origin joint or to an axis are not. A shape that itself uses `j_origin` gets an ordinary FREE (not fixed) copy of that point at its offset position; a point that was coincident with the origin comes out unattached.
- NAMES: a pasted dimension gets a new dN. Formula: a name of a copied dimension is renamed to its copy; a user parameter the target document has keeps being read (same document: always; another document WITH the parameter: re-evaluated there through `commitDimensionEdits`, frozen if the sketch refuses); any other name (a parameter the target lacks, a dimension that was not copied) freezes the formula to the dimension's number. (to verify in Fusion UI)
- WHERE: chose the OFFSET paste (+10 mm right and down on screen = down in the user's Y-up sense, `PASTE_STEP_MM`), copy left selected; pasting the same clipboard again offsets each paste one more step (+20, +30 ...); a new copy restarts at one step. Why: follow-the-cursor needs a modal placing tool (preview rendering, Esc / click states); FOLLOW-UP note: cursor-following placement like Fusion. Ctrl+D is NOT bound (browser bookmark key); repeated Ctrl+V is the "paste again". (to verify in Fusion UI: where a plain Ctrl+V lands)
- STORE: system clipboard as text, JSON envelope `{format:'sketch-studio/geometry', version:1, document}`; write or read refused / no API -> in-memory copy of this page and ONE warning notification; text that is not ours is ignored silently; a newer version / unreadable payload shows a warning. Shape ids have no central generator (each tool builds its own `Date.now()` id), so pasted shapes use `s_paste_<ms>_<seq>_<i>` and joints use `state.genJ()`; shape `groupId` (the closed-shape key) is renamed per copy; `userGroupId`, `sketchId` (copy joins the ACTIVE sketch), `glyphPos`, `__pos` are not copied; a bezier's absolute control points and a dimension's `labelPos` move with the copy.
- Undo: one paste = one `beginUndoGroup('paste')` step; the pasted items are selected afterwards. Not run while a draw is open (a paste is its own step).
- Tests: tests/clipboard.test.js (unit; rectangle + H/V + 2 dims, link to outside, origin forms, formulas same / other document with and without the parameter, cut + undo, repeated offsets, circle + bezier, fallback / foreign / newer, keys, text-field targets; fails on main with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND). Live (headless Edge, real pointer + real keys, clipboard permission granted over CDP Browser.grantPermissions, kept open): clipboard-live-sketchstudio / -shaper / -cross (SketchStudio -> reload -> Shaper). Finding: a CDP Ctrl+C key event WITH nativeVirtualKeyCode makes the browser run its native copy and the CDP call never returns; the runner omits it.
- Behaviour changes for existing users: (1) Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V / Ctrl+X no longer switch to the Circle / Pan / Coincident tools (bare c, v, x unchanged); they copy / paste / cut on the canvas selection. (2) The shortcut is in the shared input layer, so it is also live in the Shaper Design tab, Pen Plotter and Trace sketch stages (same Design tab). (3) Browser clipboard permission may be asked once on the first paste in a real browser. (4) Nothing else changes: no saved-file change, no solver change.
- Found, not fixed: shape ids are ad hoc per tool (`'s'+Date.now()` in the circle tool can collide in one millisecond).

## TURN 555 (Dimension tool picks like Fusion: entity -> preview follows the cursor -> second entity upgrades -> empty space places -> Esc cancels)
- STEP 1, the state machine on main before this task (packages/ui/input-handlers/dimension-tool.js `dimensionPointerDown`; input-manager.js hit-tests with findSnap(pickableShapes) and passes hitJoint / hitShape):
  1. Click on a dimension LABEL: double click opens the edit box; a single click falls through.
  2. A click while a dimension is PLACING (`placingConstraint.__placing`) is the drop. (2a) if the preview is a line's length (2 joints) and the click hit a different LINE: the length is removed (birth snapshot discarded) and replaced by a line-line DISTANCE (parallel) or an ANGLE; the new one is placing. (Else) a driven dimension is dropped; a driving one opens the edit box (or is made driven when both joints are already fixed).
  3. A first-picked JOINT (`pendingDimension`, rubber band): click on a line = point-to-line distance (placing); on another joint = point-to-point distance (placing); on empty space = cancel.
  4. Nothing pending: click on a joint = pending joint (3); click on a line = its LENGTH preview (placing, label follows the cursor, H/V/aligned by cursor side); click on a circle / arc = RADIUS preview (placing).
  5. Pointer up after a press-drag longer than 250 ms drops the label (touch: 6 px threshold starts the drag). `startDimensionFromSelection` is the selection / keyboard entry (one selected line = its length, two selected joints = point-to-point), also placing.
  6. Esc (input-manager handleEscape) removed a PLACING preview only; a pending first joint stayed in the tool's module state.
  Missing against Fusion: line + point, line + axis (539 asked for an axis only after a first joint, because a label drop near an axis became a pick), angle / distance to an axis, Esc forgetting a first-picked point.
- STEP 2, what changed (one state machine, three small changes): (a) a line's length preview now carries `__asksSecondPick`; while it is placing, `referenceLinesPickable` (reference-lines.js, the ONE pick rule) offers the two axes, so a click ON an axis picks it: 2a (unchanged code, scene-resolved) makes the line-to-axis DISTANCE (parallel) or the ANGLE to the axis. (b) 2b: a JOINT clicked while a line's length previews turns it into the point-to-line distance; a click on the line's own end is still a drop. Both the point-then-line and the line-then-point paths end in ONE function `createPointLineDimension` (the old inline case moved there, unchanged), and the removal of the length preview is ONE function `discardPlacingLength` (2a's inline code moved there). (c) Esc: `handleEscape` calls resetDimensionState whenever the tool is Dimension (was: only while placing), so a first-picked point is forgotten. The hover preview of the angle (dimension-tool move handler) now also looks at the axes (endless).
- Every dimension and its click sequence: line length = click line, click empty space | circle / arc radius = click it, click empty space | point-point = point, point, (place by the next click) | point-line = point then line, OR line then point | line-line distance (parallel) / angle (crossing) = line, line | line-axis distance (parallel) / angle to the axis = line, axis | point-axis distance (539) = point, axis | angle sector 10 vs 170 (543 / 553) = after the second line the label's sector under the cursor decides at the drop (unchanged code, tested) | H / V distance of a line = the cursor side while its length previews (unchanged) | selection / keyboard start = unchanged. Axis as FIRST pick: not added (a first click near an axis keeps picking real geometry, as 539 decided; "line then axis" covers the same dimensions; point-axis is point then axis).
- To verify in Fusion UI: whether Fusion offers horizontal / vertical distance by cursor position for a single line (kept as today: by cursor side); a point picked alone then a click on empty space (here: cancels the pick, no dimension; Fusion may do the same or keep waiting); an axis picked first (not offered here).
- Behaviour changes for existing users: (1) a click that lands ON an axis (within the 20 px line reach) while a line's length previews now PICKS the axis (line-to-axis dimension) instead of dropping the label there; a label is dropped by a click clear of lines, points and axes. Two live tests dropped their label on an axis by accident and moved the drop (tests/fusion-drag-live.test.js: the old drop (cv.x, cv.y+100) was 17 px from the X axis, the origin is not at the canvas centre). (2) A click on a point (within the 30 px point reach) while a line's length previews is now a point-to-line pick, not a drop. (3) Esc in the Dimension tool also forgets a first-picked point. Not a change (checked): clicking a line never placed its length immediately; the first click starts the preview and a second click on empty space places it. The 539 note "the same click is the label drop" was about a drop near an axis, which is what (1) settles.
- Tests: tests/dimension-pick-sequence.test.js (node, real handlers: every sequence above, Esc; fail-first on main: "a line preview asks for a second pick", .evidence/555/failfirst-pick-sequence.txt), tests/reference-lines-solve.test.js (pick rule), live with real pointer + key events in both hosts: tests/dimension-pick-live-{studio,shaper}.test.js over tests/dimension-pick-live-runner.js (line + axis angle, parallel line + axis distance, line + empty length, line + point, Esc). Items, order, labels identical: New design, Save as…, Duplicate, Open recent, Projects, [Save to Google Drive, signed in only], Open from file, Import SVG / DXF…. Each host's declared extras follow below a divider: Trace keeps Download SVG / Download DXF (it had no others); Shaper and Pen Plotter keep their one Download; SketchStudio keeps its Download SVG / DXF. The Edit canvas is mounted at boot (edit-view.js `mountEdit`) and bound with createDocumentBuffer exactly as Pen Plotter / Shaper do: no buffer wiring was hand-copied (the buffer is the shared one; each host only declares hostName / getHostData / onRestored, as the others do).
Wanted 2 (OWNER DECISION, marked): what Trace keeps of a design = the traced geometry (it is the Edit sketch, already the design) + `hosts.trace = { imageName, params: { threshold, blur, colorMode, simplify, smooth, outlineOnly } }`. NOT stored: the photo, the mask, the scale (mm per photo pixel: meaningless without the photo's pixel size). Reasoning: a reopened design makes sense without the photo (the sketch is the result; the photo is only a re-trace source); the buffer re-serialises the document every 1.5 s tick and Drive writes whole designs, so a photo inside would be re-stringified / re-uploaded with every edit. Sizes: a 12 MP phone photo is ~3-5 MB as JPEG, ~48 MB decoded RGBA, ~15-25 MB as a PNG data URL (IndexedDB takes it, Drive and the autosave signature do not like it). If the owner wants re-tracing from a reopened design, the way is a separate image store (blob in IndexedDB / a Drive file) referenced from hosts.trace, NOT the document JSON. Not stopped on: the reopened design does make sense without the photo.
Wanted 3: DIAG report's document section wired: `createDiagnosticLog({ appId: 'trace', state: () => getEditState() })` (the same getter shape as Shaper / Pen Plotter). A Trace design opens in SketchStudio (geometry identical) and a SketchStudio save keeps hosts.trace (tested). Saved format unchanged except the new hosts.trace.
Wanted 4: 558 had NOT landed on origin/main when this was done (fetched before the final gate): nothing Trace-specific written for tabs / save-prompt; Trace uses the same buffer and menu so it follows 558 with no special case once merged.
Behaviour changes for existing Trace users: (1) the Edit canvas now DRAWS (was blank); (2) the Edit canvas is mounted at boot, so the "Trace an image, then click Send to Editor" empty message in Edit is gone (the empty canvas + ribbon shows, you can draw / import there); (3) the demo shapes mountSketch used to seed into Trace's (never drawn) sketch are no longer seeded (seedDemo:false, as Shaper / Pen Plotter); (4) the File menu gains New design, Save as, Duplicate, Open recent, Projects, Open from file, (Drive when signed in) and the page title / header follow the design name; Trace autosaves (header shows Saved) and a reload restores the sketch and the trace parameters, landing on the Edit tab when the stored design has shapes (the photo is not kept, so the Trace tab would be empty); (5) "New design" resets the trace controls to their defaults; (6) Download SVG / DXF moved below a divider after the shared items (they were the top group).

## TURN 572 (symmetric of two lines = the INFINITE lines mirror, like Fusion; owner ruling 2026-11-13)
- FUSION (advisor, API): a (-4,0)-(-1,3) and b (1.5,0.5)-(6,2.5) about the Y axis -> a unchanged, b (1.8132,2.1868)-(5.2953,-1.2953), length
  kept 4.9244, on y = -x + 4 (mirror of a's line); ends not mirrored; the second pick moves. Arcs / circles: as ours.
- ROWS (definitions.js mirrorOnLine*): per end q of line 2, the reflection R(q) across the symmetry line lies on line 1: r = ((R - A) x v)/|v|.
  2 rows, 2 DOF. Why this form: the pair rule (q - mirror(p)) does not fit (no point of line 1 corresponds to an end of line 2); the
  reflection is an isometry, so dr/dq has unit length and each row owns its own end of line 2 (the two rows are independent in q1, q2: as
  conditioned as two point-on-line rows, world units). Full derivative on the symmetry line's ends and line 1's ends (they can move). addGrad
  only, operands only (the joints list [s1, s2, pairs..., q a1 a2 ...] + params.nPairs). Points and circles keep the pair rule.
- SHARED END (a V, re-derived): V is an end of both lines; R(V) on line 1 (which passes through V) means V on the symmetry line (or line 1
  perpendicular to it); the other end fixes the mirrored direction: 2 DOF (was 3 with end pairs). Tested (V on the axis, 2 DOF).
- REMOVED (no caller left, grep): symmetric.js pairLineEnds (ConstraintManager's end pairing at creation) and creation-placement.js
  similarityTaking (the line placement). The line placement is now the collinear one onto the anchor line's MIRROR: ontoLine(M, mover, line)
  factored out of PLACE.collinear (same code path: collinear unchanged, fusion-oracle OK).
- SAVED FORMAT: lines are { type, shapes, line } (no joints). A task-563 file (version 3) with { joints: [p1,q1,p2,q2], shapes, line } loads as
  the new form: constraints.js createConstraint (every stored constraint: load, undo, paste) keeps no joints for a shapes form. No
  DOCUMENT_VERSION bump: the new build reads the old form cleanly (tested: loads, solves without moving anything, DOF +2 (the lengths), re-saves
  as the new form, loads and saves byte-identically); the only older build that knows symmetric (563, main since 2026-11-13) keeps a no-joints
  line form stored (its createConstraint) but solves no rows for it (its operand reader wants 4 joints): it does not lose it.
