## TURN 575 — owner "can't drag the geometry / not accurate": the causes, two fixed (drag targets outliving their drag, a redundant snap constraint), one reported (Opus subagent)
Owner drawing (deployed app, Copy Report 16:59 UTC): two concentric arcs about the origin, radii d2 = 2286 / d3 = 2667, sides collinear with construction lines through the origin, angle d1 = 10 deg: DOF 1 (the rotation). Fixture: tests/fixtures/drag/owner-two-arcs-575.json.
NOT a regression of today's merges: every number below is the same at d058485 (yesterday's main) and 9ba678c.
- (A) REPORTED, not fixed (behaviour change, owner decides). Grabbing an arc RIM joint (j8 / j9, j2) starts a CLUSTER drag of the whole arc: selection-tools.js handleJointSelection adds the arc's centre and both rims (from the initial commit). The centre is welded to j_origin, so getDragDOF's cluster propagation returns lockX + lockY: the drag target stays at the start and the joint never moves (node, real handlers, owner doc, 4 px per event along the circle: gap 4, 8 ... 79 px, j8 stays at -97.067 deg; same with d2 / d3 removed). Grabbing j16 / j19 (the construction-line end in the same corner, not an arc id: no expansion) follows exactly (gap 0.0 px every event, both radii set): the owner's "now it worked". Fusion moves only the grabbed end of an arc. Options for the owner: (a) a rim joint drags itself only, like Fusion (body drag, task 538, already moves the whole arc); (b) keep the whole-arc grab but not when the arc's centre is held.
- (B) FIXED. A drag's solver targets (joint.dragTarget / shape.dragTarget, which every solve pulls toward while they exist) outlived the drag. Only the select tool's pointer-up removed them; Esc (handleEscape: state.drag = null), a touch hold and a new press after a lost release dropped the drag and kept the targets, and the autosave (serializeDocument copied every joint field) wrote them into the stored design during a long drag, so a reload / tab switch / Open put them back. Every later solve then pulled those joints toward an old cursor position: the owner's journal seq 4-6 (targets on j7/j8/j9 through a j19 drag and a dimension). Live proof (old code): Esc in a j3 drag, then a j2 drag: 1 s after its release the drawing rotated back 9.08 deg by itself (-91.577 -> -82.499, the Esc drag's target); a design autosaved during a held drag stored targets on j3/j14/j16.
  Fix: packages/ui/sketch-state.js: `drag` is an accessor; replacing or clearing it calls `releaseDragTargets(state, drag)` (exported: the one release; selection-tools pointer-up calls it too, before a snap-on-release solves, replacing its inline loops). packages/core/document.js `withoutDragTarget(record)`: serializeDocument, deserializeDocument and the undo snapshot (_captureSnapshot) copy joints and shapes through it.
- (2) FIXED. A drag release added a REDUNDANT constraint: j9 (end of the right side, held on the construction line by the collinear) dragged along its line snapped to the construction line and got pointOnLine(j9, s1794492607958) (owner's seq 18; the sandbox refused it only sometimes, residual 2.27e-7). packages/core/snap-constraints.js applySnapConstraint: a snap whose rows raise no rank over the existing driving constraints (engine.isDistanceRedundant, the rank test the dimension and symmetric paths use) adds nothing (task 537's rule).
- (3) REPORTED. While dragging a joint whose drag is masked (locked, or held on a line), the snap still locks every few frames (line / joint / axis-y / grid) and replaces the target: a locked j8 jumped onto the Y axis at release (pointOnLine(j8, ref_axis_y) added, the drawing rotated to -90 deg, DOF 0). Whether a constrained point should snap at all while dragged (Fusion: to verify) is the owner's call; snapping unchanged.
Tests: tests/drag-target-release-live.test.js (real mouse and keys, owner drawing: Esc then another drag, drift 0.0000 deg; autosave during a held drag, no target; j9 along its line, 17 -> 17 constraints). Old code: drift 9.0775 deg, targets on j3/j14/j16, 17 -> 18 [pointOnLine(j9 / s1794492607958)]. tests/drag-target-transient.test.js (node: the setter releases, a new drag releases the old one's, snapshot / save / load carry no target); fails on the old code at its first assertion.
Behaviour changes for existing users: (1) Esc / a touch hold / a new press during a drag no longer leave the dragged joints pulling toward the last cursor position; (2) a design saved during a drag, an undo snapshot, a loaded design never carry a drag target (a stored design that has one loads without it); (3) a snap the sketch already holds (any snap kind: coincident, point on line, midpoint, axis) adds no constraint at release: before, it was added or refused with an "ERR-CSOLVE-01 rejected" error toast.

## TURN 579 - tests that measure TIME run alone (exclusive set in the gate)
- PROBLEM: a merge gate failed tests/solver-perf-guard.test.js ("size 400: a drag event takes 36.8 ms, more than 36 ms"); it ran in quick beside 21 parallel node tests. BEFORE (old gate.cjs, quick with another gate:live queued/other seats' live runs on the box): `size 400: full solve 126.7 ms (limit 115)` -> FAIL (.evidence/579/before-quick.log); a direct run under that load printed `size 400: full solve 102.1 ms (limit 115), drag event 29.2 ms (limit 36)` = 89% / 81% of the limits (.evidence/579/before-perf-loop.log, run 1); quiet runs print ~38 ms / ~12.5 ms.
- MECHANISM (scripts/gate.cjs, declared in the test file): a first-column line `// gate: exclusive` in a test. The test keeps its tier; after the parallel batch of its tier it runs ALONE, one at a time, under the machine-wide lock, and prints `EXCLUSIVE <file> <seconds>`. quick takes the lock only for that part (released right after; `LOCK held for the exclusive tests only: quick=45s`); live/full/merge already hold it. Marker over a list in gate.cjs: it sits beside the limit it protects. `--list` appends ` exclusive`.
- AUDIT (every test whose pass/fail depends on wall time; 9 marked, limits and tests untouched):
  - solver-perf-guard: ms limits per size (solve/drag/batch). TIMING.
  - profile-fill: `on - off < 3` ms per frame. TIMING (a delta of two timed loops).
  - relief-model: `ms <= 1500` build (node). TIMING (the vcarve `ms` is printed only).
  - parameters-batch: `ms < 30000` (pathological-regression guard; the 1/2/10/30 and 100 times are printed only). TIMING though very loose.
  - constraint-audit: `secs > 40` fails. TIMING. coverage-properties: `secs > 30`. TIMING. coverage-matrix: `total < 30 s`. TIMING. extreme-arcs: `total < 60 s`. TIMING.
  - snap-release-slip-live (LIVE tier): `flickMs < 200` press -> release inside the app's 200 ms recovery window, measured in the browser: wall-time dependent; marked so it runs alone after the live pool.
  - NOT timing-sensitive (print or spin only): joint-dof-truth (PERF lines printed, no assert), polygon-tool (prints ms), shape-id-unique (prints ms; its same-millisecond ids are the point, uniqueness asserted), parameters-canvas (spins to a new millisecond), project-store-idb / sidebar-drive / cdp-browser / node-app waits (poll timeouts, not measured limits), review-live ("budget" is a triangle count), other `Date.now()` uses are ids/timestamps. tests/harness and packages/core/tests: no timing asserts.
- AFTER: `node scripts/gate.cjs --list` shows 9 ` exclusive` lines (8 quick + snap-release-slip-live). 10 consecutive quick runs, the first four queued behind other seats' merge/live runs on the lock (elapsed 368-384 s), the rest uncontended (50-53 s): 10/10 `GATE tier=quick ... files=262 pass=262 fail=0`, `EXCLUSIVE tests/solver-perf-guard.test.js 5.1-5.5`, lock held 44-46 s per run (.evidence/579/after-quick-x10.log). The gate prints a passing test's output nowhere, so the per-size numbers of the after runs are not quoted.
- COST: a quick run now waits for the lock when any other worktree is in live/full/merge (up to a full merge run, ~12 min seen) before its exclusive part. Not changed: tier rules, concurrency, test limits.

## TURN 584 - drag follow-ups of 582: an arc grabbed by its centre translates whole (Fusion), the origin is not a snap target of a drag that holds it, a cluster drag infers nothing (Opus subagent, relaunched after an owner interrupt)
- 1, arc by its CENTRE. Cause: handleJointSelection / pullDrag set a drag target on the centre AND both rims, but every solve pulled ONE joint: the pointer event's pass the explicit spring of the grabbed joint, the app's frame solve the FIRST joint carrying a target (joint insertion order). The rims followed the radius equality, not the drag (free arc: stretch; radius-dimensioned: rotate). Fix, one place in the solver (packages/core/solver/engine.js `_jointDragSprings`, interaction.js attaches a list): every solve pulls EVERY joint carrying a drag target, one spring per solver variable (coincident joints are one point). The select tool gives a target only to the joints the drag CARRIES (`state.drag.carried` = the grabbed point's coincident cluster + both rims of an arc-centre grab). Unchanged: one held rim = 582's pivot (rims not carried, radius kept); a held centre locks; a centre-point rectangle's group is masked with its centre, only the centre is pulled (probe: identical before / after).
- Oracle (tests/fusion-drag.test.js): before 140 same / 17 KNOWN / 4 unstable, after 146 / 11 / 4. Per KNOWN class before -> after: arc.centre 6 -> 0 (arc.free.centre.along/across/diag "MMMr / M..r stretch" -> "MMM. translate", arc.rad.centre.* "MMM. rotate" -> "MMM. translate", Fusion "MMM. translate" in all six), arc.end 6 -> 6, line.end 2 -> 2, tangent.lineend 3 -> 3. No other cell changed (oracle-before.txt vs oracle-after.txt: only those 6 rows; rerun identical). drag-known.json regenerated with scripts/fusion-oracle/drag-known.mjs ("11 KNOWN differences; unexplained: 0"); the script's arc.centre reason is removed.
- 2, the origin snap. input-manager.js updateSnapTarget's explicit origin check now skips j_origin when it is in the drag's excluded joints (the same excludeIds findSnap gets). Owner j7 (welded to the origin) dragged 10 x (2, 1) px: offers of j_origin 14 -> 0. Controls: a free point dragged onto the origin still locks and gets a Coincident at release; the line tool still snaps to the origin.
- 3, cluster inferences. Why: findInference's attached-line tests (H / V, parallel / perpendicular to another line, midpoint) run for draggedType 'joint' only; a CLUSTER drag passed 'other', so only the DRAWING scan ran, which reads the displacement start -> cursor as a line being drawn (tangent to a circle the start lies on, parallel / perpendicular to a nearby line). The owner's j3 corner (j3 = j14 = j16: the inner arc's end, the radial side, the radial construction line) moving along the arc showed TANGENT to the inner arc on 38 of 40 events.
